Initial reinforced agents logic (#22687)

- Add a Reinforced Agents background system that analyzes recent conversations during off-hours to suggest improvements to agent configurations
- Phase 1 (Analyze): For each agent, uses an LLM to analyze recent conversations against the agent's current instructions, producing "synthetic" suggestions (internal, not user-visible)
- Phase 2 (Aggregate): Collects pending synthetic suggestions, uses an LLM to deduplicate/merge/prioritize, then creates user-facing "reinforcement" suggestions. Marks consumed synthetic suggestions as approved
- Gated behind a reinforced_agents feature flag (dust_only stage)
- Structured as 3-level Temporal workflows (all workspaces → per workspace → per agent) with CLI support to run each level independently
- Synthetic suggestions are excluded from copilot/sidekick queries by default

[LLM] Refactor model availability to availableIfUnion/customAvailableIf (#22706)

* fix(models): bypass feature flag block for enterprise-enforced models

Extract `isEnforcedByEnterpriseAvailability` helper and use it in both
`isModelAvailable` and `postUserMessage`, so enterprise plans are not
rejected with a 400 when using models that set `enforceEnterpriseAvailability`.

* fix(models): add feature flag to Claude Opus 4.6 while keeping enterprise bypass

Re-adds `claude_4_5_opus_feature` flag so non-enterprise workspaces still
require the flag, while enterprise plans bypass it via `enforceEnterpriseAvailability`.

* refactor(models): introduce availableIfUnion and customAvailableIf on ModelConfigurationType

Replace flat featureFlag, customAssistantFeatureFlag and enforceEnterpriseAvailability
fields with two structured objects:
- availableIfUnion: OR-semantics gate for model use (enterprise, featureFlag)
- customAvailableIf: additional gate for custom-assistant builder

Undefined availableIfUnion means the model is always available; an empty object
disables it entirely.

* refactor(models): migrate all provider configs to availableIfUnion / customAvailableIf

Converts every model config that used featureFlag, customAssistantFeatureFlag or
enforceEnterpriseAvailability to the new structured fields introduced in the
previous commit. No behavior change intended — gates are preserved 1-to-1.

* refactor(assistant): rewrite availability helpers to use new model config shape

- isModelAvailable: checks availableIfUnion (enterprise OR featureFlag) — "can
  this model be used at runtime?"
- isModelCustomAvailable: wraps isModelAvailable then checks customAvailableIf —
  "can this model be selected in the custom-assistant builder?"
- isModelCustomAvailableAndWhitelisted: wraps isModelCustomAvailable + provider
  whitelist check (renamed from isModelAvailableAndWhitelisted)

Update all callsites to use the renamed / split helpers.

* test(assistant): update tests to match new availability API

- Replace featureFlag / customAssistantFeatureFlag mock fields with
  availableIfUnion and customAvailableIf
- Update test subjects to isModelCustomAvailable / isModelCustomAvailableAndWhitelisted
- Add missing import for isModelCustomAvailableAndWhitelisted

* refactor(workspace): update ProviderManagementModal to isModelCustomAvailable

Follows the rename introduced in the availability helpers refactor.

* fix(models): make claude-opus-4-6 available via feature flag in addition to enterprise

* fix: types

* test(assistant): add enterprise availability tests for isModelCustomAvailable

Cover the enterprise field in availableIfUnion: enterprise-only plan
(DUST_COMPANY and ENT_ prefix), and the OR semantics when both enterprise
and featureFlag are defined together.

Bridge pre-signup and post-signup user tracking (#22689)

* Bridge pre-signup and post-signup user tracking

Introduce a persistent anonymous device ID (`_dust_aid` cookie) that
survives page reloads and the OAuth redirect to WorkOS and back, enabling
stitching of anonymous website visitors to identified users after
signup/login.

Key changes:

- Anonymous ID cookie (`_dust_aid`): A first-party UUIDv4 cookie (1-year
  expiry) created after cookie consent. Gated behind `hasCookiesAccepted`
  for GDPR compliance—never set without consent.

- Identity stitching at login: On login, the `_dust_aid` value is read
  server-side and passed to PostHog's `alias()` API, merging all
  pre-signup anonymous events into the user's identified person profile.

- First-touch attribution ($set_once): UTM params and click IDs are
  recorded as permanent person properties (e.g. `first_utm_source`,
  `first_gclid`) both server-side (in trackSignup) and client-side (on
  posthog.identify), so the original acquisition source is never
  overwritten.

- Enriched client-side PostHog events: The `before_send` hook now injects
  `dust_anonymous_id`, `$referrer`, and `user_agent` into every event.
  `property_denylist: ["$ip"]` remains unchanged—IP is never sent from
  the client.

- Server-side page view endpoint (`/api/t/pv`): Captures page views with
  consent-gated IP and user-agent server-side. Rate-limited (4 req/2s per
  IP). Uses `sendBeacon` from the client for non-blocking sends.

- Email engagement stitching (Customer.io): The `dust_anonymous_id` is
  now included as a Customer.io user attribute, enabling email templates
  to append `?dust_aid={{customer.dust_anonymous_id}}` to CTA links for
  cross-device session stitching.

- URL param handling: `dust_aid` from email CTA links is persisted as the
  `_dust_aid` cookie and stripped from the URL bar alongside UTM params.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Set _dust_aid cookie with domain=.dust.tt for cross-subdomain sharing

The marketing site runs on dust.tt while the app runs on app.dust.tt.
Without an explicit domain attribute, the _dust_aid cookie set on
dust.tt would be host-only and invisible to app.dust.tt, breaking
identity stitching at login.

Derive the root domain at runtime from window.location.hostname
(e.g. app.dust.tt → .dust.tt) and set the cookie with that domain.
On localhost/IP addresses, no domain attribute is set (host-only).

Also export buildDustAidCookieString() so persistDustAidFromURL()
in utm.ts reuses the same domain logic instead of duplicating it.

results. It triggered a competing shallow router.push that raced with

(#12175) to clear search state when navigating into a sub-folder on the
DSV page (same-page navigation). The root cause of the bug was only the
searchParam.setParam(undefined) call, which shallow-pushes to the current
pathname, racing with and overriding the folder navigation on the category

fixes both: no more race, and search input still clears after navigation.

[BYOK] Notify workspace members when provider credentials health changes (#23128)

* refactor(notifications): extract getNovuClient into dedicated module

Moves getNovuClient into novu-client.ts to avoid pulling the heavy
notifications barrel (Authenticator, DataSourceResource, etc.) into
workflow files, which would otherwise create an import cycle.

* feat(byok): add provider-credentials-health-updated Novu workflow

Adds the workflow definition, trigger ID constant, and registers the
workflow with the Novu serve endpoint so the platform can execute it.

* feat(byok): notify workspace members on provider credential health changes

Calls notifyProviderCredentialsHealthUpdated on makeNew, updateApiKey,
markAsUnhealthy, and delete so all workspace members receive a signal
to refresh their auth context when credentials health changes.

* feat(byok): refresh auth context on provider-credentials-health notification

When a provider-credentials-health notification is received, silently
invalidate the auth-context SWR cache so providersHealth updates in
the UI without any user-facing notification bell.

* refactor(byok): replace non-null assertion with explicit null check in notification trigger

* refactor(byok): extract provider-credentials-health tag into a named constant

* refactor(byok): use type predicate to narrow membersWithUser so user is always defined

* refactor(notifications): fetch Novu secrets via config instead of process.env

* fix(notifications): paginate membership fetch and cap Novu bulk trigger at 100

* fix(byok): move provider-credentials-health tag constant to shared types

The constant was defined in a server-only workflow module, causing Next.js
to bundle MembershipResource and other server-side code into the client bundle,
breaking app load.

* fix(byok): fix empty subject/body causing Novu in-app step to fail

Novu's in_app schema enforces minLength: 1 on subject and body.
Empty strings triggered a 400 validation error, silently dropping the
notification and preventing the unhealthy-credentials banner from
updating in real time.

* fix(byok): auto-delete provider health notifications without showing popup

* fix(byok): move getNovuClient inside try-catch to prevent unhandled rejection

[Email Agents] Switch inbound sender auth to DMARC-style alignment (#23317)

* [Email Agents] Switch inbound sender auth to DMARC-style alignment

Evaluate inbound email authentication against the header From: domain
instead of the envelope sender. Accepts if aligned DKIM passes or if
SPF passes with an aligned envelope domain. This allows forwarded mail
with surviving DKIM signatures to reach agents.

* Fix backscatter regression: silently drop unauthenticated mail

PR #23316 removed replyToError on auth failure to prevent backscatter
(replying to potentially spoofed senders). Restore that behavior: log a
warning with full auth signals and silently drop the message.

fix: skip slack channel linking call for non-builder users (#23699)

* fix: skip slack channel linking call for non-builder users

The linked_slack_channels endpoint requires builder/admin role, but
agent creation is open to all users. Non-builder users saving agents
would get a 403 on the slack linking PATCH call, causing a spurious
"An error occurred while linking Slack channels" error even though
the agent was created successfully.

Skip the call entirely for non-builder users since they can't manage
Slack channel linking anyway.

* fix: gate slackProvider on isBuilder to prevent spurious slack linking calls

The root cause is that slackProvider was computed for all users (from
supportedDataSourceViews), but the slack channels UI and fetch hook are
already gated on isBuilder(owner). This mismatch caused the form to
call the linked_slack_channels endpoint for non-builder users, which
returns 403.

Gate slackProvider on isBuilder(owner) to match the existing pattern,
ensuring the slack linking call condition (slackProvider &&
areSlackChannelsChanged) is never true for non-builders.

[connectors] Skip Slack channel sync after persistent upstream 5xx errors (#23815)

* [connectors] Skip Slack channel sync after persistent upstream 5xx errors

Following the same pattern used in the Notion connector, give up on
syncing a channel when the upstream API consistently returns server
errors (HTTP 5xx) after 20+ activity attempts. This prevents workflows
from retrying indefinitely against a persistently failing endpoint.

* Use normalizeError for logged error

* Widen 5xx skip guard to cover all Slack API calls in syncChannel

Move the try-catch from wrapping only getMessagesForChannel to wrapping
the entire work section (message fetch + thread sync + non-threaded sync).
This ensures persistent 5xx errors during any phase of the channel sync
trigger the attempt-based skip.

Also catch ProviderWorkflowError (503s converted by withSlackErrorHandling)
in addition to raw WebAPIHTTPError 5xx. Rate limit errors are excluded
as they resolve naturally.

* Fix infinite loop when give-up returns undefined mid-pagination

When syncChannel gave up on a persistent 5xx, it returned undefined.
The workflow loop preserved the old messagesCursor, re-invoked the
activity (resetting the attempt counter), and looped forever.

Fix: return { nextCursor: undefined, weeksSynced } so the workflow
breaks out of its pagination loop.

Also trim comments and cache Context.current().info.attempt.

[Connectors] fix(slack): track run_agent sub-agent progress via child streams (#22948)

* [Connectors] fix(slack): track run_agent child agent progress via child streams

A few weeks ago, tool execution events for run_agent moved from the parent
conversation stream to per-message child streams. The slack bot was only
subscribed to the parent stream, so sub-agent tool progress became invisible,
causing long unexplained silences during deep-dive runs.

Subscribe to each child stream on run_agent notifications (once the child
agentMessageId is available), and surface progress via a plan block posted
as a standalone message — deleted on terminal events. Using a separate
message rather than the existing chat stream avoids Slack's 5-min stream
timeout on long-running sub-agents.

Implement initial reinforced skills workflows (#23917)

### Summary

  - Introduces a new "Reinforced Skills" feature that analyzes recent conversations where skills were used and generates improvement suggestions per-skill, following the same patterns as the existing Reinforced Agents feature.
  - Adds a "tools" suggestion kind to SkillSuggestionKind for suggesting tool add/remove on skills.
  - Renames existing Poke agent reinforcement plugins to include "Agents" in their display names for disambiguation.

### Architecture

  - Single workspace-level Temporal workflow (no per-skill child workflows, unlike Reinforced Agents which has per-agent child workflows)
  - Conversation-centric discovery: finds conversations that used custom skills via AgentMessageSkillModel, rather than starting from agents
  - Per-conversation analysis: each conversation is analyzed once covering all skills used in it
  - Per-skill aggregation: after analysis, synthetic suggestions are grouped by skill and aggregated
  - Optional skillId scoping: the workspace workflow accepts an optional skillId to scope analysis to one skill
  - Reuses the existing reinforced_agents feature flag

* [snowflake] Skip dropped databases instead of failing the entire sync

When a Snowflake database is dropped or becomes inaccessible between
SHOW DATABASES and the subsequent SHOW SCHEMAS/TABLES queries, the
connector gets stuck retrying indefinitely (error code 002043: "Object
does not exist").

Instead of failing the whole sync, treat the database as gone: log a
warning, skip it, and let the downstream sync() call garbage-collect
any previously synced records for that database.

fix(auth): prevent session-fixation / login-CSRF in WorkOS OAuth flow (#23379)

* fix(auth): prevent session-fixation / login-CSRF in WorkOS OAuth flow

Prevent session-fixation / login-CSRF by binding each OAuth flow to the
browser session with a cryptographic nonce (RFC 6749 §10.12).

The login endpoint:
1. generates a random nonce
2. stores it in an HttpOnly cookie
3. embeds it in the OAuth state

The callback verifies the two match via constant-time comparison
before issuing a session.

Add redirect_uri validation via origin allowlist and redirectTo via trusted-origin
check

Extracts shared helpers (decodeJwtPayload, buildExpiredCookie,
getSessionCookieParams) and adds functional tests for all five actions.

Users mid-login at deploy time will see a nonce-mismatch error and need
to re-login; the window is seconds and self-recoverable.

fix(steering): use promoted user's auth for agent loop after pending message promotion

When a pending message is promoted and triggers a new agent loop, the loop
was incorrectly running with the previous user's auth context (User A who
triggered the original agent). This caused tool approval events to be
attributed to User A instead of User B (who sent the steering message),
resulting in a confused UI where User A saw approval buttons and User B saw
"Waiting for User B to confirm" without being able to approve.

The fix creates a proper Authenticator for the promoted user inside the
advisory-locked transaction and uses it for the new agent loop, audit logs,
and all downstream operations. Also makes Authenticator.fromUserIdAndWorkspaceId
transaction-compatible by threading the transaction parameter through all
internal resource queries.

Remove legacy tool_error shim for tool_personal_auth_required

The legacy tool_error event emitted alongside tool_personal_auth_required
caused the client to set the agent message status to "failed" while the DB
kept it as "created". This desync made the client think no agent was running,
creating a spurious placeholder agent message (with header) when the user
sent a steering message while a tool was awaiting connection approval.

The legacy shim was past its removal date (2025-12-05). All clients now
handle tool_personal_auth_required natively.

Fixes https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/7432

Add dsbx forward e2e test suite (#24387)

Dockerised bun tests that exercise the full sandbox egress path:
test client -> iptables REDIRECT -> dsbx forward -> egress-proxy ->
target. Replaces egress-proxy/scripts/smoke.ts so all e2e coverage
lives in one place and runs against the production-shaped topology
instead of poking the proxy directly.

Covers:
- 6-case JWT + domain matrix (allow/deny, expired/wrong-iss/wrong-aud/
  bad-sig), with deny-log entry + reason=proxy_denied validated for
  every DENY outcome.
- Real streaming agent call (sId=dust) via @dust-tt/client against the
  live EU proxy, asserting tokens flow through the tunnel.

Stage 1 of the Dockerfile builds the dsbx binary; stage 2 is a Debian
runtime with iptables, bun, a dedicated dust-fwd uid, and the
orchestrator. entrypoint.sh installs the REDIRECT rules (requires
--cap-add=NET_ADMIN) and execs smoke.ts, which restarts dsbx forward
between JWT cases (token file is read once at startup) and drops to
dust-fwd via runuser for the actual HTTPS calls.

sandbox: bake egress plumbing into image (dormant, uid-scoped) (#24424)

* sandbox: bake egress plumbing into image (dormant, uid-scoped)

Adds dust-fwd system user, iptables package, and /etc/dust to the bedrock
image. In the template layer, creates the dormant agent-proxied user
(uid 1001) and bakes the final uid-scoped iptables ruleset (loopback
RETURN, TCP -> forwarder REDIRECT, resolver-pinned DNS, RFC1918 + IMDS
drops, IPv6 drop). Rules only match uid 1001; until a follow-up flips
tool execution to agent-proxied, nothing runs as uid 1001, so this ships
as a zero-behavior-change template bump (dust-base 0.7.4 -> 0.7.5,
bedrock 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0). Includes a build-time assertion that sudo stays
absent, since uid-based scoping is the enforcement contract.

* sandbox: fix iptables table ordering + agent/agent-proxied file handoff

Two corrections to the dormant ruleset before it goes live:

nat/OUTPUT runs before filter/OUTPUT for locally generated traffic, so
the loopback exemption and metadata/RFC1918 DROPs only worked at the
filter layer, after the nat REDIRECT had already rewritten the
destination to 127.0.0.1:9990. Localhost TCP from uid 1001 would have
landed on the forwarder instead of the original port, and the
iptables-level defense in depth for metadata/private ranges was a no-op
for TCP. Moved loopback + private + IMDS exemptions into nat ahead of
the REDIRECT; filter DROPs now see the original dst and actually fire.
Loopback has no matching rule in filter so local services keep working.

Separately, tool execs during the PR1 -> PR2 compat-skip window still
run as agent (uid 1000) and would leave files at 0644/0755 that
agent-proxied (uid 1001) can't edit after the user flip. Added setgid
on /home/agent and /files/conversation plus default POSIX ACLs via the
acl package so new files in the shared paths are group-writable by
default, regardless of umask.

* sandbox: enforce sudo invariant in bedrock build

[front] Reduce peak concurrent SQL on reaction endpoint (#24542)

* [front] Reduce peak concurrent SQL on reaction endpoint

The POST/DELETE reaction endpoint was calling getConversation, which
fully renders every message in the conversation (user/agent/content
fragments) to locate the target message and republish an event. For a
single-reaction mutation this fans out ~15-20 concurrent SQL queries
via nested Promise.all branches (batchRenderUserMessages,
batchRenderAgentMessages, batchRenderContentFragment, plus their inner
Promise.alls and the per-agent-message parent fallback).

Replace that path with:
- ConversationResource.fetchById for access checks (uses the space
  already loaded on the resource, drops the redundant
  SpaceResource.fetchById).
- A narrow MessageModel.findOne by sId for target validation
  (getReactionTargetMessageType).
- Post-mutation: render only the target message via batchRenderMessages
  on a 1-element array, and for user messages fetch only the preceding
  content fragments with a single MessageModel.findAll
  (publishReactionUpdate).

Peak concurrent queries drop from ~15-20 down to ~5-6. The new helpers
live in lib/api/assistant/reaction_update.ts to keep the API route free
of Sequelize models and avoid a cycle with messages.ts.

* [front] Add functional tests for reactions endpoint

Covers the happy paths (POST/DELETE on user and agent messages) and
the main error paths: unknown message, compaction message, unknown
conversation, missing body, unsupported method, and deleting a
reaction that doesn't exist.

* [front] Reject content fragments on the reactions endpoint

Content fragments were classified as valid reaction targets by the
route but the publish path can't handle them, so the previous behavior
was "persist the reaction, log a publish failure, return 200". Reject
them explicitly with 400 before the mutation.

* [front] Document why publishReactionUpdate fetches content fragments

Makes explicit that the fetch exists to keep the reused post/edit event
payload consistent for subscribers, and that a dedicated
reactions_updated event would make it unnecessary.

[front] fix MCP static credential submit race (#24574)

The Snowflake MCP connection flow was silently stalling with a "form is
not ready" toast because staticFormRef.current was being nulled out
mid-submit. Root cause is two independent changes that interact badly:

- CreateMCPServerDialog has `form.reset(defaultValues)` running on every
  change of defaultValues while the dialog is open.
- defaultValues depends on existingViewNames, which is derived from the
  SWR list mutated by createInternalMCPServer itself.

So on a successful POST /mcp the SWR invalidation re-renders the dialog,
defaultValues changes, the effect resets useCase to null, and that
unmounts the static credential form — nulling the ref right before we
try to submit it.

Fix:
- Capture the form handle before any async work so the submit can't race
  with a re-render that unmounts the child form.
- Reset the form only on the closed→open edge, not on every
  defaultValues change. SWR mutations during submit no longer clobber
  in-flight form state.

When the skill builder is showing pending suggestions, interacting with
version history doesn't make sense — you can't compare versions while the
editor is also being hijacked by a pending diff. This PR hardens that mode:

  background) to the instructions editor when suggestions are shown, matching
  the existing behavior when a history item is selected (`isDiffMode`). The
  editor was already made non-editable via `editor.setEditable(!hasSuggestions)`;
  this just makes the readonly state visually consistent with the history-diff
  state.

   of leaking into the policy_denied bucket. Make normalize_domain_or_ip
   private since it's no longer used outside domain.rs.

2. Add workspace policy test coverage:
   - workspace_policy_allows_domain: workspace-only allow path
   - sandbox_policy_allows_when_workspace_has_no_policy: fallback path

   allowlist" (renamed from TemporaryAllowlist → DefaultAllowlist).
   Domains in this list are allowed for all sandboxes, merged with
   per-workspace and per-sandbox GCS policies. This removes the hard
   deploy dependency on the front lifecycle PR — the existing production
   env var keeps working while GCS policies layer on top.

   A domain is allowed if it appears in ANY of: the default allowlist,
   the workspace GCS policy, or the sandbox GCS policy. The default
   allowlist is checked first (cheap in-memory) to skip GCS lookups
   for common infrastructure domains like dust.tt.

2. Reject IP literals at handshake parse time: switch handshake.rs from
   normalize_domain_or_ip to normalize_dns_name so IPs fail as
   MalformedHandshake instead of leaking into the policy_denied bucket.

* feat(sbx): Add cache invalidation endpoint to egress proxy

Policy changes made through the admin UI were taking up to 60 seconds
to propagate due to the egress proxy's moka cache TTL. This adds a
POST /invalidate-policy endpoint on the proxy's internal health
listener so front can bust specific cache keys immediately after
writing or deleting workspace policy files.

Proxy side:
- GcsPolicyProvider gains invalidate(key) to evict a single cache entry
- Health server gets POST /invalidate-policy (JWT-authenticated, same
  secret as the forwarder protocol)
- Accepts { keys: ["w:<wId>", "s:<sbId>"] }, returns { invalidated: N }

Front side:
- writeWorkspacePolicy/deleteWorkspacePolicy fire-and-forget an
  invalidation request after successful GCS writes
- New optional EGRESS_PROXY_INTERNAL_URL env var; when unset the call
  is silently skipped (graceful degradation)

* fix: cargo fmt formatting

* fix: address review feedback on cache invalidation

1. Wrap entire invalidateWorkspacePolicyCache body in try/catch so
   config/token-mint errors can't escape as unhandled rejections from
   the fire-and-forget call sites.

2. Strengthen the eviction integration test: after populating the cache,
   swap the mock GCS backing policy to deny "localhost", invalidate,
   then assert the next handshake is DENIED — proving the cache entry
   was actually evicted and re-fetched.

   This required making MockGcsState.objects mutable (RwLock) so the
   test can change the backing policy while the proxy is running.

* fix: biome formatting for config.ts

* feat(sbx): Proper JWT auth for cache invalidation endpoint

- Make sbId optional in JWT claims (normalized to None when empty)
- Add optional "action" claim for admin operations
- Invalidation endpoint now requires action="invalidate-policy";
  a regular sandbox tunnel token (no action) is rejected with 403
- Connection handler enforces sb_id is present (rejects admin tokens)
- Front: new mintEgressInvalidationJwt() with 60s TTL and action claim
- Rename ValidatedSandboxToken → ValidatedToken to reflect flexibility

This ensures a sandbox forwarder token cannot be repurposed for cache
invalidation, and vice versa. Invalidation tokens are short-lived (60s)
to limit blast radius.

* feat(sbx): Derive invalidation target from JWT claims, not request body

- Remove request body from /invalidate-policy; the cache key to evict

- Connection handler now rejects tokens with an action claim — a

feat(sbx): Sandbox-level egress allowlist tool (#24894)

Adds a new `add_egress_domain` tool to the sandbox internal MCP
server. The tool appends a single user-approved exact domain to the
current sandbox's policy file in GCS (`sandboxes/{providerId}.json`),
which the egress proxy already merges with the workspace policy on
every connection. The tool requires user approval (stake `high`) and
only accepts exact domains — wildcards are rejected.

After a successful write, fires a fire-and-forget invalidation against
the proxy admin endpoint so the change applies to the next connection
without waiting for the moka TTL. The sandbox resource also deletes
the GCS object after the provider destroy succeeds, so we don't keep
orphaned policies around after a sandbox is reaped.

Audit logged as `sandbox_egress_policy.sandbox_updated`.

* fix(sbx): preserve shell variable references in bash tool

User commands were embedded inside a double-quoted bash string by
wrapCommand, so the outer shell expanded $VAR, $(...) and backticks
against its own (empty) environment before the inner shell tool ever
saw the command. Variable assignments succeeded but every reference
silently resolved to "".

Wrap the user's command in a single-quoted heredoc instead, which
disables every form of expansion. Throw if the command contains the
heredoc delimiter on its own line. Add execution-level tests that
actually run the wrapped output through bash, so this class of bug
can't slip past string-snapshot tests again.

feat(sbx): show execution wall clock time on action details (#24982)

* feat(sbx): show execution wall clock time on action details

The MCP layer already measures and persists executionDurationMs for every
tool call. Plumb it through ToolExecutionDetailsProps and render it on the
sandbox bash action details: next to the exit code in the status line, and
in the sidebar Output header. Helps users understand how long sandbox
commands actually take to run.

* refactor: render execution duration in ActionDetailsWrapper for all tools

Move the wall clock duration rendering from MCPSandboxActionDetails into
ActionDetailsWrapper so every tool detail (web search, sandbox, browse,
tables query, ...) gets it for free. MCPActionDetails wraps its dispatch
in an ActionExecutionProvider that publishes action.executionDurationMs
through context, and the wrapper picks it up automatically. Each detail
component can still override via an explicit prop if needed.

* feat: live ticking duration on action details, "executed in" label

Update the duration label to read "executed in 4.2s" once the action
completes. While the action is running, tick a live elapsed counter
("running for 12s") sourced from action.createdAt, refreshed every
second. Both pieces flow through ActionExecutionContext so every
tool detail picks them up automatically.

* fix: render live ticking duration as whole seconds

The 1Hz tick was producing fractional readouts (1.3s, 2.3s, ...) because
the formatter always used .toFixed(1). While running, floor to whole
seconds so the user sees a stable 1s, 2s, 3s, ... cadence. The completed
state keeps the precise sub-second formatting (4.2s).

* fix: stop the live duration ticker as soon as the action status is final

Previously the ticker only stopped once executionDurationMs landed in the
client state, which can lag the actual completion. Pass the action's
status into ActionExecutionContext and treat any final status (succeeded,
errored, denied) as "no longer running" — the ticker stops immediately
and the wrapper switches to the executed-in label as soon as the
duration arrives.

* fix: prefer live streaming action over SWR snapshot in tool detail panel

AgentSingleActionPanel was reading the action exclusively from
useConversationMessageAction (a one-shot SWR fetch). During streaming,
the action is updated live in virtuosoMsg.actions via agent_action_success,
but the panel never saw those updates — so status, output, and
executionDurationMs all lagged the actual completion, leaving the live
duration ticker running well past the action finishing.

Prefer the action from virtuosoMsg.actions when available, fall back to
the SWR snapshot otherwise (e.g. cold-loading the panel with no active
stream).

* chore: biome format

* fix: address review findings on action duration display

- Gate the live ticker on status === "running" specifically, instead of
  any non-final status. Otherwise an action sitting in ready_allowed_*
  or any blocked_* state (auth, validation, user-input...) would tick
  for minutes of approval time and then jump to a much smaller
  executed-in value, since executionDurationMs only covers the actual
  tool invocation. Renamed the context flag from isFinal to isExecuting
  to make the intent explicit.
- Let the single-action panel render the streamed action immediately
  even while SWR is loading. Previously the loading branch returned a
  spinner unconditionally, defeating the live-action preference on
  initial open.
- Fix the minute formatter to never produce "1m 60s" for inputs like
  119.6s. Round to whole seconds first, then split into minutes and
  remainder via integer division.

* fix: snapshot client-observed execution start, drop unused wrapper prop

Two related cleanups on the live elapsed counter:

- Replace the use of action.createdAt as the elapsed origin with a
  client-observed snapshot taken when isExecuting transitions to true.
  This ensures any time the action sat in ready/blocked states isn't
  counted toward "running for...". Also explicitly refresh nowMs on the
  rising edge so the first rendered tick after enabling isn't computed
  from a stale mount-time value. Falls back to startedAtMs only when the
  panel mounts mid-execution and we have no transition to observe.
- Remove the unused executionDurationMs override prop on
  ActionDetailsWrapper. The wrapper now reads exclusively from
  ActionExecutionContext, which simplifies the contract: there's one
  source of truth, no prop/context override semantics.

Fix multiple stake approvals for same tool (#25006)

When the agent fires multiple tool calls in parallel (or several blocked actions land before any are approved), each call is stored as `blocked_validation_required`. Clicking "Always allow" on one only flipped that single row — the other pending confirmations stayed blocked, forcing the user to click through every duplicate.

This change adds a client-side cascade in `MCPToolValidationRequired` after the always-approved call succeeds, the component scans the queue for other pending blocked actions of the same tool (`mcpServerName + toolName`) and approves them sequentially before removing them from the queue. The user's `user_tool_approvals` row is already persisted by the first call, so future calls remain auto-approved through the normal `getExecutionStatusFromConfig` path; this only resolves the duplicates that were already queued at the moment of the click.

Suppress payment-failure banner/email for enterprise workspaces (#24975)

Enterprise customers were repeatedly receiving "Your payment has failed" banners and emails while their workspaces were healthy and contracts active. Two triggers, one root cause:

- The Stripe `invoice.payment_failed` webhook fires for enterprise invoices within their 30-day wire-payment window, marking the workspace past-due.
- For workspaces that transitioned from Pro to Enterprise, a legacy Pro subscription tied to the same Stripe customer can still fire `invoice.payment_failed`. The webhook resolved that event via `fetchByStripeId` back to the workspace and processed it without checking
  what the workspace's *current* plan was.

Both surfaces now key on the workspace's **current active plan** (`auth.subscription()` server-side, `useAuth().subscription` client-side), not the plan attached to the failing Stripe invoice:

- **Webhook** (`pages/api/stripe/webhook.ts`): early-return from the `invoice.payment_failed` handler when the workspace's current plan starts with `ENT_`. No `paymentFailingSince` set, no email sent.
- **Banner** (`components/navigation/AppStatusBanner.tsx`): hide `SubscriptionPastDueBanner` for enterprise workspaces. Belt-and-suspenders, and crucially this **retroactively hides the banner for the already-affected customers** without a DB cleanup — their
`paymentFailingSince` flag stays in the table but stops rendering on next page load.

feat(sbx): redact env var values from bash output, instruct agent on disclosure (#25051)

* feat(sbx): redact env var values from bash output, instruct agent on disclosure

Two-layer disclosure control for sandbox env vars:

1. Skill instruction. Tells the agent that workspace env vars are reachable
   via standard env APIs and may be used to authenticate or feed code paths,
   but never printed/echoed/cat'd/encoded/listed. Refuse user requests for
   values; presence-check via boolean (`"FOO" in os.environ`). Also explains
   what the `«redacted: $FOO»` marker means if the agent ever sees it in
   tool output (don't retry, don't reconstruct).

2. Bash-tool output redactor. After `formatExecOutput`, scan the assembled
   payload for occurrences of any eligible workspace env var value and
   replace them with `«redacted: $NAME»` markers before returning the MCP
   content blocks. Emits `logger.warn` with `varNames` on any replacement.
   Eligibility floor: value length >= 12, not in a low-value denylist
   (`true`, `production`, `admin`, ...), not pure digits, not pure
   alphanumeric < 16 chars. Ineligible values get a one-time-per-process
   `logger.info` so misconfigured short secrets are visible once. Fail-
   closed: a `loadEnv` `Err` (decryption failure) returns an MCP error
   from the bash tool, suppressing the output entirely.

This is defense-in-depth, not a guarantee: encoded output, network calls
from sandbox code, transformed values, and short / dictionary-like values
can still leak. The skill instruction is the primary control.

Tests cover: eligible value redacted in stdout, eligible value redacted in
the appended `<network_proxy_logs>` block, ineligible values not redacted
(once-per-name `logger.info` across two invocations), fail-closed on
`loadEnv` error.

* clarify DST_ prefix and re-export pattern in skill instructions

Tell the agent that all workspace env var names are prefixed with DST_, and
that if a tool / CLI / SDK expects a specific unprefixed name (e.g.
OPENAI_API_KEY) the agent must read the DST_-prefixed variable and
re-export it under the expected name itself before invoking the tool.
Examples given for both bash (inline VAR=$DST_VAR cmd ...) and Python
(os.environ assignment).

* simplify redaction eligibility check; tighten skill instructions

Redactor:
- Drop the LOW_VALUE_DENYLIST and the pure-digit / pure-alphanumeric
  carve-outs. They were redundant once you have a length floor + a real
  entropy check.
- New rule: value.length >= 16 AND Shannon entropy >= 3.5 bits/char.
- Drop logIneligibleRedactionValueOnce and its process-scoped Set —

  signal that matters.

Skill instructions:
- Mention the bash shell explicitly (env vars are reachable from regular

- Drop language-specific API names (process.env / os.environ) — obvious.

[front] no-store on X-Reload-Required responses (#25115)

* [front] Add Origin to Vary and no-store on X-Reload-Required

Reproduced via Playwright: with two tabs (one on a flagged commit, one on
prod), Chrome served the flagged tab's cached response (with its own
Access-Control-Allow-Origin) to the other tab, breaking it with a CORS
error and propagating X-Reload-Required: true. Two gaps in the previous
Vary fix (#25112):

1. Origin missing from Vary - ACAO varies per request origin, so cache
   entries keyed only by URL + X-Commit-Hash get reused across origins.
2. Flagged responses were cache-control: public, max-age=120 - once a
   tab on a flagged commit cached the X-Reload-Required: true response,
   it kept reload-looping for 2 minutes even after the flag was cleared
   in Redis.

Fix: Vary on X-Commit-Hash + Origin, and Cache-Control: no-store on
flagged responses so they never enter the cache.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Drop Origin from Vary - production has a single SPA origin

Origin in Vary only matters when multiple origins consume the same API
cache, which is only true for preview deploys/testing. In production all
users are on app.dust.tt with a single Origin, so Vary: Origin does not
help. Keeping just X-Commit-Hash and the Cache-Control: no-store on
flagged responses, which together cover the actual production bug.

[front] Heal poisoned X-Reload-Required cache entries via 304 merge (#25166)

Idle clients keep firing reload logs hours after the flag is cleared
because their cached entries never get overwritten: ETag-based 304
revalidations on stable-body endpoints (user, auth-context, app-status)
preserve the original X-Reload-Required: true since 304 doesn't carry
the header. Per HTTP spec, the browser merges 304 headers into the
stored entry and leaves untouched fields alone.

Always emitting X-Reload-Required: false on non-flagged responses lets
the next 304 merge overwrite the stored true with false, so cached
entries self-heal on the next revalidation.

[sandbox] Phase 0 PoC for egress MITM secret swap (#25073)

* [sandbox] phase 0 PoC for egress MITM secret swap

Adds the minimum machinery to prove the dsbx-side MITM substitution path
works end to end. Behind a config flag (EGRESS_MITM_EXPERIMENT_HOST), so
prod behavior is unchanged when unset.

- dsbx: ephemeral CA via rcgen, per-SNI leaf signing, HTTP/1.1 byte
  rewriter that swaps __DUST_EXPERIMENT_PLACEHOLDER__ for an equal-length
  __SUCCESSFULLY_REPLACED________ on the request side. MITM only kicks in
  on port 443 when the SNI matches the configured experiment host.
- front: new --mitm-experiment-host / --mitm-ca-path flags wired into
  the dsbx start command. After dsbx is healthy, install the issued CA
  into the sandbox trust store and build a merged bundle at
  /etc/dust/ca-bundle.pem. Inject SSL_CERT_FILE / CURL_CA_BUNDLE into
  the agent env so curl trusts the dsbx leaf without breaking non-MITM
  TLS to public sites.
- front: POST/GET /api/v1/w/[wId]/sandbox/egress-experiment that logs
  the X-Dust-Experiment header to Datadog and echoes it back, so we can
  observe whether the swap reached the upstream.

* [sandbox] address review and fix CI

- Gate the egress-experiment endpoint on EGRESS_MITM_EXPERIMENT_HOST
  being set, return 404 otherwise. Stops the unauthenticated v1 endpoint
  from being reachable in regions where the experiment is not active.
- Drop the inbound Authorization header from the Datadog log; the
  endpoint only needs `received` for the smoke flow.
- Add the new config getter to the egress.test.ts mock so the existing
  setupEgressForwarder tests pass.
- Fix doc comments that claimed the placeholder was 32 bytes (it is 31).
- Trim a noisy info log that was emitting two static constants per
  request.
- Simplifier pass: drop the MitmTarget struct in dsbx, trim a couple of
  comments to keep only the WHY.

* [sandbox] address review feedback on phase 0 PoC

- dsbx: generate and write the MITM CA before binding the listener.
  Front uses port-LISTEN as the readiness signal then immediately reads
  /etc/dust/egress-ca.pem; bind-then-write was racey on cold boot and
  on restart (stale CA).
- front: run setupEgressForwarder before mounts in tools/index.ts. The
  agent env exports SSL_CERT_FILE / CURL_CA_BUNDLE pointing at
  /etc/dust/ca-bundle.pem; mounts (gcsfuse) make HTTPS calls that read
  it, so the bundle has to exist first.
- front: gate the egress-experiment endpoint on a shared bearer token
  (X-Dust-Experiment-Token) in addition to the env-var enable check.
  Returns 404 if either the host or the token is unset, 401 on token
  mismatch.
- dsbx: tighten the request rewriter to split at \r\n\r\n and only
  rewrite the header prefix. Body bytes pulled into the same TCP read
  pass through unchanged. Adds a negative test asserting that.
- Mark Phase 0 temporary code with PHASE0(remove with the experiment)
  comments and add TODO(phase 1) for the bits that stay but are
  incomplete (non-curl trust setup, ALPN h1.1 forcing, allowedDomains
  policy, cross-chunk straddle handling).
- Update CLAUDE_SECRET_SWAP_DESIGN.md to use the actual padded
  replacement string (__SUCCESSFULLY_REPLACED________, 31 bytes).
- More tests: MITM-enabled setupEgressForwarder, install-failure
  surfacing, no-MITM-flags-when-disabled, token reject paths.

* [sandbox] phase 0: don't rewrite URL or method line; expose token to agent

- dsbx: rewriter now skips the request line entirely (everything up to
  the first \r\n). A placeholder in the URL passes through unchanged,
  matching the design's "no URL rewriting" rule. New negative test
  covers a placeholder in the query string.
- front: when the experiment is enabled, also inject DUST_EXPERIMENT_TOKEN
  into the agent env so the smoke curl from inside the sandbox is
  self-contained (no out-of-band token setup).
- design doc: smoke flow updated to include the token header.

* [sandbox] mark egress-experiment endpoint as temporary in a file header

* Rename design doc and rewrite in design-doc voice

Drops the "design notes / investigation" framing in favor of a
Context / Goals / Non-goals / Proposal / Phases / Open Questions
structure. Updates all in-repo references to the new filename.

* Resolve open questions on phasing and env-var classes

- HTTP/2 is part of the MVP but sequenced as Phase 2 after h1 lands.
- Headers + URL only in Phase 1; bodies move to Phase 3.
- Split env vars into config vars (offline, plaintext) and secrets
  (HTTPS only, per-domain scoped, substituted on the wire).
- Full mainstream trust coverage in Phase 1.

* Resolve remaining design open questions

- Cross-sandbox replay: documented as expected behavior, no special
  detection. Upstream rejection is the loud failure.
- CA private key: memory-only, never on disk. Agent UID can't reach
  dsbx memory under the "agent never escalates to root" invariant, so
  ptrace_scope is not load-bearing.
- Migration: existing rows default to config vars, promotion is fully
  manual (internal-workspace-first rollout).

Skill prompt update is the only remaining open question.

* Resolve skill prompt design

- Explicit, not opaque: name the substitution mechanism in the prompt
  so the agent can use secrets correctly and explain failure modes to
  users (cert-pinning, config-vs-secret misuse, etc.).
- Two env-var prefixes lexically distinguish classes: config (DST_*)
  vs secrets (different prefix, TBD).
- Hard "DO NOT" list at the top of the prompt for known foot-guns;
  per-secret inline notes deferred.
- Future: a "list-secrets" command on dsbx for dynamic discovery.

* Sync code comments with rewritten design doc

Replaces stale "§3-§4" / "§5" / "§5.3" section pointers with the new
section names from the rewritten SECRET_SWAP_DESIGN.md. Clarifies that
HTTP/2 is a Phase 2 step and bodies are Phase 3.

* Address design-review feedback

Doc:
- Drop HMAC for placeholder derivation; use a per-secret 16-byte random
  nonce stored on the row. Sidesteps the "where does the workspace key
  live" question both reviewers flagged.
- Clarify placeholder identity: workspace-scoped, not sandbox-scoped.
  Within-workspace replay across sandboxes substitutes correctly and
  that's fine - the secret IS a workspace authority. Drop the
  contradictory "sandbox-version-bound" claim.
- Make "loud failure" actually loud: dsbx drops the connection on
  recognized-placeholder + disallowed destination instead of forwarding
  the literal placeholder to a potentially attacker-controlled upstream.
- Phase 1 MITM scope is the union of all configured secrets'
  allowedDomains. Other 443 traffic stays on the existing TCP-splice
  path so cert-pinned and mTLS clients to non-secret domains aren't
  affected.
- Substitution gate requires SNI + Host (h1) + :authority: (h2) to all
  agree on a domain in the matching secret's allowedDomains. Closes
  the SNI/Host confused-deputy edge case.
- CA persisted on tmpfs at /run/dust/egress-ca.{pem,key}, per-sandbox-
  VM lifetime. Survives dsbx restart so trust env vars (Node, Java)
  that read at process start don't go stale on a forwarder restart.
- Live update / rotation is out of scope for Phase 1; document as
  recreate-only. Phase 2 may add kill-and-recreate.
- Body-substitution phasing standardized on Phase 3 throughout.
- Trust matrix splits Requests (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE) from HTTPX
  (SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR). Source-cite Node, Requests, HTTPX docs.

Code:
- Phase 0 enablement: dsbx MITM flags and SSL_CERT_FILE / CURL_CA_BUNDLE
  injection now require BOTH EGRESS_MITM_EXPERIMENT_HOST and
  EGRESS_MITM_EXPERIMENT_TOKEN to be set, matching the experiment
  endpoint's own gating. Setting only one was a half-on state.
- New test for the host-without-token regression case.

* Address second-round review feedback

- Weaken the "literal placeholder is never forwarded" overpromise.
  The real invariant is "real value never forwarded outside
  allowedDomains". The placeholder is an opaque random nonce; whether
  it reaches non-MITM domains is informationally null. dsbx still drops
  on placeholder-to-disallowed on the MITM-scoped surface where it can
  see the bytes.
- Specify the egress-secrets.json schema and storage model: plaintext
  on tmpfs at /run/dust/egress-secrets.json, root-owned 0600,
  { name, placeholder, value, allowedDomains }[]. Same posture as the
  CA private key. Drop the misleading "encryptedValue" wording.
- Port 80: drop on placeholder, never substitute. Substituting on
  plaintext would put the real secret on the open internet.
- Non-HTTP over MITM-scoped TLS: pass through unchanged. Consistent
  with the weak-claim framing; dsbx doesn't substitute (no HTTP
  framing) and doesn't scan.
- Raw TCP / non-80/443 ports: remove the design claim. Egress today
  denies non-HTTP/non-HTTPS. Out of scope here.
- Wildcard support in allowedDomains: yes, leading `*.` form. Same
  shape as the workspace egress policy.
- Skill prompt: add Rust-specific steer (use `reqwest` default features
  or rustls-tls-native-roots; not rustls-tls / webpki-roots).

Phase 0 host-only gating bug both reviewers flagged was already fixed
in cf97251256; verified still in place.

* Note broad Linux-tool coverage in trust section

Adds an explicit paragraph before the trust-env matrix calling out that
the system-store install plus the env-var matrix covers the vast
majority of Linux CLI tools and language runtimes by convention - curl,
wget, git, apt, pip, npm, cargo, go, gcloud/aws/kubectl, etc. The
matrix exceptions are the actual known holes; everything else is
implicitly covered.

* Address third-round review feedback

Phase 1 spec changes:
- Full HTTP/1.1 message loop in the rewriter, not Phase 0's
  first-headers-prefix shape. Per-request parsing, per-request Host
  validation, pipelining, fail-closed on malformed/oversized headers.
  Carrying Phase 0's prefix-only shape would be unsafe on keep-alive
  connections where multiple requests share a TCP.
- Live update via file-watch promoted into Phase 1. front rewrites
  /run/dust/egress-secrets.json on every active sandbox of a workspace
  when admin updates/rotates/deletes a secret; dsbx inotify-watches
  and reloads. Closes the up-to-30-day stale-secret window the
  snapshot-only model would have left open.
- Secret value validation, two layers: admin UI rejects CR/LF/NUL/
  other ASCII control chars and enforces 8KB max length; dsbx
  fail-closed at substitution time as defense in depth. Closes the
  CRLF header-injection primitive at both ends.
- Per-secret allowedDomains and central egress allowlist are
  configured independently, no save-time validation, no auto-add.
  Reason: the central allowlist is union(default, workspace,
  sandbox-dynamic via add_egress_domain), not fully knowable at
  admin secret-edit time. Errors surface at runtime via the proxy
  deny path.
- Secret env-var naming: prefix-only (DSEC_*), no shadowed natural
  names. Agents alias to SDK-expected names with a one-line snippet
  in their script. Trade: lexical clarity in env wins over the no-
  code-changes goal, which was overstated for SDKs that auto-
  discover by exact name.
- mTLS on MITM-scoped domains documented as explicitly unsupported.
  dsbx opens fresh outbound TLS without the agent's client cert.

Doc cleanups:
- CA wording consistent: tmpfs-persisted per sandbox VM, not
  "memory-only" (table fix). Boot-script installs cert into system
  store, not the agent UID (line-219 fix).
- Trust coverage prose narrowed to verified-as-of-design list +
  unverified-hypothesis list. Drop scp/rsync/docker (not TLS or
  not through MITM).
- Phase 0 footprint now correctly says "@ignoreswagger" instead of
  "one swagger annotation".
- Phase 0 http_rewriter.rs comment updated to reference the random-
  nonce placeholder (was HMAC-derived).

* Address fourth-round review feedback

Placeholder model:
- Make it explicit that the placeholder nonce is stable for the life of
  the secret row. Generated once at create time. Value rotation does
  NOT change it. allowedDomains edits do NOT change it. Only deletion
  ends it. Running sandboxes that hold the placeholder string in env
  continue to work after a value rotation, no env refresh needed.
- The earlier "rotation regenerates the nonce" wording was inherited
  baggage from the HMAC-derived design and bought us nothing
  security-wise: the placeholder is opaque, an exfiltrated placeholder
  doesn't help an attacker without a provisioned sandbox, and breaking
  persisted state was a UX cost without a security gain.

File-watch failure semantics:
- Atomic write at front (temp + rename, POSIX-atomic).
- dsbx fail-closed parse: on parse error, clear the in-memory secret
  map rather than retain old state. No substitution until a valid file
  appears. Fail-closed beats risking a rotated value release.
- Sleeping sandboxes: front rewrites the secrets file on the wake path
  before any agent code runs.
- Unreachable sandboxes / write failures: front retries with backoff;
  after exhaustion, kill the sandbox so a fresh provisioning happens
  on next use. Accepted disruption cost for the security guarantee
  that rotation/deletion can't linger past the propagation deadline.

URL substitution:
- Deferred from Phase 1 to Phase 2. Phase 1 substitutes in headers
  only. dsbx drops the connection on observed placeholder in the
  request line (loud failure; agent learns to use headers). URL-context
  encoding rules will be specified in Phase 2.

Goals doc:
- Soften "no agent code changes required" to match the resolved
  DSEC_*-prefix decision: most clients work without changes, SDKs that
  auto-discover env vars by exact name need a one-line aliasing snippet.

* Address fifth-round design review

- URL scope: unambiguously Phase 1 = headers only, URL = Phase 2,
  body = Phase 3. Removed contradictory "headers + URL" wording.
- Placeholder lifecycle: rotation does NOT change the nonce.
  Resolved-decisions wording fixed to match the main spec.
- Tmpfs write mechanism specified: front writes
  /run/dust/egress-secrets.json via a single privileged exec piping
  JSON on stdin, install -o root -m 600 to a temp in /run/dust,
  atomic mv. No agent-readable temp, no secret in argv.
- Encoded auth coverage honestly documented: literal bearer/api-key
  headers only in Phase 1. Basic auth, HMAC, SigV4 fail loudly at
  upstream. Skill prompt and admin UI advertise the limit. Richer
  formats deferred to Phase 4+ via a per-secret format field.
- Live update deferred out of Phase 1: rewrite-on-wake only for
  Phase 1, push-to-active-sandbox + race serialization moved to
  Phase 4+ with a knowingly-underspecified callout.
- Migration scope clarified: existing sandboxes at promotion time
  keep plaintext DST_* env. Acceptable because rollout is
  internal-only.

* Tighten design doc: align placeholder prefix, drop HMAC callbacks

- Placeholder marker: __DST_SECRET_<hex>__ -> __DSEC_<hex>__ so it
  matches the env-var prefix scheme (DSEC_* secrets, DST_* config).
- Drop the vestigial non-goal about not replacing the central
  egress allowlist; redundant with the rest of the doc.
- Remove references to the prior HMAC-derived placeholder design;
  irrelevant now that the format is a per-secret random nonce.

* Treat WebSocket support as MVP

- Phase 1: upgrade-request headers go through the normal h1
  rewriter (covers Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Realtime, anything
  that authenticates in the upgrade). On 101 Switching Protocols,
  dsbx flips the connection into byte-splice mode for the rest, so
  MITM-scoped WS connections work without parsing frames.
- Phase 3: in-frame substitution lands alongside body substitution,
  same per-secret includeBody opt-in. RFC 6455 framing via
  tungstenite, bounded-buffer fragment reassembly. permessage-
  deflate is stripped at upgrade time so the rewriter stays on
  plaintext; full deflate support moves to Phase 4+.
- Removed the bare "Websocket Upgrade" entry from Phase 4+.
- Resolved decisions: explicit MVP commitment for WS.

* Add HTTP Basic auth to Phase 1 scope

Basic auth is just base64-around-a-literal-credential-string, and
the placeholder alphabet round-trips through base64 cleanly. The
rewriter detects Authorization: Basic, decodes, scans, substitutes
under the normal SNI/Host/allowedDomains gate, re-encodes. Fail-soft
on invalid base64. Small bounded code path, doesn't generalize to
HMAC/SigV4 (those still need real request signing and stay Phase 4+).

* Fix overstated "loud failure" claim for encoded auth

For HMAC/SigV4/transformed-placeholder cases, dsbx does nothing
special: it forwards bytes unchanged and the upstream returns 401
because what arrived isn't a valid credential. That's an upstream
property, not something our system enforces. Reword accordingly.

* Clarify the "JVM without keytool import" known hole

The previous one-liner read like an unconditional JVM hole; it's
actually a conditional one. Java has no env-var fallback for trust
roots (no SSL_CERT_FILE, no NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS), so the only way
to add a CA is keytool -importcert into $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/
cacerts. The boot script does that, but the import only sticks to
the keystore of the JDK that was current at boot. Spell out the
failure modes (JDK installed mid-session, multiple JDKs, agent
overrides javax.net.ssl.trustStore) and the symptom (PKIX path
building failed, no silent leak).

* Skill prompt: warn the agent about JDK mid-session installs

Java has no env-var fallback, so the per-sandbox CA only lives in
the boot JDK's cacerts. Tell the agent to stick with the boot JDK
and not override javax.net.ssl.trustStore. PKIX path building
failed is the symptom if they do.

* Expand the "boot order" known limit to actually say what it means

The previous one-liner ("don't pick up the trust. Boot order is
enforced.") was too terse to be informative. Spell out: trust env
vars are read at startup only; agent processes are fine because
boot order puts env export before the agent runs; the residual
case is image-level daemons that come up during early init, which
we don't have today but would need to be ordered after env export.

* Drop boot-order known-limit; clarify per-protocol rewriters

- Removed the long-lived-process / boot-order bullet. The case it
  named (image-level daemons coming up before env export) doesn't
  exist in the current image and the bullet was just noise.
- Expanded "per-protocol rewriters, opt-in by domain" to actually
  describe what it means: a Postgres-wire-aware rewriter for
  Postgres-over-TLS auth, MySQL for MySQL, etc., each tagged onto
  a secret/domain via a protocol field so dsbx doesn't blindly
  reinterpret arbitrary non-HTTP frames. Phase 4+ (was Phase 3+,
  stale now that Phase 3 is body + WS frames).

* Drop the 'feature' framing on encoded placeholders

The doc was implying an automated smoke matrix runner exists per
dsbx release, which it doesn't. Removed the Verification section
and the surrounding "verified by the smoke matrix" framing.
Kept the list of expected-to-work clients and the known holes
since those are real design facts, not test claims.

not in this design doc.

The doc will outlive any single PR and is meant to be the

[sandbox] don't let dsbx inherit SSL_CERT_FILE pointing at the unbuilt bundle (#25204)

When the MITM experiment is enabled, buildSandboxEnvVars sets sandbox-wide
SSL_CERT_FILE / CURL_CA_BUNDLE to /etc/dust/ca-bundle.pem. That file is
created by installMitmTrustBundle, which only runs after the forwarder is
healthy. dsbx inherits those env vars on startup, rustls-native-certs honors
SSL_CERT_FILE, fails to read the missing bundle, and the process exits before
binding 9990. Health check times out, "did not become healthy in time".

Strip both vars from dsbx's own env via `env -u`. Agent processes still see
them (they're set at the sandbox env layer), so the trust handoff for curl
and friends still works once the bundle is installed.

feat(sandbox): scaffold sandbox_tool_executions storage (#25162)

Adds the storage layer for sandbox-originated MCP tool executions (the
approval-flow PR will land on top). New `sandbox_tool_executions`
table plus a single `spawnChildSandboxToolExecution` instance method
on the parent `AgentMCPActionResource`.

The two-table split (`agent_mcp_actions` for regular agent reasoning
steps, `sandbox_tool_executions` for tool calls originating from
inside the sandbox bash tool) avoids the `agent_step_contents`
unique-index race when several sandbox tools fire in one bash command
— sandbox tool executions aren't agent reasoning steps and don't need
a step-content row.

Spawner is an instance method (not static) so it can fill the FKs
(`workspaceId`, `agentMessageId`, `agentMCPActionId`) from `this`,
exploiting the parent–child relationship instead of threading IDs at
call sites. Returns the new execution's sId. Read/update paths (and
their dedicated Resource) land with the approval-flow PR — no point
adding them here without consumers.

Nothing in production reads or writes the table until the approval
flow ships. Worst case, an empty unused table — safe to rollback.

Fix plugins after migration to Zod (#25268)

The io-ts → zod migration in #25236 silently broke every resource-targeted poke plugin (Run Reinforcement, and others) — they all failed with their "resource not found" error.

Root cause: `RunPluginParamsSchema` was a `z.union` with the simpler 2-field schema listed first. zod's `z.union` returns the first variant that parses, and `z.object` strips unknown keys by default. So a request carrying `{ pluginId, resourceType, resourceId, workspaceId }` matched the simpler variant, came back without `resourceId`/`workspaceId`, and the handler then skipped both `fetchPluginResource(...)` and the workspace-scoped auth.

io-ts `t.type` retains extra keys, which is why the previous code worked.

Fix: collapse to a single `z.object` with optional `resourceId`/`workspaceId`, matching how downstream code already uses them.

Reinforcement: support agentFacingDescription edits in skill suggestions (#25253)

Reinforcement currently lets the analysis/aggregation flow suggest changes to a skill's instructions and tools, but not its agentFacingDescription. The description is what the agent reads to decide when to enable the skill, so a stale or misleading one shows up in conversations as routing mistakes (skill enabled in the wrong context, or not enabled when it should have been). This PR lets reinforcement suggest fixes to it.

### Schema & persistence

- Added agentFacingDescriptionEdit (single object with content) to SkillEditSuggestionSchema. The refine now accepts a suggestion that carries only a description edit. The field is also threaded through both edit_skill tool schemas (parser in lib/reinforcement/types.ts and the JSON schema sent to the LLM in run_reinforced_analysis.ts) and through createSuggestionForSkill.
- skill_suggestion_pruning.ts: a new pending suggestion that touches the description marks any older pending one that also touches the description as outdated (same idea as the existing tool/instruction conflict logic).

### Prompts

- analyze_conversation.ts: new agent_facing_description_guidance section, plus a step in the analysis workflow telling the model to consider description edits when the conversation reveals a routing mistake.
- aggregate_suggestions.ts: removed the previous prohibition (you MUST NOT use edit_skill to change it), added an aggregation rule (max 1 description-edit suggestion per skill), and extended formatSuggestion so the aggregator can see prior description-edit drafts.

### UI

- SkillSuggestionCard: new AgentFacingDescriptionEditSection rendered above the tool/instruction sections (they're typically standalone). Shows the current description with a strikethrough above the proposed text inside a DiffBlock for visual consistency with instruction diffs.
- SkillBuilderSuggestionsPanel: passes getCurrentAgentFacingDescription to the card and applies the new content to the form's agentFacingDescription field on accept.
- Poke details page + endpoint: returns skillAgentFacingDescription so the poke preview renders the same diff.

add support for agentFacingDescription edits in skill eval tests (#25289)

Follow-up to the agentFacingDescription support PR — adds end-to-end eval coverage for description edits in tests/reinforcement-evals.

Framework changes

- New editSkillWithAgentFacingDescription(skillId, sourceSuggestionIds?) assertion. It scans all edit_skill calls (not just the first) since description edits typically land in their own call alongside other edit_skill calls.
- noSuggestion now also fails if a stray agentFacingDescriptionEdit slipped through — previously it only checked instruction/tool edits, so a model returning only a description edit would have been silently accepted.

New scenarios

- Analysis: misleading-agent-facing-description — "Payment Issue Resolver" skill with a deliberately vague description ("Helps customers with payment issues"). The conversation shows the agent enabling it for a billing-address change, which the user calls out as wrong routing. Instructions and tools are correct — only the description should change. Judge top-scores when the new description (a) narrows scope to failures + chargebacks and (b) explicitly steers the agent away from billing/invoice/account-management requests; scores 0
  if the description edit is bundled with instruction/tool edits (per the standalone-call guidance).
- Aggregation: merge-description-edits-keep-tool-separate — three drafts on the same skill: two description edits (different routing-fix angles) plus one unrelated tool addition. Aggregator must produce exactly two edit_skill calls — one merging the description drafts (with both sourceSuggestionIds), one for the JIRA tool addition. Scores 0 if they get bundled into a single call.

definition, and tests.

fix(sbx): don't remount GCS FUSE on wake (#25340)

* fix(sbx): make GCS FUSE mount idempotent

ensureSandboxReady now calls a single helper that probes the mount and
token server, refreshes the token in place when both are alive, and
otherwise rebuilds local state and remounts. The freshlyCreated /
wokeFromSleep branching for the mount step is gone (egress still gets
the freshlyCreated branch).

Hot path is one sandbox exec (probe + token refresh, same round-trip
count as the old refresh-only path). Cold path is two execs: agent-side
setup script (kill stale token server, write token, restart server,
verify with a 5x250ms poll) and one root-side script (lazy-unmount any
stale mount, run gcsfuse). Down from four execs in the old fresh-create
path.

Removes the dependency on E2B preserving or wiping the mount across
pause/resume — the probe is the source of truth either way.

* tighten token-server poll: 10 x 100ms instead of 5 x 250ms

* fix two real bugs found via e2e test against e2b

1. pkill -f token-server.sh in the cold-path setup script matched the
   running shell's own argv (which carries the entire script source),
   killing the very shell trying to restart the server. Switch to
   fuser -k 9876/tcp so we target the listener by port.

2. The hot-path probe's curl was a single shot. token-server.sh is a
   while-true loop around 'nc -l -p 9876 -q 1' which lingers ~1s after
   each request, so right after gcsfuse fetches a token there is a
   short window with no listener bound. A single curl flakes ~30% of
   the time. Retry up to 5x100ms before declaring NEEDS_MOUNT, so we
   do not false-negative into an unnecessary remount on every tool
   call right after the previous one.

Verified end-to-end against a real e2b sandbox: fresh -> NEEDS_MOUNT,
mount, READY on hot probe (4x in a row), and on betaPause + connect
the mount and token server are preserved -> probe returns READY,
no remount.

* simplify: drop the idempotent probe, just don't remount on wake

Verified empirically against a real e2b sandbox: betaPause + connect
preserves both the FUSE mount and the token server. So on wake we just
need a fresh GCS access token in /tmp/token.json — the running token
server hands it to gcsfuse on the next request.

The fix is therefore a one-line change vs the original PR #25339:
drop the || wokeFromSleep from the freshlyCreated branch. Self-healing
when gcsfuse dies mid-life is out of scope (rare, and the reaper picks
those up anyway).

* Skip tables_query for delimited files in sandbox workspaces

For workspaces with both `sandbox_tools` and `new_file_explorer`, delimited
files (CSV, TSV, XLSX, XLS) uploaded in the conversation input bar now skip
all upload-time processing (Tika, snippet, table upsert) and land in GCS as
raw blobs. The model is steered to analyze them with code via the sandbox
mount under /files/conversation. Per-file size cap raised from 50 MB to 350
MB for these files.

New `useCaseMetadata.skipFileProcessing` bit (orthogonal to the existing
`skipDataSourceIndexing`) is the durable record of "this file was meant to
be sandbox-only". Bit is stamped at upload time only when both flags are on
and the content is delimited; pre-existing files keep their queryable
behavior.

All callers already filter upfront and the predicate can never be true here.

* Drop new_file_explorer FF gating

The flag was ungated in #25327. Treat it as always-on: remove the
hasNewFileExplorer plumbing from the file uploader, size resolver, and
sandbox raw delimited stamp; delete the FF declaration.

* Rename mountRelativePath to path on file content fragments

Shorter, easier to read at call sites. Helper renamed to
getConversationFilePath for consistency.

* Extract buildEffectiveUseCaseMetadata to upload_metadata.ts

It composes upload-time metadata for all files, not just sandbox ones,
so it doesn't belong in sandbox_raw.ts. Sandbox predicates stay there.

* [front,sandbox] phase 1 slice 3: swap https secrets at the egress hop

Wires up the actual secret-swap mechanism so HTTPS-secret env vars never reach
agent-visible plaintext. dsbx now persists its MITM CA across restarts and reads
a per-sandbox /run/dust/egress-secrets.json (mode 0600 root) that front writes

- New ExecOptions.stdin channel; e2b provider routes it through sendStdin /
  closeStdin with a fixed per-RPC timeout, kills the handle on send failure
  to avoid orphaned background commands.
- buildEgressSecretFileEntries + writeEgressSecretsFile build and atomically
  install the secrets JSON via install -m 600 /dev/stdin && mv.
- buildSandboxEnvVars injects DSEC_* placeholders alongside config DST_* vars.
- On wake from sleep, force a secrets-file rewrite + dsbx restart (pkill TERM,
  short grace, then KILL) instead of trusting the health probe.
- shellEscape and renderEgressSecretPlaceholder hoisted to shared modules.

dsbx:
- MITM CA path moved to /run/dust/egress-ca.pem with key at egress-ca.key
  (root 0600, atomic create_new + rename).
- New load_or_generate path reuses the persisted CA on dsbx restart, fails
  closed on partial / corrupt state.
- --mitm-ca-path kept as a hidden ignored arg so older front deployments
  shipping the flag during rollout don't break.
- dsbx 0.1.6, base image 0.8.5.

* [front,sandbox] rip phase-0 experiment scaffolding

The single-host hardcoded MITM swap (PHASE0) is no longer needed now that
phase 1 has the per-secret placeholder + secrets file foundation in place.
The actual per-secret allowed-domain swap lands in the next slice; this
just clears the dead path so it doesn't have to be deleted then.

dsbx:
- Drop --mitm-experiment-host arg, the runtime field, and the host gate.
- Delete http_rewriter.rs (the __DUST_EXPERIMENT_PLACEHOLDER__ rewriter)
  along with run_mitm_session, rewrite_request_then_copy, and the
  header-prefix helpers that fed it.
- handle_connection now always bidi-copies; no MITM stage runs.
- Keep MitmCa::load_or_generate so /run/dust/egress-ca.pem exists and the
  trust bundle install on front stays meaningful for the next slice.
  server_config_for is held with allow(dead_code) until then.

Front:
- Drop getEgressMitmExperimentHost / Token from config.
- Delete pages/api/v1/w/[wId]/sandbox/egress-experiment.{ts,test.ts}.
- Stop passing --mitm-experiment-host to dsbx.
- DUST_EXPERIMENT_TOKEN env var is gone; SSL_CERT_FILE / CURL_CA_BUNDLE
  are now set unconditionally (the trust bundle install is also always-on).
- Tests updated: experiment-host conditional cases collapsed into a
  single guard that asserts the flag is never passed.

* [front,sandbox] split egress health probe + drop stale assumptions

Health check now reports portOk and bundleOk separately. If dsbx is
running but installMitmTrustBundle never finished (transient fault on
first setup), the next exec sees the missing bundle and reinstalls it
idempotently without bouncing the forwarder. Previously the port-only
probe masked the half-configured state and SSL_CERT_FILE pointed at a
file that did not exist.

Also drops the SIGTERM grace from the dsbx restart (restarts only run
when no client is using the forwarder), the unverified "/run is tmpfs,
sleep+wake clears it" claim from comments, and the rollout-history
phase-0 references.

* [front,sandbox] seed /etc/dust/ca-bundle.pem in the sandbox image

Inject the system root bundle into /etc/dust/ca-bundle.pem at image
build time so the SSL_CERT_FILE / CURL_CA_BUNDLE env vars (set
unconditionally on the sandbox process) point at a valid file from the
moment the sandbox boots.

Closes two windows that the previous "create the file at egress setup
time" approach left open: fluent-bit boots before ensureSandboxReady
runs egress setup, and dev-unrestricted mode skips the install
entirely. installMitmTrustBundle still atomically replaces the bundle
with (system roots + dsbx CA) once the forwarder is up; in
dev-unrestricted the placeholder remains as the system-only copy.

* [sandbox] verify CA cert/key SPKI match on load

load() previously trusted whatever cert and key files happened to be on
disk. The current write path never overwrites an existing pair, so a
cert-from-A + key-from-B state isn't reachable through dsbx itself.
But the invariant was implicit, load-bearing on the absence of an
overwrite path. A future re-key path or external tampering could
silently introduce the inconsistency: leaves we sign would validate
against the in-memory key's public key, while front installs the
on-disk cert in the trust bundle, so clients would reject every forged
leaf.

Compares the cert's SubjectPublicKeyInfo against the key pair's public
key on every load and bails on mismatch. New unit test crosses cert
from one generated CA with the key from another and asserts the load
fails closed.

* Tighten egress trust-bundle health and drop dead MITM scaffolding

Health probe now checks a /etc/dust/.ca-bundle.merged sentinel alongside
the bundle file, so the image-seeded system-only ca-bundle.pem placeholder
no longer makes bundleOk=true before installMitmTrustBundle ever runs.
The install also fails loudly when the dsbx CA is missing instead of
silently succeeding with system-only trust.

Drop the leaf-cache + server_config_for path on dsbx that was wired up but
unreachable in slice 3. The slice that adds TLS termination will reintroduce
both, with the LRU bound the TODO already calls out.

Drop the redundant chmod 0755 on /run/dust from writeEgressSecretsFile so
front does not silently undo any directory hardening dsbx may apply.

[front] Stamp PLAN_CODE on every Metronome contract at creation (#25459)

Threads an optional planCode through createMetronomeContract and its three
wrappers (provisionMetronomeContract, switchMetronomeContractPackage,
provisionShadowEnterpriseMetronomeContract), and through their call sites
(Pro checkout, Stripe webhook shadow path, Business switch, shadow Enterprise
upgrade, Poke Enterprise upgrade). When provided, createMetronomeContract
now sets PLAN_CODE_CUSTOM_FIELD_KEY on the contract internally, so every
new contract carries the target plan code without a separate call.

Previously, if Metronome contract creation succeeded but the subsequent
PLAN_CODE stamp failed, the contract was left orphaned without its plan
code and the 409 conflict-recovery branch on retry returned the existing
id without re-stamping. The contract.start webhook would then have nothing
to dispatch on.

Restructures createMetronomeContract so once we hold a contract id (from
fresh create or 409 recovery), the post-create steps (Stripe billing,
PLAN_CODE stamp) always run. setMetronomeContractCustomFields and
addStripeMetronomeBillingConfig are both idempotent on Metronome's side,
so re-running them on retry is safe.

Extends recovery to packageId callers via a new
findMetronomeContractByUniquenessKey helper (mirrors the existing
findMetronomeCommitByUniquenessKey pattern).

Adds uniqueness keys to the two callers that lacked them:
- switchMetronomeContractPackage: switch:<oldContractId> — one switch
  per old contract.
- upgrade_enterprise.ts: composite of customer + package + plan code +
  start date — retries of the same Poke call dedup, different upgrades

[front] Swap Business contracts at the current hour, not the next (#25464)

switchMetronomeContractPackage previously hardcoded the swap point to the
next hour boundary (ceilToHourISO), borrowed from the Enterprise flow
where future scheduling is intentional. Used from upgradeToBusinessPlan
this produced a window of up to ~1h where the DB pointed at the new
Business plan but the Metronome contract hadn't started yet.

Add a swapAt: "current-hour" | "next-hour" parameter. Business passes
"current-hour": Pro/Business are seat-based, so there's no usage in the
current partial hour to attribute to the old contract, and we can swap
retroactively at the current hour boundary. The sync DB flip in
upgradeToBusinessPlan is now consistent with Metronome's view.

Replace the isEntreprisePlanPrefix carve-out in the contract.start handler
with a check on the workspace's active subscription: only swap when the
sub is Metronome-only billed.

The old gate was a conservative safety belt from when Enterprise was the
only path going through here. With PLAN_CODE now stamped on every
contract, the right gate is "is this workspace's billing source of truth
Metronome?" — which:

- Correctly excludes shadow-billed (Stripe + Metronome): Stripe drives
  state transitions, not contract.start. The old gate happily swapped
  shadow-billed Enterprise — a latent bug.
- Excludes pure Stripe naturally (no Metronome contract id, so the
  subscription has nothing to compare against).

The test that asserted "non-enterprise PLAN_CODE → skip" no longer maps
to behavior we want; replace it with one that exercises the new gate
directly (shadow-billed → skip).
