Introduce Hono router alongside Next.js (strangler) (#25136)

Starts a strangler-style migration from Next.js API routes onto Hono, with a custom Node server (front/server.ts) that dispatches requests to either Hono or Next based on an explicit allow-list in front-api/app.ts. Anything not listed falls through to the existing Next handler, so this PR is opt-in and reversible per route. **At this point, it is only meant for local testing, and does not affect production at all.**

Two routes are served by Hono in this PR, as a proof of concept:

- GET /api/healthz — direct port of the existing healthcheck (with statsd timing).
- GET /api/w/:wId/spaces and POST /api/w/:wId/spaces — ported from the Pages Router handler, going through the existing lib/api/spaces business layer and SpaceResource.

Notable pieces:

- front-api/middleware/workspace_auth.ts — mirrors withSessionAuthenticationForWorkspace: tries bearer token first, falls back to the WorkOS session cookie, builds an Authenticator, sets client IP, and stashes it on the Hono context. Refreshed Set-Cookie headers from the session helper are forwarded back to the response.
- front-api/middleware/cors.ts — re-implements the Next.js Edge CORS middleware so Hono-served requests get the same headers (allowed-origin check, preflight handling, X-Reload-Required exposed).
- front-api/middleware/validator.ts — thin wrapper around @hono/zod-validator that emits errors in our standard { error: { type, message } } shape using zod-validation-error.
- The OPTIONS method is auto-added to every Hono-listed route so CORS preflights stay inside the Hono CORS middleware rather than bouncing through Next.
- tools/mprocs.yaml adds a front-hono proc (autostart off) running npm run dev:hono, plus a launch config in front/.vscode/launch.json.

[front] Poke: add unified switch_contract endpoint for Metronome-billed subs (#25485)

Adds a new Poke endpoint that handles plan transitions for Metronome-billed
workspaces under a single package-first flow. Operator picks a Metronome
package; the endpoint classifies it (pro / business / enterprise), validates
the target plan code matches that tier, and dispatches:

- Pro / Business: switchMetronomeContractPackage with swapAt: "current-hour"
  + sync DB flip via swapMetronomeContract on the active subscription.
- Enterprise: future-scheduled contract (≥1h out), PLAN_CODE stamped, no DB
  flip — the contract.start webhook handles the transition.

Mechanisms:

- classifyMetronomePackage in lib/metronome/types.ts uses an exhaustive switch
  (with assertNever) over KnownPackageAlias, returns null for any unknown
  alias. listMetronomePackages now exposes tier on each summary so the form
  can derive its compatible plan list.
- validatePlanPackageCompat rejects mismatched plan ↔ package combos (e.g.
  PRO_PLAN_SEAT_29 with an enterprise package, free plans entirely).
- The legacy upgrade_enterprise endpoint is unchanged — it continues to
  serve Stripe-billed Enterprise upgrades via the existing drawer dialog.

Tests: 11 new tests covering enterprise / pro / business success paths,
plan-package compat rejection, free-plan rejection, Stripe-billed
rejection, missing-contract rejection, and unknown-alias rejection.

Replaces the legacy "🔥 Upgrade / Downgrade" drawer with a focused
"🔁 Switch contract" dialog when the workspace is Metronome-only billed.
Stripe-billed workspaces continue to see the legacy drawer.

UX is package-first:

- Operator picks a Metronome package from the existing list (filtered to
  packages with a classifiable tier).
- Based on the package's tier, the form derives:
  - Pro package  → planCode = PRO_PLAN_SEAT_29, no startingAt input
  - Business pkg → planCode = PRO_PLAN_SEAT_39, no startingAt input
  - Enterprise   → planCode picker over all ENT_* plans + startingAt
                   (datetime-local, ≥1h future, on the hour)
- PAYG guard disables the button when PAYG is enabled (matches the existing
  drawer's behavior).

Submit hits /api/poke/workspaces/[wId]/switch_contract; on success the
page reloads to reflect the new state (sync for Pro/Business, scheduled
for Enterprise via the contract.start webhook).

[docs] drop DSBX_DISABLE_MITM kill switch from phase 1 design (#25496)

The kill switch was meant as an incident-rollback primitive, but the
env var is read at dsbx startup so a GCP-secret flip only affects
newly spawned sandboxes. Covering active sandboxes required a
separate pkill-via-root-exec oncall script, which adds enough moving
parts that the rollback path stops being self-contained.

Dropping it from the plan. If we end up needing this later, it goes

Add support for csv files in UTF-16 with BOM (#25510)

CSV/TSV files exported as UTF-16 (e.g. some Excel "Save As CSV" variants) fail to upload to a conversation with:

```
CSV parse error: record 0 (line 1, field: 1, byte: 0): invalid utf-8: invalid UTF-8 in field 1 near byte index 0
```

csv_async only accepts UTF-8, and byte 0 of such files is the 0xFF of the UTF-16 LE BOM.

This PR transcodes the downloaded content to UTF-8 when a UTF-16 BOM is detected (LE FF FE or BE FE FF), stripping the BOM. The fix lives in GoogleCloudStorageCSVContent::parse, so it covers both validate_csv_content (snippet generation) and the actual table upsert path.

UTF-8 files (with or without a BOM) and other encodings without a BOM are unchanged.

* home(hero): tighten chat-card animations against Emil Kowalski's guide

Reviewed the message component against animations.dev principles. Issues
were: scale-from-zero pops, mismatched entrance/exit easings, an oversized
overshoot on reaction pills, layout-triggering left/top animation on the
fly emoji, and no prefers-reduced-motion support.

Card entrance / exit
- scale(0.2) → scale(0.96) (entrance) and scale(1) → scale(0.96) (exit) so
  the card settles instead of popping in/out from nothing.
- 420 ms entrance / 280 ms exit → 220 ms / 180 ms. Exit is now ~20% faster
  than entrance per Emil's rule.
- Both share cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1) (ease-out-quart). Paired
  motion now reads as one unit instead of two different curves.

Reaction pill
- 360 ms / cubic-bezier(.2,1.4,.3,1) / scale(0.2 → 1.15 → 1) was a strong
  pop with a 15% overshoot.
- 220 ms / cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.4, 0.64, 1) / scale(0.85 → 1.04 → 1) keeps
  a hint of spring without the cartoon bounce.
- Added will-change: transform during the pop.

Fly emoji (reactions arc)
- Was animating left/top (triggers layout) with will-change including them.
- Now drives the path entirely via transform: translate(...) deltas;
  static left/top set once on creation. will-change tightened to
  transform, opacity. Trims duration 850 ms → 700 ms; scale curve relaxed
  to 0.6 → 1.1 → 1.05 → 0.8.

Reduced motion
- New @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block in heroOfficeStyles.ts
  zeros every decorative animation/transition (human bob, agent pulse /
  halo, status pulse, activity emoji, door light, caret, both reaction
  pills, fly emoji).
- showChatCard, the exit fade, and flyReaction also check

[metronome] Add credit state machines for Enterprise Pooled contracts (#25686)

Introduce two orthogonal credit state machines that gate user spend for
Enterprise Pooled workspaces. Per-user and workspace-level state are
tracked independently; a user is allowed to spend iff
`membership.creditState = 'normal'` AND
`workspace.poolCreditState != 'depleted'`.

User state machine (per-user dimension)
- States: `normal | capped`, persisted on `memberships.creditState`,
  cached on `metronome:user_cap:<ws>:<user>`.
- Events:
  - `per_user_cap_reached`: admin-configured per-user spend cap hit, fired
    by per-user `alerts.spend_threshold_reached`. Transitions
    `normal -> capped` and sets the Redis cap key.
  - `per_user_cap_resolved`: spend dropped below the cap (billing-cycle
    renewal or cap raised mid-cycle). Transitions `capped -> normal` and
    clears the Redis cap key.
  - `admin_raised_user_cap`: admin manually raised this user's cap.
    Transitions `capped -> normal` and clears the Redis cap key.
- Only Enterprise Pooled memberships (`seatType = 'workspace'`) go through
  the state machine. Other plans fall back to direct Redis writes so the
  pre-existing block behaviour is preserved.

Workspace state machine (pool dimension)
- States: `active | overage | depleted`, persisted on
  `workspaces.poolCreditState`, cached on `metronome:pool_depleted:<ws>`.
- Events:
  - `pool_exhausted`: combined contract-credit + commit balance reached
    zero (canonical pool-exhaustion signal). Guard on `paygEnabled`:
    `active -> overage` if PAYG, `active -> depleted` otherwise. The
    PAYG flag is stubbed to `false` for now (TODO once contract location
    is settled).
  - `payg_cap_reached`: workspace-level PAYG cap hit, fired by
    workspace-level `alerts.spend_threshold_reached` (no `user_id` in
    `group_values`). Transitions `overage -> depleted`.
  - `credits_added`: pool was replenished (admin top-up or billing-cycle
    renewal). Transitions `overage|depleted -> active`; clears the Redis
    depleted key on the depleted path. Driven exclusively by the combined
    `_resolved` alert rather than `commit.segment.start`.

from ~70K to ~3.1K (-95%). get_document_structure and
get_presentation_structure are removed.

Each resolver translates anchors (text snippets, A1 notation, slide
numbers) into the underlying batchUpdate requests and exposes a raw
escape hatch for cases the lean schema does not cover. 32 unit tests
cover anchor resolution, ordering, A1 parsing, and the raw passthrough;
the MCP metadata snapshot is regenerated.

* [front] enh: Restore batching + preserve-formatting guidance on Google Drive write tools

The prior refactor stripped index-mechanics advice from the write tool
descriptions (correctly — the model no longer sees indices). But it also
dropped two pieces of guidance that are still relevant:

- Batch as many operations as possible in a single call to minimize
  API round-trips.
- Prefer the find/replace ops (replaceText, replaceAllText,
  replaceTextInShape) when you want to preserve the original
  formatting; delete + insert resets to default styling.

Adds these back to update_document, update_spreadsheet, and
update_presentation. Index/cell-boundary mechanics stay out — the
resolver handles them.

* [front] revert: Keep get_document_structure and get_presentation_structure

The prior commit removed these two read-only tools on the theory that
their only purpose was feeding indices/objectIds to the write tools.
That's now true for our write path (update_document and
update_presentation resolve anchors server-side), but some user-built
agents call these tools directly to inspect document/presentation
structure. Removing them is a breaking change for those agents.

This restores both tools with refreshed descriptions: they are kept as
inspection tools, and the descriptions explicitly note that calling
them is NOT required before update_document / update_presentation.
Token impact is small — both tools are ~150 tokens each in the spec.

Restores format_document.ts and format_presentation.ts (used only by
these handlers) and regenerates the MCP metadata snapshot.

* [front] fix: Drop Node 'crypto' import that breaks Vite bundling

Vite externalizes Node built-in modules when bundling, so the
'import { randomUUID } from "crypto"' added in the prior commit fails
at runtime. The rest of the codebase uses bare crypto.randomUUID()
(file_resource.ts, mcp_client_side.ts, academy.ts, frame_session.ts,
AgentBuilderTriggersBlock.tsx) — crypto is a global in both Node and
browsers via WebCrypto, so no import is needed.

Switches the addTextBox helper to match.

* [front] enh: Phase 2a — Google Docs structural ops (tables + headers/footers)

Adds 8 new structural operations to update_document, sitting alongside
the Phase 1 text-anchor operations:

Tables (addressed by 0-indexed tableIndex / rowIndex / columnIndex):
- replaceTableCell — replaces entire cell content (delete + insert at
  cellStart + 1, matching the existing format_document.ts convention)
- insertInTableCell — insert at cell start or end
- insertTableRow / insertTableColumn — add via tableCellLocation,
  afterRowIndex=-1 / afterColumnIndex=-1 inserts before the first row/col
- deleteTableRow / deleteTableColumn

Headers / footers (addressed by segment + role):
- replaceHeaderFooterText — emits document-wide replaceAllText
  (per PR #24668, replaceAllText matches inside headers/footers
  automatically; we still validate the segment exists for a clear error)
- insertInHeaderFooter — emits insertText with location.segmentId

Resolver moves to front/lib/api/actions/servers/google_drive/resolution/.
Adds 9 new tests covering cell resolution (with cellStart + 1 invariant),
out-of-range errors, row/column insertion direction, header insertion
with segmentId, and missing-role error path. 21 docs resolver tests pass.

* [front] enh: Phase 2b — Google Slides structural ops (shapes + notes + tables)

Adds 4 new structural operations to update_presentation, evolves
replaceAllText to support slide-scoping, and removes the now-redundant
replaceTextInShape (its only use case is covered by
replaceAllText({slideNumbers}) and replaceShapeText combined):

- replaceAllText now accepts optional slideNumbers: number[] (1-indexed)
  to scope find/replace; omit for document-wide
- replaceShapeText — replaces all text in a specific shape. The shape
  is identified by a discriminated union: { byText }, { byIndex }, or
  { byType: TITLE/SUBTITLE/BODY/TEXT_BOX }. byType reads
  shape.placeholder.type for placeholders and falls back to
  shape.shapeType for TEXT_BOX. Shape resolution walks into
  elementGroup.children recursively so grouped shapes are reachable
- insertInShape — inserts at start (insertionIndex=0) or end
  (insertionIndex=current text length)
- replaceSlideTableCell — addresses a table on a specific slide by
  0-indexed tableIndex, emits deleteText + insertText with cellLocation
- replaceNotes — targets slide.slideProperties.notesPage.notesProperties
  .speakerNotesObjectId

Removes replaceTextInShape (superseded). 21 slides resolver tests pass.

* [front] enh: Phase 2c — Google Sheets structural ops rewritten (sheetName + A1)

Reshapes update_spreadsheet to match the Phase 2 contract: every op
takes a human-readable sheetName plus an A1 range WITHOUT the sheet
prefix, and the server resolves sheetName → numeric sheetId from the
spreadsheet's metadata.

Op changes:
- updateCells: { sheetName, range, values } (was: single A1 string)
- formatCells: { sheetName, range, format: { bold, italic, fontSize,
  backgroundColor: {r,g,b}, textColor: {r,g,b}, horizontalAlignment,
  numberFormat: { type, pattern? } } } — replaces formatRange's flat
  hex-color shape with the same RGB structure the Sheets API uses
- mergeCells: { sheetName, range, mergeType } (was: single A1)
- sortRange: { sheetName, range, sortSpecs: [{columnIndex, ascending}] }
  — array of specs instead of one flat columnIndex/order
- findReplace: adds matchEntireCell; sheetTitle → sheetName
- insertRows / deleteRows / insertColumns / deleteColumns — replace the
  single insertDimension / deleteDimension with explicit row/column ops.
  insertRows/insertColumns take startIndex + count; deleteRows/Columns
  keep the startIndex/endIndex (exclusive) shape
- autoResizeColumns: takes sheetName + range explicitly

Kept from Phase 1: addSheet, deleteSheet, raw escape hatch.

Exports parseA1Range as a utility (now rejects ranges with a sheet
prefix to keep the contract clean). Sheet names with spaces or special
chars are quoted with single quotes when re-built for the values
batchUpdate API.

* [front] chore: DRY error-prefix wrapping + rename Sheets fontSize→fontSizePt

and applies it across all three resolvers. Replaces ~20 sites of the

  return new Err(new Error(`opName: ${result.error.message}`));

with:

  return prefixErr("opName", result.error);

* [front] fix: Strip redundant list markers when replacing bulleted/numbered table cells

When the agent calls replaceTableCell on a Docs cell whose paragraphs
already have bullet or numbered list styling, Google Docs reapplies
the cell's bullet to every paragraph we insert. If the model's content
included its own list markers ("• item", "1. First"), the result is
double-formatting:

  Cell has numbered list → "1. Walk us through" renders as
  "1. 1. Walk us through"

  Cell has bullet → "• Excellent writing" renders as
  "● • Excellent writing"

resolveTableCell now reports hasBulletStyle by checking whether any
paragraph in the cell has a non-null bullet property. When true, the
replaceTableCell handler runs the content through stripListMarkers,
which removes a leading bullet glyph (•, ‣, ◦, dashes, etc.) and/or a
numbered prefix ("1. ", "a) ") from each non-empty line. Numeric
content without a punctuation marker (e.g. "5 years of experience")
is preserved — the regex requires the period/paren to be followed by
whitespace. Lines that would become empty after stripping keep their
original content.

Scope: replaceTableCell only. insertInTableCell appends to existing
content where the agent may intentionally want markers; raw passthrough
is never modified.

Tool description gains one sentence noting the auto-strip behavior.

28 docs resolver tests pass (7 new). Full suite still 80 green.

* [front] fix: Drop blank lines from replaceTableCell content into bulleted cells

Phase-2c stripped redundant bullet/number markers from replaceTableCell
content but preserved whitespace-only lines as-is. In a list-styled
cell that produces empty list items between real items:

  Model sends: "1. content\n\n2. more content"
  After strip: "content\n\nmore content"
  Inserted:    cell renders as "1. content / 2. (blank) / 3. more content"

Whitespace-only lines are now dropped inside stripListMarkers (which
only runs when the cell has bullet styling), so blank-line separators
in the agent's output don't become blank list items. Empty lines in
non-list write paths (replaceText, insertText, raw) remain untouched.

29 docs resolver tests pass (1 new).

* [front] enh: expectedOccurrences on Docs edit ops + replaceTableCell edge fixes

Addresses the Flavify nits + the carryover OOC on edit ergonomics.

deleteText and formatText now take an optional `expectedOccurrences`
field (defaults to 1). The resolver counts all matches and errors if
the count differs, so the model can't silently edit the wrong location
when the anchor isn't unique. To delete/format every match the model
sets the field explicitly. Matches Anthropic's str_replace contract
and Flav 2.22's edit-tool guidance.

  deleteText({ text: "foo" }) on doc with 2 "foo"s
    → Err: Expected 1 occurrence(s) of "foo" but found 2. Set
      expectedOccurrences explicitly to delete multiple matches.

  deleteText({ text: "foo", expectedOccurrences: 2 })
    → 2 deleteContentRange requests, sorted highest-index-first

replaceTableCell hardening:
- stripListMarkers now requires ASCII hyphen/dash markers to be
  followed by whitespace, so "-Wallow" isn't truncated to "Wallow"
  (unicode bullets like • remain optional-whitespace since they're
  unambiguous).
- CRLF normalised at the top of stripListMarkers — agent output is
  usually LF but Windows copy/paste survives via tool input.
- If stripping reduces content to "" (e.g. the model sent only blank
  lines), the resolver now skips the insertText entirely instead of
  emitting an empty-text request that Google would reject.

update_document description widened to mention the blank-line drop
alongside the marker strip.

35 docs resolver tests pass (6 new: 3 expectedOccurrences cases,
empty-strip short-circuit, ASCII-hyphen edge, plus existing "first
match silently" test reframed as the new error path). Full suite
remains 87 green. Snapshot regenerated.

* [front] chore: Tighten Google Drive tool descriptions to match Dust house style

Two issues with the prior phrasing:

1. The three get_*_structure / get_worksheet descriptions ended with
   "Useful when you need to inspect ... Not required before calling
   update_*..." That framing is defensive filler — the model can read
   the update_* description if it wants to know about the read/write
   relationship, and "useful for inspection" is tautological for a
   read tool. Dropped both lines.

2. update_document / update_spreadsheet / update_presentation each
   rendered as a markdown bullet list enumerating every operation.
   That's out of pattern — every other write tool in the repo
   (copy_file, create_comment, create_reply, append_to_spreadsheet,
   and the Notion / Confluence / google_sheets equivalents) uses
   short prose. The per-operation JSON schema (via .describe() on
   each discriminated-union arm) already documents each op for the
   model. Replaced the bullet lists with terse two-three sentence
   descriptions that keep the load-bearing hints:

   - "no need to call get_* first" (the whole point of the refactor)
   - the `raw` escape hatch
   - the auto-strip behavior for bulleted cells (Docs)
   - the append_to_spreadsheet cross-reference (Sheets)
   - the {{placeholder}} hint (Slides templates)

Total tool spec ~10.5K → ~10.1K tokens. Modest side effect; the
primary goal is alignment with the repo's terse-prose pattern.

87 tests + metadata snapshot still green.

* [front] chore: Stop exposing server-internal mechanism in write-tool descriptions

Tool descriptions should tell the agent what it can do, not how the
server implements it. The agent doesn't know there's a server vs a
function call, and the "the server fetches / resolves / strips X
automatically" framing was leaking implementation details that
don't help the model make better decisions.

Specific edits:

- Removed "the server fetches the current state and resolves text
  anchors automatically" — reduced to the load-bearing assertion
  "No prior call to get_*_structure is needed." Same information,
  no mechanism leakage.

- Removed the bullet-strip / blank-line-drop mention from
  update_document. The transform makes the result match the agent's
  intent — it's only a surprise to inspect, and agents don't usually
  re-read the doc post-edit. If a regression shows up, we can add
  the hint back.

- Removed "skips sheet-name resolution" — gratuitous: the agent
  doesn't know what sheet-name resolution is.

What stayed (load-bearing):
- "No prior call ... is needed" — actively contradicts the model's
  prior training pattern (call-structure-first); without the hint we
  pay for redundant fetches.
- `raw` escape hatch — documents an op the model can choose.
- append_to_spreadsheet cross-reference — tool-selection guidance.
- `{{placeholder}}` hint — template idiom worth surfacing.

87 tests + snapshot still green.

[dsbx] scope MITM to allowlist union from secrets file (#25762)

* [dsbx] scope MITM to allowlist union from secrets file

Reintroduce the TLS-termination branch in dsbx: when SNI is in the
loaded allowlist union, terminate inbound TLS with a leaf signed by
the persistent CA, dial outbound through the proxy tunnel, and
bidi-copy decrypted bytes. Force http/1.1 ALPN on both sides so the
upcoming rewriter never sees h2. Leaf cert cache is LRU-bounded at
256 entries from the start. No header substitution yet.

Bumps dsbx 0.1.7 to 0.1.8 and dust-base 0.8.11 to 0.8.12.

* [dsbx] review: tighten MITM session plumbing

Apply review feedback:
- server_config_for now takes &self instead of &Arc<Self>, the Arc
  receiver was unused noise that propagated to callers.
- Drop the redundant default crypto provider install inside
  server_config_for, it's already wired at startup.
- mitm_target_for returns Option<&str> borrowed from the existing
  domain string, no per-connection allocation on the hot path.
- HTTP_1_1_ALPN const lives in tls_mitm and is imported by mod, no
  more duplicated constant.
- Treat UnexpectedEof on the bidi copy the same as BrokenPipe and
  ConnectionReset (peer dropped without close_notify).
- Bump lru 0.12 to 0.16 to drop the GHSA-rhfx-m35p-ff5j advisory
  noise from dep scans (we don't use IterMut so we were not affected
  at runtime, but it keeps showing up).

* [dsbx] review: restore rustls provider install + add splice path test

Restore the idempotent `rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider()
.install_default()` call inside `server_config_for`. Removing it was
a regression: focused runs like `cargo test server_config_for_forces_http1_alpn`
panic with "Could not automatically determine the process-level
CryptoProvider" because no other test installs the provider first.

Add `splice_session_preserves_upstream_chain` covering the SNI-miss
branch: empty allowlist union, agent trust store contains only the
upstream's real CA (not the dsbx CA). If the splice path ever silently
terminated and re-signed, the agent connect would fail.

* [dsbx] document outbound trust set threat-model assumption

After a wake, the trust-bundle installer has added dsbx's own CA to
/etc/ssl/certs, so the restarted dsbx loads it into its outbound
trust set. We accept this because forging a cert with that CA needs
the private key at /run/dust/egress-ca.key (mode 0600 root-owned),
and an attacker getting root in the sandbox is outside the threat
model. Comment in the connector builder so future readers do not
re-discover this and try to filter the CA out.

[dsbx] parse HTTP/1.1 requests with host/SNI invariants (#25829)

* [dsbx] parse HTTP/1.1 requests with host/SNI invariants

Replaces the pass-through stub in the MITM rewriter with a real
HTTP/1.1 parser that:
- parses request headers (bounded by MAX_HEADER_BLOCK_BYTES / MAX_HEADERS)
- enforces Host == SNI on TLS, single Host header, absolute URI authority
  matches Host
- frames request bodies (Content-Length and chunked) and forwards them
- falls back to raw splice when the first client bytes do not look like
  HTTP (so unknown protocols on 443 still work)
- splices the rest of the connection on WebSocket upgrade requests

No secret substitution or Basic auth rewriting yet (placeholders keep
flowing through verbatim, same as the current pass-through stub). Bumps
dsbx to 0.1.10 and dust-base to 0.8.14 so the new binary lands in the
image.

* [dsbx] review: add smuggling tests, bound trailers, checked chunk arithmetic

- request-smuggling regression tests: CL+TE conflict, duplicate Content-Length,
  TE list with non-chunked tokens
- cap chunked trailer block at MAX_TRAILER_BLOCK_BYTES (32 KiB) so a sender
  cannot stream unbounded trailer lines after the terminating chunk
- checked_add on chunk_size + 2 to deny rather than overflow on a malformed
  chunk header
- add PlainHttp happy-path + non-default-Host-port integration tests
- drop default_host_port() (identical to port())
- fmt fixes for CI

* [dsbx] clarify why unused deny variants ship in this build

* [dsbx] relax rewriter limits for LLM/SaaS header sizes

* [dsbx] reword rewriter limit comment to not assume API traffic

* [dsbx] deny CONNECT requests inside the rewritten session

The upstream TCP destination is pinned by the SNI gate before HTTP
parsing runs, so a CONNECT request-target cannot redirect the tunnel.
Forwarding CONNECT to a non-proxying upstream is harmless today (the
server just returns 405) but is nonsense inside an already-established
session and is the kind of thing future refactors might accidentally
start honoring. Reject up front with a named deny reason.

* [dsbx] document why non-HTTP fallback is not a policy bypass

* [dsbx] substitute secret placeholders in MITM'd HTTP requests

Wire the request rewriter to replace `__DSEC_<32hex>__` placeholders with
real secret values when forwarding on an allowlisted MITM'd TLS session.

  the URL is logged and indexed in too many places to be safe.

  contain control bytes.

- Bump dsbx to 0.1.11 and the dust-base image to 0.8.15.

the placeholder.

  per-request check (and its now-unused `ValueControlChar` deny reason).

[dsbx] coordinate WebSocket upgrades between rewriter request and response tasks (#25872)

* [dsbx] coordinate WebSocket upgrades between request and response tasks

The rewriter splices raw bytes after a WebSocket upgrade request only when
upstream actually returned 101 Switching Protocols. The request task sends a
oneshot watch through the existing channel before forwarding any upgrade
bytes, the response task sniffs the next status line and signals back, and
the request task either raw-splices (101) or tears the upstream write half
down (anything else) so client frames never reach an upstream that didn't
accept the upgrade.

Bumps dsbx 0.1.11 -> 0.1.12 and dust-base 0.8.15 -> 0.8.16.

* [dsbx] review: clarify upgrade verdict states and tidy WS tests

Replace the two-step Option pattern in the upgrade branch with an explicit
UpgradeVerdict enum (NotAnUpgrade, AwaitingResponse, ResponseTaskGone,
NoWatchWired) so each path is named rather than recovered by re-inspecting
the watch sender. Document why is_switching_protocols_response treats an
unexpected 100 Continue interim response as rejected. Drop the magic 12 in
the WebSocket integration test, propagate the upstream TLS shutdown error
instead of swallowing it, and replace a unicode arrow in a comment with
ASCII.

* [dsbx] make the WebSocket upgrade watch channel required

Drop the Option around websocket_watch_tx and the dead NoWatchWired
verdict. Production callers always wire the channel; the test helper
now spawns a small auto-accept task on the channel so the existing
splice-after-upgrade test keeps exercising the raw-splice path.

(tsx wraps the JSON require in \`{ default }\`).

Routes migrated:

  workspaces sub-app (which already mounts the [wId] children)

Supporting changes:
- \`listWorkspacesForPoke\` extracted to \`lib/api/poke/workspaces.ts\`
  with the search-by-{sId, Stripe sub, email, domain, phone} branching
  and plan-priority sort. Returns \`PokeWorkspaceType[]\` for both

- \`lib/poke/search.ts\` wraps the \`tryParsePhoneNumber\` call in
  try/catch to degrade gracefully — phone-number search becomes a
  no-op under the dev-time CJS/ESM issue while the other search axes
  keep working. Same workaround in the workspaces lib's phone-axis
  branch.

Per-handler patterns match the post-#25899 codebase:
- Hono handlers use \`HandlerResult<T>\` with explicit response types
- Errors go through \`apiError(ctx, ...)\`
- \`ctx\` (not \`c\`) as the Context parameter name
- Import ordering enforced by biome

Note on libphonenumber: this is a temporary mitigation. The proper fix
is to migrate front-api to ESM (\`"type": "module"\` + \`format: "esm"\`
in esbuild) so tsx loads CJS deps correctly; that's a separate PR.

* Bundle ESM-only packages so front-api production builds work

Replace \`packages: "external"\` in the front-api esbuild config with a
custom plugin that externalizes every node_modules import by default,
except for an explicit \`ESM_ONLY_PACKAGES\` allowlist that esbuild
bundles inline.

\`packages: "external"\` left Node 22 to \`require()\` ESM-only packages at
runtime, which it does by wrapping the default export in
\`{ default: ... }\`. That breaks libphonenumber-js's internal CJS code
(\`var metadata = require('./metadata.min.json')\` ends up with
\`metadata.countries\` undefined) and any other ESM-only package that
gets pulled in via \`@app/*\` re-exports.

Bundling those packages inline at build time sidesteps the require()
interop entirely. \`libphonenumber-js\` is the first entry on the
allowlist; new entries can be added as we discover them.

The dev runtime (tsx) still hits the same issue because tsx doesn't
bundle — it loads source via Node's module loader on the fly. The
existing \`tryParsePhoneNumber\` try/catch in \`lib/poke/search.ts\` and
\`lib/api/poke/workspaces.ts\` stays in place to keep dev usable; the
inline comments are updated to clarify the mitigation is now dev-only.
Full ESM output for front-api (\`format: "esm"\` + \`"type": "module"\`)
is deferred until Next.js is retired from the strangler setup.

Side note: the plugin's externalize-by-default filter also catches our
\`@app/\` and \`@front-api/\` path aliases, which we want bundled (they
point at source code, not node_modules). Skip them explicitly so
esbuild's alias resolution applies and the resolved paths get bundled
normally.

Close UDP/53 DNS exfil hole for the agent UID (#25991)

* Close the UDP/53 DNS exfil hole for the agent UID

Agent code in the sandbox could exfiltrate via DNS by querying 8.8.8.8
directly (E2B auto-allows it whenever any domain entry is in the
sandbox policy). The TCP-only egress proxy enforcement never covered
this path.

Per-UID nftables now REDIRECTs all uid 1003 UDP/TCP port-53 traffic to
a local synthetic resolver (dsbx resolve, bound on 127.0.0.1:1053,
unprivileged). The stub returns a sentinel A record for any name,
NODATA for every other qtype, FORMERR on malformed input. Drops the
old resolv.conf-reading loop so the boundary no longer depends on a
mutable file. Root keeps provider DNS untouched.

Adds dsbx healthcheck reporting forwarder/resolver/nftables state and
wires it into the existing create/wake/exec egress check so the
sandbox fails closed if DNS enforcement is missing. Design notes in
design_docs/DNS_EXFIL_FIX.md.

* Apply review feedback on the sandbox DNS exfil fix

Replaces the hand-rolled type guard around dsbx healthcheck output with
a zod schema (per GEN13) and stops swallowing healthcheck stderr or
non-zero exits, so a missing or stale dsbx binary surfaces in logs
instead of degrading silently to "all signals false".

Other corrections from the review:
- Resolver writes a const u16 rdata length instead of unwrap_or_default
  on an infallible conversion (no more "fall back to zero-length
  rdata" bug if SENTINEL_A_RECORD ever changes shape).
- cmd_resolve aborts the sibling transport task on shutdown so
  Restart=on-failure actually kicks in promptly.
- Tighten the filter_output DNS accept rule from 127.0.0.0/8 to
  127.0.0.1 (the only address the REDIRECT ever targets).
- Adds a SANDBOX_AGENT_PROXIED_UID constant so the relationship with
  SANDBOX_UNTRUSTED_UIDS is explicit instead of an [0] tuple-of-one
  indirection.
- nft_ipv4_ruleset logs the actual failure reason (missing binary,
  non-zero exit, non-UTF8) instead of silently None.
- dsbx healthcheck drops the proxied_uid default; front always passes
  it explicitly so the dead default would just rot.
- Resolver systemd unit gains the standard hardening menu
  (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, RestrictAddressFamilies=
  AF_INET, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, ...) since this is a process that
  exists to parse attacker-shaped input.

Plus design doc and comment polish: the exec-time healthcheck is now
documented as intentional detection on top of the boot-time enforcement
invariant, sentinel-with-no-SNI behavior is pinned in the behavior
table, and parse_qname has notes on why we reject extended labels and
accept lossy UTF-8.

* Drop design doc from the PR

* Run dsbx healthcheck as root and validate the full nftables boundary

The healthcheck exec was inheriting the sandbox default user (agent), so
`nft list table` would fail with EPERM and every nft_*_ok signal returned
false even when the rules were installed correctly. Pass `user: "root"`
explicitly and pin the exec options in the test so this cannot silently
regress.

Extend the runtime check to also validate the broad TCP redirect to
:9990, the generic UDP and ICMP drops, and the IPv6 uid drop. The design
invariant is wider than DNS: a partially damaged table with the DNS
redirects still present but the no-UDP / no-IPv6 rules missing would
have passed the previous healthcheck while reopening non-53 UDP.

* Decouple agent-proxied UID from untrusted-UID coverage list and surface healthcheck stderr

Use SANDBOX_AGENT_PROXIED_UID directly for the useradd step instead of
indexing into SANDBOX_UNTRUSTED_UIDS. The list is the canonical coverage
set for the nftables ruleset; the named export is the identity of the
agent-proxied user. Reordering the coverage list must not silently
change which UID gets assigned to that user.

When dsbx healthcheck exits zero but reports nft_*_ok: false, the
underlying cause (nft missing, EPERM, non-UTF8 output) was being logged
inside dsbx and then dropped, because front only forwarded stderr on
non-zero exits. Surface it on the unhealthy-but-exit-zero path too so
prod failures stay actionable.

* Apply biome formatter to egress tests

* Bump sentinel A record TTL to 24h

The answer never changes for the lifetime of a sandbox: it is a fixed
RFC 6890 sentinel that will never resolve to anything useful. A 60s
TTL just caused clients to re-query the stub for the same answer.
Behavioral changes ship via image rebuilds and sandbox recreation,
so TTL-driven invalidation buys nothing.

Fix sandbox egress healthcheck nft fragment matching (#26047)

* Fix sandbox egress healthcheck nft fragment matching

The 0.1.15 dsbx binary looks for `meta l4proto udp drop` and `meta
l4proto icmp drop` in the live nft ruleset, but `nft list` normalizes
those to `meta l4proto 17 drop` and `meta l4proto 1 drop`. Every healthy
0.8.19 sandbox therefore reports `nft_udp_drop_ok: false` and
`nft_icmp_drop_ok: false`, which the strict aggregate turns into a
"DNS enforcement health check failed" rejection on every sandbox tool
call.

Two-part fix:
- dsbx healthcheck now accepts both numeric and named l4proto forms.
- Front masks those two signals out of the nftablesOk aggregate. The
  rules themselves are installed by egress-nftables.sh under `set -eu`
  at sandbox boot, so their presence is already gated by the sandbox
  coming online; we no longer need a runtime verification that the
  printer always disagrees with.

Also adds a per-signal warn log when the aggregate fails so the next
mismatch is diagnosable from logs alone.

dsbx bumped to 0.1.16 so a future image build picks up the matcher fix.

* Restore strict nft aggregate, ship via image bump

User asked to avoid the version-conditional comment: we'll cut a new
release and kill-switch the prior fleet rather than carry advisory
logic in front. Reverts the front-side mask back to requiring all 7
nft signals, keeps the per-signal warn log on aggregate failure for
diagnosability, and bumps DUST_BASE_IMAGE_VERSION to 0.8.20 so the
dsbx 0.1.16 fragment fix actually ships.

[dsbx] HTTP/2 inbound termination with h1 outbound bridge (#25895)

* [dsbx] add HTTP/2 inbound bridge

Accept h2 on MITM-scoped inbound TLS connections and bridge each stream to a fresh h1 upstream connection. The bridge reuses the shared rewrite policy for allowlist checks, DSEC substitution, Basic-auth rewriting, authority/SNI validation, and per-stream deny logging.

HTTP/1.1 remains the fallback ALPN path; h2 WebSocket extended CONNECT is rejected with a structured deny reason.

* [dsbx] bump dsbx to 0.1.17 and base image to 0.8.21

dsbx now ships HTTP/2 inbound termination. Without the version bumps,
release-dsbx-cli would retag dsbx-v0.1.16 and the sandbox image at
0.8.20 would keep pulling the previous binary.

Bumps Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock to 0.1.17, DSBX_CLI_VERSION to 0.1.17,
DUST_BASE_IMAGE_VERSION to 0.8.21 (plus the registry test pin).

* [dsbx] fix clippy needless_borrow in rewrite_request_headers

* [dsbx] address h2 bridge review fixes

* [dsbx] tidy h2 bridge after review pass

Switch the remaining h2 deny-log tests to tempfile::tempdir so parallel
test runs cannot collide on a fixed /tmp path. Drop the dead PathBuf
import. Reuse the bound RewriteMode in the malformed-authority deny
branch. Surface drain errors from the Expect: 100-continue body discard
task. Add a rationale on MAX_H1_RESPONSE_CHUNK_BYTES, dated form on the
26109 TODO, and a doc comment on OpenProxyTunnel.

* [dsbx] harden h2 request body bridging

Force chunked h1 framing whenever an inbound h2 request still has a body stream, stripping content-length in that path so the h1 wire never carries both content-length and transfer-encoding.

Use INTERNAL_ERROR for unsupported h2 trailers after request bytes have reached upstream, and release h2 request-body flow-control only after the corresponding upstream writes complete.

Remove the unreachable h2 WebSocket deny branch because the h2 server does not advertise SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL. Add regressions for content-length body streams, trailer denial, and end-stream content-length preservation.

* [dsbx] tidy h2 bridge after round-2 review

Expand the rationale on forced chunked framing, fold the bridge-header
strip and content-length skip into one predicate, drop a redundant
ends_with assertion in the trailer-deny test, and shorten the streaming
content-length test name.

* [dsbx] address h2 bridge round-3 review fixes

Fold split h2 cookie request headers into one h1 Cookie header after policy substitution. Reject non-HTTPS h2 schemes on the TLS bridge before opening upstream. Add content-length mismatch coverage for h2 dependency resets and guard end-stream header validation.

[dsbx] HTTP/2 outbound origination with shared upstream pool (#26117)

* [dsbx] HTTP/2 outbound origination with shared upstream pool

Builds on #25895. Two changes that together deliver end-to-end h2:

Full-duplex per-stream forwarding. Request body and response read run
concurrently on the same upstream IO. Expect: 100-continue is forwarded
literally and 1xx responses pass back as h2 HEADERS without END_STREAM.
te: trailers is preserved on the h1 outbound with connection: te added.
Removes the synthetic 417 path and the ExpectContinueUnsupported deny
reason.

Upstream TLS advertises h2, http/1.1. On h2, streams multiplex onto one
shared connection per (authority, peer addr) from a process-scoped pool
with GOAWAY-driven draining + eviction, a saturation-triggered second
connection up to a per-key cap, and a 5-minute idle timeout. Concurrent
first-opens for the same key are de-duplicated. On h1, falls back to the
full-duplex bridge from #25895.

The h2 to h2 path strips inbound pseudo-headers and rebuilds them fresh,
runs the shared rewrite policy before building the outbound header map,
keeps split cookies split (unlike the h1 bridge which folds them per
RFC 7230), and bridges flow control in both directions.

dsbx 0.1.17 -> 0.1.18, base image 0.8.21 -> 0.8.22.

Drops the to_ascii_lowercase allocation on every header by switching
should_strip_h2_upstream_header to eq_ignore_ascii_case. Removes the

realistic dsbx lifetime). Drops a noisy explicit drop(lease) at the
end of handle_h2_to_h2_stream where scope-end drop is identical.

Adds the rationale that was previously only in the handoff doc as
inline comments: why H2_UPSTREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT is 5 minutes, why
MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_KEY is 8, why open_or_reserve_new serializes
across keys, why active_streams starts at 1, and the difference
between mark_draining and mark_closed.

front-api: keep next out of skill-instructions HTML import graph (#26087)

  The Hono-only `front-api` server is guarded at runtime by `forbid-next.cjs`, which throws if anything resolves `next` or `next/*`. Two chains in the front-side code base were tripping it:

  1. `front/lib/notifications/email-templates/_layout.tsx` imported `Head` from `next/head` to render a `<title>` inside React Email markup. Replaced with a plain `<head><title>…</title></head>` — same output, no Next dependency.

  2. Route handlers under `routes/w/[wId]/skills/...` transitively reach `front/lib/reinforcement/skill_instructions_html.ts`, which calls `buildSkillInstructionsExtensions(...)`. That builder imported the full TipTap extension set, including the React `addNodeView` on
  `KnowledgeNode` — which pulled the React `KnowledgeNodeView` → app hooks → SWR → `@app/lib/platform` (the routing shim) → `next/navigation`.

  The TipTap static HTML renderer (`renderToHTMLString`) never instantiates `NodeView`s — it only calls `renderHTML` / `parseHTML` / `markdownTokenizer`. So the React side is dead weight on the server path. This PR splits the affected extension so the server-side build doesn't load it.

feat(dsbx): retry transient network errors during action polling (#26192)

Polling must survive sandbox pause/resume cycles. When the host pauses
the sandbox via betaPause, in-flight TCP sockets may be closed by the
front side or the tunnel before RAM is thawed; on resume the next
`.send()` surfaces an I/O error.

Retry up to 30 consecutive `reqwest` errors with exponential backoff
(cap 5s). Action IDs are durable, so re-polling is idempotent. Terminal
failures (HTTP 4xx, parse errors, anything bail!-ed) still fail fast.

fix(streaming): reconnect SSE on iOS Safari bfcache restoration

iOS Safari puts pages in bfcache (Back/Forward Cache) when switching apps
or closing the browser. While in bfcache, JS is frozen and the underlying
SSE/XHR connection is killed by the OS at the network level. When the user
returns, no onerror fires (JS was suspended), so setReconnectCounter is
never called and the stream appears permanently stuck.

Fix: add visibilitychange and pageshow listeners inside useEventSource's
main useEffect. When the page becomes visible again (or is restored from
bfcache with event.persisted === true), we check if the EventSource is
CLOSED and trigger a reconnect counter increment. We also reset
reconnectAttempts so bfcache restorations don't count against the
MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS budget. The existing lastEventId mechanism in
buildEventSourceURL guarantees the reconnect picks up exactly where the
stream left off."

Treat client errors as 400s in unhandledErrorHandler (#26253)

  In front-api/middlewares/utils.ts, unhandledErrorHandler now special-cases HTTPException before the generic unhandled-error path:

  - Malformed JSON (and any other Hono HTTPException) no longer logs at error level. 4xx cases log at info as "Client API Error"; only genuine 5xx HTTPExceptions would keep the server-error type.
  - Returns the exception's intended status (e.g. 400 for malformed JSON) instead of forcing a 500.
  - statsd api_errors.count is emitted with the correct status_code and error_type (invalid_request_error for 4xx).

  So the /api/w/:wId/mcp/register malformed-body requests will now surface as info-level 400s rather than error-level 500s — matching the intent of the validator and keeping client mistakes out of your error stream.

[metronome] fix: converge swapped Metronome-only subs to "ended" (#26289)

During a contract switch, the old contract's scheduled end and the new
contract's start fire at the same instant, so Metronome emits `contract.end`
(old) and `contract.start` (new) concurrently with no guaranteed order.

The `ended_backend_only -> ended` transition only happens when `contract.end`
finds the sub already in `ended_backend_only`. But the sub is *put into* that
state by the `contract.start` handler. When `contract.end` is delivered first,
the old sub is still `active`, so it hits the "active + successor -> skip"
branch and is ack'd; `contract.start` then sets `ended_backend_only`, and no
event is left to converge it — stranding the sub (flagged by the hourly
check_ended_backend_only_subscriptions production check).

Fix: in the contract.start-driven swap paths (`activatePending`,
`swapMetronomeContract`), finalize the old sub directly to `ended` when it is
Metronome-only. Subs backed by a Stripe subscription keep `ended_backend_only`
since Stripe's `customer.subscription.deleted` converges them. Both webhook
orderings now converge with no scrub.

[sandbox] fix: block agent-proxied from reaching local sshd (#26298)

* [sandbox] fix: block agent-proxied from reaching local sshd

The in-image sshd accepted any key for root@localhost, letting uid 1003
read /run/dust/egress-secrets.json. Disable and mask sshd in the base
image, write a hardening drop-in (PermitRootLogin no, UsePAM no,
AuthorizedKeysCommand none, AllowUsers agent, DenyUsers root agent-proxied),
neutralize pam_permit.so in /etc/pam.d/sshd, and add an nftables drop on
uid 1003 -> 127.0.0.0/8:22 as a belt-and-suspenders net layer. The dsbx
healthcheck now asserts the new rule is present so a damaged ruleset
fails closed.

Image bump: dust-base 0.8.25 -> 0.8.26, dsbx 0.1.21 -> 0.1.22.

* [sandbox] chore: document load-bearing layers, drop dead build-time pkill

Review feedback:
- Comment the sshd hardening array so the four-way layering (AllowUsers /
  UsePAM / PAM neutralize / DenyUsers) doesn't read as accidental redundancy.
- Comment the nat_output 127.0.0.0/8 return as load-bearing for the new
  filter_output ssh drop (without it the broad TCP redirect would rewrite
  dport to 9990 before filter sees port 22).
- Drop the pkill -KILL sshd step. It ran at image build time where no sshd
  is alive, so it was dead. The systemctl mask is what actually prevents
  sshd from coming up at boot.

* [sandbox] chore: only mask canonical ssh units

Confirmed empirically against the e2b template: sshd.service is a symlink
alias to ssh.service and sshd.socket does not exist. Masking only ssh.service
and ssh.socket covers both and stops the build log from emitting
"already a symlink" / "does not exist" warnings that would otherwise hide
real failures.

[front] perf: cache workspace-wide metronome aggregates for members-usage (#26346)

The members-usage endpoint fetches three workspace-wide Metronome
aggregates (per-user usage, seat data, per-user/default spend caps) on
every request, re-scanning all of a customer's alerts and usage each
time. This is bounded today because the table only loads page 1, but
becomes O(N^2) external work once the table paginates.

Cache each aggregate in Redis (60s TTL) via cacheWithRedis, scoped to
the display path only — the spend-limit enforcement and webhook paths
keep reading fresh. Seat-data and cap caches self-invalidate at their
mutation chokepoints (syncSeatCount, the cap upsert/clear functions) so
config changes reflect immediately; usage is TTL-only.

Add bestEffortInvalidateCacheWithRedis to the cache utility family so
invalidation failures never break a billing mutation, and use it for the
three invalidatable caches.

duplication in the default-spend-limit hook goes away.

feat(sandbox): bash tool pause/resume capability (#26193)

* feat(sandbox): bash tool pause/resume capability

Teaches the sandbox bash tool to survive a child-action pause and
resume cleanly when the parent agent loop comes back.

- Adds `SandboxResumeState` zod schema + `isSandboxResumeState` type
  guard so bash can detect "this stepContext.resumeState is mine"
  among the other resume-state shapes (e.g. user-question).
- On first run, bash stashes the execId in the returned
  `tool_blocked_awaiting_input` resource if the parent action was
  flipped to `blocked_child_action_input_required` mid-flight by
  the upstream pause caller. The generic exit-events path persists
  it into stepContext.
- On resume, bash detects the prior execId and invokes
  `buildWaitAndCollectCommand` (already on main) instead of re-running
  the command — tails the existing capture file and surfaces the
  original exit code.
- If the sandbox had to be freshly created on resume (paused sandbox
  reaped or GC'd), bash fails clean with an unrecoverable error
  rather than spinning on a capture file that no longer exists.
- Exec-token JWT TTL bumped from 60s to 24h so it spans the pause
  window. Redis revocation list still bounds real lifetime.

* refactor(sandbox): address review feedback on bash pause path

- Destructure runContext once after a single defined-check.
- Use isToolExecutionStatusBlocked over a specific string match.
- Skip duration recording when the bash was paused (duration is
  only meaningful for terminal outcomes); drop "paused" from the
  recordToolDuration status union.
- Drop the three wrap/build-command spies in the bash tool test;
  assert directly against the command passed to sandbox.exec. Drop
  the now-redundant "blocked_validation_required does not pause"
  case (any blocked status is now treated as paused).

[audit-logs] Fix a few schema mismatches and tighten test coverage to future proof (#26412)

* fix: align user.identity_merged and user.login_failed audit emits with schemas

user.identity_merged:
- Schema declared targets = [user] but the emit sent
  [workspace, user-primary, user-secondary]. Update the schema to
  [workspace, user] — WorkOS schemas declare the set of allowed target
  types, so an emit can include multiple targets of one type without the
  schema repeating it.

user.login_failed:
- Schema declared targets = [user] but the emit only sent [workspace].
  Per [AUDIT7], workspace must be the first target.
- Capture user.email after authenticateWithWorkOSCode and emit a user
  target alongside workspace, following the member.invited pattern of
  using email as the user target's sId when no Dust UserResource exists
  (the failed login may not correspond to an existing Dust account).
- Audit logs are workspace-scoped: when workspace context is missing the
  emit is skipped entirely. When workspace is known but the email isn't
  (post-WorkOS-auth/pre-workspace-context failures), the user target
  falls back to { sId: "unknown", name: "unknown" } so emit and schema
  targets always match — no subset emits.

Includes the Hono counterpart at front-api/routes/workos/[action].ts
per [BACK17].

A _comment on the user.login_failed schema documents the "unknown"
placeholder pattern.

* feat: emit membership.role_updated for SCIM-driven role changes

Role changes triggered by SCIM group membership go through
handleRoleAssignmentForGroup, which updated the role and tracked it via
ServerSideTracking but never emitted an audit log event. Customers using
directory sync therefore saw no role-change events in their audit logs.

Emit membership.role_updated after each successful updateMembershipRole
call (both the add and remove branches), following the same pattern as
membership.origin_updated in the same file. The emit logic is extracted
into a small helper so the two branches don't duplicate the call body.
The actor uses the WorkOS directoryId when available so the audit row
identifies which directory triggered the change.

* chore: include workspace, action, and target types in audit log failure logs

The previous catch block in createAuditLogEvent only logged the raw
error, which made it impossible to identify which workspace or action
was failing without correlating across logs. Add workspaceId, action,
and target types so failures are immediately actionable in Datadog.

* test: prevent audit log schema/code drift

Add audit_log_schemas.test.ts that enforces three invariants:
- every AuditAction has a schema JSON file (Test A)
- every schema JSON file maps back to a valid AuditAction and the file
  basename matches the action (Test B)
- every emitAuditLogEvent/emitAuditLogEventDirect call site emits
  targets whose set of types exactly matches the schema's declared
  set (Test C, via brace-balanced extraction + regex). Set comparison
  lets one emit include multiple targets of the same type (e.g.
  user.identity_merged sends two user targets against a [workspace,
  user] schema) without forcing the schema to repeat the type.

To support reflection at runtime, AuditAction is now derived from a
runtime AUDIT_ACTIONS const array.

The Test C scan caught a pre-existing drift: the credentials.created
emit in pages/api/w/[wId]/credentials/index.ts only sent the workspace
target while the schema declares [workspace, credential]. Add the
missing credential target to match the schema and the other
credentials.* emit sites in provider_credentials, including the Hono
counterpart at front-api/routes/w/[wId]/credentials/index.ts.

* docs: add [AUDIT10] rule and tighten the audit-log skill

Add [AUDIT10] documenting that schema JSON files, emit calls, and WorkOS
registrations must stay in sync, with a pointer to the re-registration
command and the new CI test.

Update the dust-audit-log-event skill:
- fix the camelCase/snake_case inconsistency in the schema example and
  emit pattern so they match [AUDIT9]
- extend the Validation checklist with schema/emit/registration checks
- bump the references range to include the new [AUDIT10] rule

* fix: full schema/code audit + harden Test C against silent drift

Audit covered all 88 schema files in front/admin/audit_log_schemas/.
The 6 production-failing events flagged by Datadog
(membership.origin_updated, membership.role_updated, space.created,
space.permissions_updated, space.deleted, member.invited) split into
two categories:

1) member.invited had real drift — the emit sent [user, user, ...] only
   (no workspace target, violating [AUDIT7]) and slipped past the
   initial Test C because targets were built via
   successfulInvites.map(). Add the workspace target as the first
   element and update the schema to [workspace, user].

2) The other 5 events already agreed schema-vs-code; the production
   errors come from stale WorkOS registrations. Running
   register_audit_log_schemas.ts --execute post-merge fixes those.

Harden Test C so it cannot silently miss similar drift again:

- Scan the entire emit body for buildAuditLogTarget(...) calls instead
  of restricting to a `targets: [...]` array literal, catching dynamic
  shapes like targets: arr.map(r => buildAuditLogTarget(...)).
- Tighten the literal-target regex to require `id:` after the type so it
  no longer false-matches the sibling actor: { type: ..., id: ... }.
- Fail the test loudly when an emit site is detected but no targets can
  be extracted, instead of silently skipping (which is what hid
  member.invited from the first version of the check).

The new "unextractable" guard surfaced file.moved (targets built across
a switch in a local variable). The emit also had a subset-of-schema
problem: pod moves sent [workspace, space] and conversation moves sent
[workspace, conversation], while the schema declared all three. Refactor
to always emit [workspace, space, conversation], using "unknown"
placeholders for the inapplicable target — same pattern user.login_failed
uses when an email is missing. Targets are now inlined in the emit call
so Test C can see them. A _comment in the schema documents the pattern.

* fix: bound audit log payload size to stop "request entity too large"

"Request entity too large" was the single largest source of audit log
emit failures (~26k errors/month) — WorkOS rejected oversized requests
silently. Three layers of defense:

1) Per-value truncation in serializeMetadata. Any metadata value longer
   than 1000 chars is sliced and capped with a "...[truncated]" suffix.

2) Pre-flight size check in createAuditLogEvent. If the serialized event
   still exceeds 60KB after truncation, log a warning with workspaceId,
   action, target types, and the offending size and skip the emit. This
   turns silent WorkOS rejections into observable warnings we can act
   on. The failure-path log reuses the precomputed payloadSizeBytes
   instead of recomputing, and a comment notes that the size is an
   approximation (UTF-16 code units, not bytes).

3) Targeted fix for the likely production culprit, tool.executed. The
   extractDataSourceIds helper joined arbitrary IDs unbounded, producing
   strings that scaled with the number of resources a tool touched.
   Cap each ID list at 30 sample IDs with a "+N more" suffix — keeps
   forensic cross-reference (the sample) AND total count (the suffix)
   while staying well under the 1000-char per-value cap. No schema
   change; the field stays accessed_data_source_ids /
   accessed_table_ids.

Adds a unit test that verifies long metadata values are truncated.

* test: assert audit log schema metadata keys are snake_case

Add Test D: for every schema JSON file, every metadata key must match
^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ (snake_case). Catches camelCase, PascalCase, kebab-case,
and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

This duplicates the npm -w front run lint:audit-log-schemas check at the
vitest level so the same invariant is enforced via the test runner used
in CI, not only via the shell-based lefthook hook (which is easy to miss
if running tests directly).

* fix: attribute SCIM-driven membership.created/revoked to Directory Sync

createAndTrackMembership hard-coded the audit actor to
{ type: "user", id: user.sId }, which is correct for self-signup but
misleading when called from SCIM provisioning — the audit row reads
like the user provisioned themselves instead of identifying the
directory sync as the actor.

revokeAndTrackMembership had the symmetric issue: it used
emitAuditLogEvent({ auth, ... }), and in SCIM flows where auth is
Authenticator.internalAdminForWorkspace, buildAuditActor falls back to
a generic { type: "system", id: auth.authMethod() } actor that loses
the directory_id.

Add an optional `auditActor` parameter to both functions. The current
behavior is the default (no override). The SCIM handlers in
workos_events_queue/activities.ts now pass
{ type: "system", id: String(eventData.directoryId), name: "Directory Sync" }
for both membership.created (via createAndTrackMembership) and
membership.revoked (via revokeAndTrackMembership), matching the actor
shape already used for membership.role_updated, membership.origin_updated,
and the scim.* events in the same file.

feat(sandbox): wire up sandbox-child pause + resolve (#26221)

Connects the bash pause/resume capability to the blocked-action
lifecycle. When a sandbox-spawned child action blocks (approval,
auth, file-auth, user-question), the parent bash is paused; when the
block resolves, the parent agent loop is relaunched in resume mode.

Pause side
- New `pauseSandboxBashForBlockedChild`: flips the parent bash action
  to `blocked_child_action_input_required` and calls
  `SandboxResource.pauseForApproval`. No-ops if the action isn't a
  sandbox-child. The parent is provably still `running` here — the
  child was spawned by a synchronous `dust call` the bash is blocked
  on, so `sandbox.exec` cannot have returned yet.
- Called from the four block sites: the three `getExitOrPauseEvents`
  branches (personal-auth, file-auth, user-answer) and the validation
  branch of `createSandboxChildAction`.

Resolve side
- New `resolveSandboxChildBlock` replaces `resumeSandboxChildAction`.
  Defers relaunch until the LAST blocked sibling of the same parent
  resolves (the bash may have issued several child calls at once),
  then flips the parent to `ready_allowed_explicitly` and relaunches
  the agent loop in resume mode via the stored execId.
- The approval / user-answer / authentication flows now always call
  it (dropping the prior `approvalState !== "rejected"` /
  `outcome === "completed"` guards): the parent bash is frozen on any
  block, so it must be unfrozen regardless of the resolution outcome.

Set up the global error handler in Hono (#26431)

The front-api Hono server had no process-level error handling. Uncaught exceptions and unhandled promise rejections that escaped a request's lifecycle (timers, background promises, stream callbacks) were not routed through our logger, so they never produced the panic log entries we rely on for alerting.

This wires setupGlobalErrorHandler(logger) into front-api/server.ts, registering the process.on("uncaughtException") / process.on("unhandledRejection") handlers as the server module loads — bringing the Hono process to parity with the Temporal worker
(front/start_worker.ts), which already does this.

What this is not

This is distinct from the existing per-request error handling, which stays in place:

honoApp.onError(unhandledErrorHandler) — request-scoped; catches errors thrown inside middleware/handlers and returns a 500 to the client.
server.on("error", ...) — HTTP server-level errors only (e.g. listen failures).
Those only see errors tied to a request or the server socket. The process-level handlers added here cover everything else.

fix(sandbox): use native TLS roots for dsbx API client (#26520)

The dsbx CLI's DustApiClient was compiled with reqwest's `rustls-tls`
feature, which embeds Mozilla's webpki-roots at compile time and ignores
the system trust store entirely. Once `dust.tt` entered the egress MITM
allowlist, `dsbx tools` traffic to the Dust API began getting a leaf cert
signed by the Dust Sandbox Egress MITM CA. webpki-roots has no knowledge
of that CA, so the TLS handshake failed with a statusless network error.
It worked locally only because dev tears down the in-sandbox egress
redirect, so that traffic is never intercepted.

Switch the API client to `rustls-tls-native-roots`, which loads roots via
rustls-native-certs from SSL_CERT_FILE (/etc/dust/ca-bundle.pem) and the
OS store, both of which contain the MITM CA. This only affects the reqwest
stack; the dsbx forwarder uses a separate tokio-rustls trust path and keeps
its loop-prevention behaviour.

Bumps dsbx 0.1.23 -> 0.1.24 and the dust-base image 0.8.32 -> 0.8.33 so the
new binary is baked in and rolled out.

Drop upserts that have been in the queue for over an hour (#26534)

## What

  Stop the table upserts background worker from retrying a "poison" queue entry forever, while guaranteeing we never drop an entry that has never actually been tried.

  ## Why

  In `table_upserts_background_worker.rs`, tables are pulled from a Redis queue (`TABLE_UPSERT`) and processed once they're past the debounce window. When `process_table` fails, the error is logged and we move on — but the entry stays in the queue. A consistently-failing table therefore gets re-fetched from GCS and re-attempted on **every** loop iteration (~once per second), indefinitely. Not only this spams the logs with errors, but if it's due to a bad item causing an OOM condition, it can keep crashing the Core worker.

  Previously this was only handled for two specific errors (`"Too many columns in CSV file"`, `"CSV file is too large"`) via string matching. This PR adds a general backstop for any consistent failure.

  ## How

  **1. Age-based drop.** Any queue entry whose last activity is older than `MAX_UPSERT_AGE_MS` (1 hour) is dropped (`HDEL`) with an error log instead of being retried. The check sits right after the existing debounce check, before the table load, so it also covers entries where the load itself is what's failing. The cutoff is far beyond normal processing latency (debounce is 10s), so a healthy table never hits it.

  **2. "Has been attempted" guard.** Age alone can't distinguish "failing for an hour" from "sat in the queue for an hour because the worker was down." So an entry is only dropped when it's aged out **and** has failed at least once:
  - Added `attempts: u32` (with `#[serde(default)]`, so existing in-flight entries deserialize as `0`) to `TableUpsertActivityData`.
  - On each `process_table` failure, `attempts` is incremented and the entry is written back (`HSET`), keeping `time` unchanged so the age anchor is preserved.
  - The drop condition is `age > MAX_UPSERT_AGE_MS && attempts > 0`.

  The producer's unconditional `HSET` on new activity resets `attempts` to `0` — which is desired: fresh data earns a fresh attempt.

  ## Behavior

  - **Live poison table:** fails repeatedly, `attempts` climbs, age eventually crosses 1h → dropped. No longer retried forever.
  - **Worker was down > 1h, then restarts:** entries are old but `attempts = 0` → **not dropped**; each gets a genuine attempt. If still poison, the next iteration drops it.
  - **New activity arrives:** producer overwrites with `attempts = 0` and fresh `time` → fresh start.

  ## Trade-offs

  - Dropping an entry leaves its CSV files orphaned in GCS — an accepted, small, separately-cleanable trade-off that keeps the change simple and robust to load failures.
  - The failure write-back can race a concurrent producer `HSET` (worst case: one slightly-stale entry / off-by-one counter). Producer-clobbering isn't a concern here, so this is acceptable.
  - During a prolonged GCS/DB outage, entries that have already failed once could age out and be dropped en masse. Acceptable given the 1-hour window; revisit with error classification (retry transient errors) or a dead-letter queue if it becomes a concern.

Treat missing table CSV as empty when GCS returns a 404 (#26566)

  ## What

  Fix a recurring `TableUpsertsBackgroundWorker: Failed to process table` error caused by a 404 when reading a table's CSV during a non-truncate upsert.

  ## Symptom

```
  TableUpsertsBackgroundWorker: Failed to process table: Google(GoogleErrorResponse {
    error: ErrorList { errors: [GoogleError { reason: NotFound,
      message: "No such object: bkt-...-tables/project-...//.csv" }],
      code: 404, ... } })
```

  The entry then stays in the queue and is retried every loop iteration.

  ## Root cause

  `GoogleCloudStorageDatabasesStore::get_rows_from_csv` already intends to treat a missing CSV as an empty table — but it only catches one of the two ways the `cloud_storage` crate reports "object not found":

  - `Object::download` (the file download) → `Error::Other("No such object")` ✅ handled
  - `Object::read` (metadata fetch) → `Error::Google(GoogleErrorResponse { code: 404 })` ❌ not handled

  `csv.parse()` was later changed to call `Object::read` **first** (a metadata probe for its file-size guard) before downloading. So when the CSV is missing, the *metadata* call now 404s before the download is ever attempted — surfacing the `Google` variant that the handler doesn't match. It falls through to `_ => Err(e)` and propagates.

  This fires for **any** non-truncate upsert whose `{table_id}.csv` doesn't exist yet:
  - the table's CSV was deleted (e.g. table deleted/recreated) while a queued upsert was pending,
  - the table was truncated away,
  - or it's simply a brand-new table's first upsert.

  All of these used to be handled as "empty table" before the metadata probe was added.

  ## Fix

  Extend the not-found handler in `get_rows_from_csv` to also treat the `Error::Google(... code: 404 ...)` variant as an empty table, mirroring the pattern already used in `delete_table_data`. The stale comment is updated to document both code paths.

  With this, the upsert merges into an empty row set and re-writes the file, and the queue entry clears normally.

[front-api] fix: use relative SSE redirect to preserve Authorization (#26594)

redirectToSse built an absolute Location from ctx.req.url's origin. front-api
runs as a plain-HTTP server behind a TLS-terminating ingress, so that origin is
http://, producing an https -> http downgrade on the 307. HTTP clients (the
CLI's reqwest) strip the Authorization header on a protocol downgrade, so the
redirected SSE request hit front-sse unauthenticated -> 401.

Emit a relative Location (path + query) instead. The client resolves it against
the original https request URI, preserving scheme, origin, and the Authorization
header. This mirrors the effective behavior of the Next middleware redirect,
which keeps the public https origin via x-forwarded-proto.

[front] Only surface egress allowlist denials to sandbox agents (#26635)

The sandbox deny log is written by two layers into one file: the egress
proxy's domain-allowlist gate (reason "proxy_denied") and the in-sandbox
request-rewrite harness (malformed headers, secret-to-host scoping, SNI
checks, etc.). Both were dumped raw into the <network_proxy_logs> block, so
agents read harness rejections and upstream 4xx/auth failures on allowed
domains as "the proxy blocked this domain".

Filter the agent-facing block to allowlist denials only and present them as a
clean line. Unrecognized lines are kept verbatim so we never swallow a real

Reject table upserts when too many files are already pending (429) (#26587)

  ## What

  Add producer-side backpressure so a single table can't accumulate an unbounded number of pending update files. Once a table has too many unprocessed files queued, the API rejects further upserts/deletes with **429 Too Many Requests** instead of letting them pile up.

  ## Why

  The background worker (`TableUpsertsBackgroundWorker`) reads **all** pending update files for a table and merges them — into memory — in one shot (`get_deduped_rows_from_all_files` + the non-truncate merge in `batch_upsert_table_rows`). Each individual file is size-bounded, but nothing bounds the *count* or *aggregate* size. If the worker falls behind or a table is hammered, files accumulate until the merge is large enough to **OOM-crash the worker**.

  Per-file limits exist at the API level, but the background path had no protection against accumulation. The cleanest fix is to fail fast at the source rather than build heroics into the worker.

  ## How

  **Backpressure at the producer** (`databases/table.rs`):
  - `schedule_background_upsert_or_delete` (the non-truncate path, used by both row and CSV upserts *and* deletes) now counts the table's pending files and, if `>= MAX_PENDING_UPSERT_FILES` (100), returns a new typed error `TableUpsertError::TooManyPendingUpserts` instead of writing another file.
  - Truncate upserts bypass this path and reset the pending files, so they remain the recovery escape hatch for a wedged table.

  **429 mapping** (`api/tables.rs`):
  - `tables_rows_upsert` and `tables_csv_upsert` downcast the error and return `429 too_many_pending_upserts`; everything else stays `500`.

  **Reclaim orphaned files on drop** (`databases/table_upserts_background_worker.rs`):
  - The existing max-age drop (for poison entries) previously left the table's CSV files orphaned in GCS. With backpressure in place, orphaned files would keep the pending count high and 429 that table **forever**. The drop now also deletes the table's CSV files (`delete_all_files_for_table`), so the count can return to zero. The check moved into the `Some(table)` branch to reuse the existing delete helper — behavior-preserving, since the `attempts > 0` guard could only ever fire on the `process_table` path anyway.

  ## Trade-offs / notes

  - The pending-file count uses a full prefix list rather than a capped probe. In steady state the count is capped at ~100, so the list is small; a larger list only happens for a pre-existing backlog, which the worker drains.
  - **Front (separate repo) still needs to handle the 429** — pass it through and back off/retry rather than treating it as a hard failure.

[front] cut sandbox cold-start round-trips in egress + GCS setup (#26654)

* [front] cut sandbox cold-start round-trips in egress + GCS setup

Each setup sub-step was its own round-trip to the VM, and the Datadog
waterfall showed that latency (plus a hardcoded sleep) dominating cold
start. Bundle them.

GCS: the token write, token-server start, and readiness check were three
execs ending in a flat `sleep 1`. Fold into one exec that nohups the
server and polls curl every 50ms, returning the instant it listens
(typically <100ms). Removes ~1s + 2 round-trips.

Egress: merge the token write + chmod into a single root
`install -m600 /dev/stdin` (token via stdin, never argv), and run the
token/secrets/manifest writes concurrently since they touch independent
files. The forwarder start still waits for all three. Collapses ~4
sequential round-trips into ~2 of wall-time; ordering and the
write-secrets-before-kill invariant on the restart path are preserved.

* [front] address review: surface token-server failure detail, extract constants

- GCS token-server error path now logs the exec stdout/stderr instead of
  swallowing it into an opaque "not ready in time".
- Pull the token-server URL, poll attempts/interval, and exec timeout into
  named constants (the 5s poll ceiling vs 10s hard timeout was invisible).
- Drop dead writeFile mock fields from egress.test.ts sandbox stubs; the
  token now goes through execRoot + install, not writeFile.

* [front] address review: gate egress writes, preserve gcs exec errors

Two failure-path fixes from review:

- egress: await the token write before the secrets/manifest writes instead
  of firing all three in one Promise.all. Restores the old contract where a
  token failure short-circuits before any secrets/manifest hit disk, which
  matters on the restart path (a still-running forwarder's files must not be
  rewritten while setup returns Err). Secrets and manifest still run
  concurrently once the token is in place.

- gcs: when the combined token-server exec returns Err (sandbox-not-found,
  transport failure, timeout), return it as-is instead of flattening it into
  the generic "not ready in time" error, so the concrete cause survives to
  the caller.

* [front] address review: serialize egress writes for no-op failure semantics

The previous Promise.all let the manifest write land even when the secrets
write failed, diverging the sandbox-visible manifest from what the forwarder
loaded on the restart path. Restore the original sequential gating: token ->
secrets -> manifest, each short-circuiting the rest on failure. Add a test
asserting the manifest write is skipped when the secrets write fails.

* [front] fix: confirm missing connector workflows via describe() to avoid visibility lag false positives

The check_active_workflows_for_connectors check determined workflow
"running" status solely via client.workflow.list(... ExecutionStatus =
"Running"), which reads from Temporal's eventually-consistent visibility
store. Incremental sync workflows (e.g. Google Drive) continueAsNew on
every cycle, so a genuinely running workflow can transiently be absent
from the visibility query, producing false "Missing temporal workflows"

report the ones that truly are not running. This runs only for the
(normally tiny) candidate-missing set, so the batched visibility query
remains the fast path. Matches the describe()-based approach already used
by the schedule path and check_active_workflows_for_front.

* [front] cut sandbox cold-start: drop update-ca-certificates, overlap GCS mount

The egress trust-bundle install ran update-ca-certificates, which forks openssl
once per system root and rebuilds the whole CA store. On the constrained microVM
that was ~1.65s of cold start, the single largest remaining cost after the
round-trip bundling in #26654.

The image already ships the public roots and the dsbx MITM CA is the only
runtime addition, so reproduce the same outcome incrementally: snapshot the
pristine system bundle once, then rebuild /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt as
pristine + dsbx CA and drop in the single SSL_CERT_DIR hash symlink. Same files,
~tens of ms instead of ~1.65s. Idempotent across the health-probe repair path.

Separately, run egress prep concurrently with the GCS mount on cold start. The
mount only talks to storage.googleapis.com as root, which the in-sandbox
nftables rules never touch (every rule is scoped to the agent uid; chains
default to accept), so it does not depend on egress finishing. Egress errors
still take precedence.
