fix(mobile): stop conversation SSE streams leaking after navigating away (#26722)

The conversation events and message stream tasks captured `self` strongly
via `guard let self` at the top of their loops, so the view model could
never deinit and the SSE reconnect loop ran forever. Visiting several
conversations left an equal number of streams reconnecting indefinitely
(and refreshing the token on each reconnect).

Capture the immutable inputs by value and reference `self` weakly so deinit
fires and cancels the stream when the conversation is dismissed. Also log
SSE disconnect/cancel so teardown is observable.

fix(streaming): fix GCS write stream leaks and SSE double-unsubscribe (#26600)

Three distinct leak fixes, no behaviour changes.

1. GCS write streams leaked on upload error paths (utils.ts, processing.ts)
   When parseUploadRequest rejected a file (wrong MIME type, size, empty)
   or threw, the GCS WritableStream passed in was abandoned without
   destroy(). The GCS SDK internally allocates a PassThroughShim and
   wires five event-listener closures on creation; without destroy() these
   are never collected. Fix: call writableStream.destroy() on both error
   paths. Secondary case in processing.ts: writeStream was allocated before
   createReadableFromUrl, so a URL-fetch failure left it orphaned; moved
   allocation inside the try block after the fetch succeeds.

2. SSE generators double-unsubscribed after normal exit (pubsub.ts, mcp_events.ts)
   After a generator exits cleanly (timeout / end-of-stream), finally{}
   correctly calls unsubscribe(). Then res.end() causes the response close
   event to fire -> controller.abort() -> AbortSignal fires -> the still-
   registered signal.addEventListener("abort", unsubscribe) listener fires
   a second time. For multi-subscriber channels this double-decrements
   activeSubscriptionCount, causing the metric to drift negative over time.
   Fix: signal.removeEventListener("abort", unsubscribe) in finally before
   calling unsubscribe(), ensuring exactly one cleanup call per subscription.

Route MCP OAuth token traffic through static IP proxy for verified domains (#26711)

* Route MCP OAuth token traffic through static IP proxy for verified domains

MCP OAuth token activity in core (finalize/refresh) unconditionally used the
untrusted egress proxy, ignoring whether the token endpoint is under a
workspace-verified domain. This diverged from front's MCP tool-call routing,
which uses the static IP proxy for verified domains. This change makes token
traffic consistent while keeping the security invariant: static IP only for
verified targets, untrusted egress otherwise, never direct egress.

front:
- computeUseStaticIpProxy (workspace_has_domains.ts): HTTPS-only, verified-domain
  check on the token endpoint host; returns a boolean.
- MCPOAuthProvider.getUpdatedExtraConfig stamps use_static_ip_proxy authoritatively
  from the final persisted token_endpoint, strips any caller-supplied value, and
  writes it last so restConfig cannot override security-sensitive fields.
- MCPMetadataSchema requires use_static_ip_proxy ("true"/"false") for new connections.
- New MCP-aware token helper (mcp_oauth_access_token.ts) recomputes + PATCHes the
  flag BEFORE the access-token fetch (TTL-gated ~5 min), so refreshes never use a
  stale decision. All MCP token callers funnel through it.
- OAuthAPI.updateConnectionMetadata (Result-returning) targets the new PATCH route.

core:
- proxy_client: STATIC_IP_PROXY lazy_static; pure build_proxied_no_redirect helper
  disables redirects (Policy::none()); try_build_* return Option.
- mcp provider: use_static_ip_proxy: Option<String> ("true" => static); fail-closed
  client_for (static -> untrusted -> error, never reqwest::Client::new()); finalize
  and refresh use it.
- PATCH /connections/{id}/metadata (mcp/mcp_static only) persists the flag as a
  string and returns the full connection metadata shape.

Tests: front unit tests for the helper, override-proofing, and freshness sync;
core unit tests for proxy build + client_for fallback/fail-closed + metadata
(de)serialization; core functional tests for the PATCH endpoint.

Metadata values are strings end-to-end (Record<string,string>); a JSON bool in
the struct would fail deserialization.

* Honor legacy static-IP workspace + direct fallback for local dev

- computeUseStaticIpProxy now also returns true for the legacy
  isWorkspaceUsingStaticIP workspace, matching MCP tool-call routing.
- client_for / reqwest_client fall back to a direct (no-redirect) client
  when no egress proxy is configured (local dev) instead of erroring/panicking;
  production still prefers static -> untrusted.
- Drop design docs from the branch.

* Address review feedback

- Don't mark freshness as checked after a failed metadata PATCH (retry next
  call instead of waiting out the TTL with a stale flag).
- Extract MCPConnectionMetadata::use_static_ip() so the "true" discriminator
  lives in one place.
- Inline the two trivial proxy-url accessor wrappers.
- Clarify comments: helper adds an HTTPS-only gate vs tool-call routing; schema
  field is stamped authoritatively, never caller-supplied. TTL idiom.

* Make use_static_ip_proxy schema field optional (absence fails safe to false)

* Only allow direct egress fallback when no proxy is configured (local dev)

core has no environment flag, but a deployed environment always sets an egress
proxy env var. Gate the direct (un-proxied) fallback on is_egress_proxy_configured():
- no proxy configured (local dev) -> direct fallback allowed.
- a proxy is configured but fails to build (deployed misconfig) -> fail closed
  instead of silently egressing directly.

* cargo fmt

* Rename computeUseStaticIpProxy -> shouldUseStaticIpProxy

* Address review: log unproxied MCP client + rename colliding helper

- reqwest_client() now logs when it falls back to an unproxied (direct) client
  so a deployed-env misconfiguration isn't silent (local dev still works).
- Rename data_classification_labels' getMCPConnectionAccessToken ->
  getInternalMCPServerAccessToken to remove the name collision with the new
  MCP OAuth token helper (it takes an internal MCP server id, not a connection).

refactor(mobile): extract AgentMessageStream reducer (#26757)

The streaming-event reduction was smeared across the ViewModel — handleMessageEvent
/ handleGenerationTokens / finalizeMessage / flushThinkingBuffer mutating six
@Published fields plus two private buffers in a specific order, reachable only
through a live @MainActor SSE subscription. That's the most intricate logic in the
conversation view and it had no home and no test surface.

Move it into a pure AgentMessageStream value type (apply(event) -> snapshot, no
SwiftUI / networking / concurrency) that owns token & chain-of-thought accumulation,
the thinking-buffer flush ordering, the action lifecycle, and terminal status. The
ViewModel keeps the subscription and a thin router, and commits the finished snapshot
onto the persisted message.

Blocking (approval / personal auth / file auth) is split out of the activity
lifecycle into a separate BlockedState. AgentStreamingPhase survives only as a
derived view projection, so the message views are unchanged. Behavior-preserving.

fix(mobile): unstick the blocked-action banner after out-of-app resolution (#26758)

When a tool needs authentication, the server parks the agent loop and closes the
message-events SSE. The stream is then dead — so when the user authenticates in
the web app and comes back, nothing in the app clears the blocked banner, and it
stays up over a conversation that has actually resumed.

reconcileBlockedActions was set-only: it set a block when the server reported one
but never cleared it. Make it authoritative in both directions — an empty server
result now drops the block and releases the stream id so startMessageStream can
re-attach to the resumed message. Drive it from a scenePhase foreground hook,
which is the only resume signal the app has while the stream is parked.

Decode the tool_ask_user_question stream event and the blocked_user_answer_required
reconcile status, render the question with single/multi-select options and an

[dsbx] Skip secret substitution in reflection-prone headers (#26828)

* [dsbx] Skip secret substitution in reflection-prone headers

A recognized DSEC placeholder placed in a non-credential header (User-Agent,
Origin, X-Request-Id, trace headers, ...) was substituted with the real secret
on the wire. Endpoints like Cloudflare's /cdn-cgi/trace echo those headers back
in the response (uag=...), so an agent could read the plaintext secret back out,
defeating the placeholder model.

Block substitution for a curated set of headers that are never credentials and
are routinely reflected or logged. The opaque placeholder is left in place (it
reveals nothing) rather than dropping the connection. Authorization, Cookie, and
custom headers still substitute, so bespoke auth header names are unaffected.

Single choke point in rewrite_header_value covers both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2.

* [dsbx] Lock down reflection-skip blocklist

Address review: document that the blocklist short-circuit also suppresses the
substitution path's unknown-placeholder / non-allowed-host denies for these
headers (forged/cross-host placeholder travels upstream as the opaque token
instead of dropping; acceptable since it reveals nothing). Add x-cloud-trace-
context and the x-datadog-* prefix family given our GCP+Datadog stack. Add a
membership unit test so a dropped header fails CI instead of silently leaking.

* [dsbx] Bump dsbx to 0.1.26 and base image to 0.8.36

Ship the reflection-skip fix: bump dsbx so a new release binary is built, bump
DSBX_CLI_VERSION so the base image pulls it, and bump the base image tag so the
registry rebuilds the image with the new dsbx baked in.

* [dsbx] Add more reflected/forwarding/trace headers to blocklist

Bug-hunt follow-up: add baggage and grpc-trace-bin (trace context that gets

* [front] DangerJS: require audit schema version bump on schema changes

When a schema file under front/admin/audit_log_schemas/ is added or
modified, verify its version in schema_versions.json was bumped relative
to main. A missing or non-incremented version means the registration
script wasn't run, so the deployed code would emit a stale version and
WorkOS would reject the event.

Preserve special tags and render skill references when updating skills via skill_authoring (#26805) * Preserve special tags when updating skills via skill_authoring update_skill could silently break a skill's nested-skill wiring. Two problems: - referencedSkillIds was never synced, so the SkillReferenceModel rows (the actual runtime nested-skill links) drifted from the tags in the instructions. Now we re-derive them from the resolved instructions on every instruction change, like the builder UI does. - A full instructions replace could drop the special tags (nested skill, knowledge, tool references) that the builder manages. We now reject a full replace that drops any tag present in the current instructions, and tell the agent to keep them or use a targeted edit. Also updated the tool description and the code-defined skill playbook so the agent knows these tags are load-bearing and must be preserved. * Type special-tag categories and tighten regex export * Render skill references in server-side instructions HTML The server markdown-to-HTML converter (convertMarkdownToBlockHtml) handled knowledge and tool tags but not skill references, so was HTML-escaped into literal text in instructionsHtml. The builder loads that HTML, so edits made via the skill_authoring tool rendered as raw XML. Wire skill references through the same path as knowledge and tool: - Split SkillNode into a schema-only base (skill_builder/SkillNode) and the React view (input_bar/SkillNode), mirroring ToolNode/ToolNodeWithView, so the server renderer can register it without pulling in React. - Register the base node in the server extension list and recover standalone / lines. - Preserve the id attribute on skill/unavailable_skill during the strip step. Two rendering bugs fixed along the way: - skillUnavailable was parse-only but had no renderHTML, so the static renderer emitted a malformed skillunavailable="false/" attribute (the client only avoided it because DOMPurify drops all but id/name/icon). Make it render nothing; the unavailable state is encoded by the tag name. - A childless 2-tuple renderHTML self-closes as in the static string renderer, and HTML5 parsers ignore self-close on unknown tags, so trailing text got swallowed into the node. Render an explicit chip child like ToolNode/KnowledgeNode to force a properly closed element. Add a targeted backfill for skills whose stored HTML escaped their skill references. * Store skill references as empty paired tags, not chip-wrapped The previous renderHTML emitted a chip child inside the skill tag (Name) to stop the server static renderer from self-closing the element. That child broke SKILL_REFERENCE_TAG_REGEX, which only matches the self-closing or empty-paired form. Because instructionsHtml is now saved in the chip-wrapped form on both the client (getHTML) and server paths, normalizeSkillReferenceTags could no longer rewrite references in instructionsHtml: skill rename and availability reconciliation silently updated the markdown instructions but left instructionsHtml stale, desyncing the two. Render an empty-string child instead. That produces , the same empty paired form serializeSkillTag({ html: true }) emits and the regex matches, while still avoiding the self-close that swallows following siblings. The visible chip comes from the React node view, not from the stored HTML, so nothing changes in the editor. This also stops the "Unavailable skill" chip label from leaking into instructionsHtml (and the model prompt) for unavailable references. Tests assert the stored tag is an empty paired element and that extractUniqueSkillReferenceIds recovers the id from the rendered HTML, which is the exact path the reconciliation relies on. * Drop the instructionsHtml backfill script The escaped-skill-reference bug never reached prod, so there are no corrupted rows to re-render. Remove the one-off backfill instead of shipping a script nobody needs to run. * Guard targeted edits and attribute changes in skill_authoring The special-tag guard in update_skill only ran on full instructions replaces and only compared tag ids. A targeted old_string/new_string edit could drop a builder-managed tag, and a full replace could keep a tag id while stripping the attributes that make it usable. Both desynced the stored instructions and references from the builder-managed wiring. Run findDroppedSpecialTags on the resolved instructions for both edit modes, and compare normalized knowledge/tool tag payloads instead of ids. Nested-skill tags stay id-based because normalizeSkillReferenceTags already rewrites their name and icon to canonical form on every save. * Reject phantom special tags on skill create and update The skill_authoring update guard only caught dropped or altered special tags, and create did not check at all. An agent could add a or tag (e.g. copied from a skill it read) and it would persist as dead markup with no real attachment behind it, on both the create and update paths. Split the handling by what can actually be wired from the instructions: - Nested skill references re-derive from the text on save, so the agent may add them (they get wired) but not drop them (that would silently unlink a skill the builder attached). - Knowledge and tool tags cannot be wired from text; their attachments are carried over untouched. Any add, drop, or change desyncs the markup from the real attachments, so reject all three. - A freshly created skill has no attachments, so reject any special tag in create instructions outright. The skill stays instructions-only. Reword the guard comment to spell out this asymmetry instead of implying all three tag types are handled the same way. Reseed the update-guard tests via SkillFactory (a realistic builder-made skill) instead of injecting tags through create_skill, and add coverage for added tags and for create. --------- Co-authored-by: Henry Fontanier <14199823+fontanierh@users.noreply.github.com>

[front] Attribute sub-agent usage to the originating API key (attribution only) (#26888)

* Attribute sub-agent usage to the originating API key (attribution only)

Sub-agents re-authenticate to the Dust API with the workspace system key, so
usage analytics (which resolves api_key_name from the persisted
userContextApiKeyId) collapsed all sub-agent usage to "DustSystemKey". The
prior x-dust-api-key-name header only overrode the in-memory key name and
became a no-op once analytics switched to id-based resolution.

Carry the originating key as an attribution-only reference, never touching
auth.key() (so role, caps and system-key checks are unaffected):
- Authenticator gains _attributionKey + withAttributionKey/attributionKeyId,
  persisted through toJSON/fromJSON.
- withPublicAPIAuthentication resolves the x-dust-api-key-name header to a key
  within the same workspace and attaches it as the attribution key.
- User messages persist apiKeyId = attributionKeyId ?? key.id.
- getApiKeyNameHeader forwards the attribution name so it propagates
  transitively through nested sub-agents and across the Temporal boundary.
- Metronome events never surface the system key as api_key_name (keyless
  internal runs resolve to "unknown").

Only the key name travels over the wire (no ModelId), preserving SEC2.

[connectors] Bound concurrency in Microsoft getRootNodesToSync fan-out (#26937)

getRootNodesToSyncFromResources fired one Graph API call per root
resource through an unbounded Promise.all. On connectors with many roots
(500+) this produced a burst large enough to self-induce Graph 429
throttling. Any single rejection failed the whole activity, which retried
and re-fired the identical burst, looping forever (the retry-after backoff
could never win because each retry recreated the cause).

Convert the fan-out to concurrentExecutor with concurrency 5, matching the
sibling siteDriveNodes block and the other call sites in the file (BACK7).

[front] Add claude-fable-5 behind a dust-only feature flag (#27113)

* [front] add claude-fable-5 behind a dust-only feature flag

Adds the GA claude-fable-5 model (config, pricing, registry, router
whitelist, SDK types, UI config, tests) following the Opus 4.8 pattern.

The model is gated by its own dust-only flag (claude_fable_5_feature)
and keeps routing through the dedicated EAP Anthropic key (useEapKey),
which also forces non-Vertex routing.

Minimum reasoning effort is medium: Fable 5 400s on an explicit
thinking disabled, and our client sends that for none/light efforts,
so those are unsupported. Pricing is $10/$50 per MTok per the official
models page.

Also fixes the LLM integration test harness for Anthropic/Google
models: getLLM now calls getFeatureFlags unconditionally (since the
Vertex routing change), which threw with the workspace-less mock
authenticator. Mock it to return no flags so tests hit providers
directly.

* fix claude-fable-5 description context size copy

Said 200k (copied from the Opus 4.8 block) while contextSize is 400k.

* point dust-lionel agents at claude-fable-5

dust-lionel agents were bound to custom model index 1 from the infra
custom-models config (the EAP checkpoint). Now that the GA model is in
the repo, convert them to static-model agents on
CLAUDE_FABLE_5_DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIG, mirroring the dust-ant pattern.

The base agent moves from light to medium reasoning effort since
that's the model's minimum (light maps to disabled thinking, which
Fable 5 rejects). They stay gated by dust_internal_global_agents and
no longer depend on custom_model_feature.

* add claude_fable_5_feature to SDK whitelistable features

front-api's feature_flags route types its response with the SDK union,
so the new flag must exist there too (caught by front-api tsgo in CI).

* clamp anthropic reasoning effort to the model's supported range

Some callers default the reasoning effort to "none" when unset, which
maps to an explicit disabled thinking. Claude Fable 5 rejects that with
a 400, so unsupported efforts now fall back to the model's minimum
supported one before building the thinking config.

No behavior change for existing models: the only currently-unsupported
effort is "none" on recent Opus/Sonnet configs, where the minimum
("light") maps to the same disabled-thinking request.

Also fixes import sorting in dust.ts (caught by biome ci).

* support light effort on claude-fable-5 via native light reasoning

With useNativeLightReasoning, light maps to adaptive thinking with low
effort instead of an explicit disabled thinking (which Fable 5 rejects),
so light becomes supported. Default stays medium. Restores the base
dust-lionel agent to light effort.

Validated against the EAP key: 33/34 live tests pass, the light variant
included; the remaining failure is forced tool_choice, which the model
does not support.

[audit-logs] per-user member.invited + agent execution traceability (#27021)

* [front] Emit one member.invited audit event per invited user

A bulk invite of 20+ users produced a single member.invited event with one
target per invite, exceeding WorkOS's maxItems: 20 targets limit and failing
with invalid_audit_log. Emit one ["workspace", "user"] event per invited user
instead, each recording the role the user was invited with.

Schema updated: member.invited.json now declares ["workspace", "user"] targets
and `role` metadata (dropping the batch-oriented `emails`/`invited_count`).
Bulk-vs-individual is already captured by the separate member.bulk_invited
event, so it is not duplicated here. This schema change must be registered with
WorkOS and schema_versions.json committed as a separate, approved step.

* [front] Audit log enhancements for agent execution traceability

Adds run correlation, sub-agent lineage, and tool-approval audit events for
agent executions (enterprise compliance requirement, issue #8573).

- agent.executed / tool.executed: add agent_message_id (the durable per-run
  correlation id — 1:1 with an agent execution) so a run's invocation, tool
  calls, and (future) completion can be correlated.
- agent.executed: add trigger_type ("user" | "agent" | "trigger" | "handover"),
  parent_agent_message_id and depth for sub-agent lineage. trigger_type is
  derived via deriveAgentTriggerType (unit-tested) from the triggering user
  message's agenticMessageData and conversation.depth/triggerId.
- New tool.approval_requested: emitted (direct, worker context) when an MCP
  action is persisted as blocked_validation_required.
- New tool.approval_resolved: emitted in validateAction after the status update,
  with the deciding user as actor and the outcome in the `decision` metadata
  (approved | rejected | always_approved). Fire-and-forget and isolated so it
  can never block or break the approval flow; the agent config is resolved via
  AgentMCPActionResource.getLightAgentConfiguration so the model lookup stays in
  the resource layer.

Schema version bumps are intentionally NOT included here: register the schemas
with WorkOS and commit the updated schema_versions.json as a separate, approved
step (see the dust-audit-log-event skill). CI (the version-presence test and
the DangerJS schema-version check) will be red until that lands.

Note: parent_conversation_id was intentionally omitted — there is no
MessageResource yet, so resolving the parent agent message to its conversation
would require direct Sequelize models in lib/api (against BACK1/BACK5), and it
is derivable from parent_agent_message_id (which maps to the parent's
agent.executed.conversation_id).

* [front] Register audit log schemas and commit version map

Registered the new/changed schemas with WorkOS and committed the resulting
schema_versions.json so emitted events send the correct version:

- member.invited      -> v6 (targets + role metadata change)
- agent.executed      -> v5 (agent_message_id, trigger_type, lineage)
- tool.executed       -> v4 (agent_message_id)
- tool.approval_requested -> v1 (new)
- tool.approval_resolved  -> v1 (new)

This greens the version-presence test and the DangerJS schema-version check.

Config-driven server-side fallback for Anthropic models (#26813)

* feat(llm): config-driven server-side fallback for Anthropic models

Add an optional fallbackModels field to the model config. When set, the
Anthropic request carries a server-side fallback param so the provider
retries against those models, in order, if the primary refuses or is
unavailable. The fallback targets live in the model config (GCS), nothing
is hardcoded in the client.

Also harden the top-level Anthropic stream-event switch: a new server-side
fallback SSE event would previously hit assertNever and 500 the stream.
Log and ignore unknown event types instead via assertNeverAndIgnore.

The fallback beta header is carried through the existing customBetas config,
so no code change is needed to enable it.

* fix(llm): scope fallback to streaming path, harden stream-event guards

Address review findings:
- Move the fallback param off buildBaseRequestPayload onto the streaming
  request only. The batch path does not forward customBetas, so a fallback
  param there would have been sent without its required beta header.
- Log only the event type (not the full event object) when ignoring an
  unhandled stream event, to avoid dumping prompt/response content into logs.
- Apply the same ignore-and-log treatment to the content-block and delta
  switches, since a new beta can introduce new block/delta types the SDK
  does not yet model, same as top-level events.

* fix(llm): align server-side fallback with the released API, enable on Fable 5

The released param is `fallbacks` (not `fallback`) and requires the
server-side-fallback-2026-06-01 beta header exactly, so the client now
attaches the header itself instead of relying on customBetas. The fallback
boundary arrives as a content block (start/stop pair with no deltas), so
content_block_stop now ignores blocks whose start was ignored instead of
failing the index assertion. Fable 5 sets Opus 4.8 as its fallback target
(the only allowed one per the Models API).

fix: resumable GCS uploads for large files, retry replayable streamed writes (#27142)

* fix: use resumable GCS uploads for large files and retry replayable streamed writes

Large file uploads (POST /files/[fileId]) stream the request body to GCS as a
single non-resumable multipart POST. Streamed uploads bypass the SDK
retryOptions and the request stream cannot be replayed, so any transient
connection reset ("socket hang up") fails the upload with a 500. 97% of failing
uploads in Datadog are these multipart POSTs, large audio files are hit hardest
since transfer time scales exposure.

Sandbox child tool calls resolved their stake from raw tool names and

of that, "always approve" on a child action recorded the approval under

content). Net effect: medium/low stake tools called through dsbx
re-prompted for approval on every call, even after "always approve".

  argumentsRequiringApproval through getToolExtraFields (same as the

Rewrite ensureAllAutoToolsAreCreated as parallel reads plus one bulk insert (#27303)

* [front] perf(mcp): rewrite ensureAllAutoToolsAreCreated as parallel reads + one bulk insert

The function ran ~5 sequential queries per auto server through
MCPServerViewResource.create (system space fetch, listByMCPServer,
internal server fetch, insert), which Datadog traces show at 750ms-1.4s
per call (~265 sequential queries at workspace creation).

It now runs the three read checks in parallel and creates all missing
views with a single bulkCreate using ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, which also
makes concurrent calls converge instead of failing on the unique
constraint. Rows swallowed by a conflict on another constraint (e.g.
name uniqueness per space) are counted and logged.

Behavior note: the bulk insert does not clean up regular-space views of
the same server when creating the global view. That case is only
reachable on a manual -> auto availability transition, which the
snapshot guard routes to the dedicated migration script.

* Distinguish benign insert races from genuine conflicts in ensure logging

A bulkCreate shortfall is expected when a concurrent call inserted the
same rows (info), and an anomaly only when a row was swallowed by a
conflict on another unique constraint and the view is genuinely missing
(warn). Re-read after a shortfall to tell them apart; the re-read only
runs in that rare path.

Create auto MCP server views just in time instead of backfilling all workspaces (#27297)

* [front] feat(mcp): create auto MCP server views just in time instead of backfilling

Adding a new auto internal MCP server used to require running a temporal
workflow over every workspace to insert the 2 views (system + global).
Slow, manual, and easy to forget.

Views are now created lazily on the read paths that list tools (agent
builder, space tool listings, agent loop, front-api routes), guarded by
a per-process cache keyed on the fingerprint of the expected auto server
set (feature flags incl. global rollouts, plan, deep-dive setting, all
short-TTL memoized), with in-flight dedup. Any availability change
re-hydrates within seconds; the cache entry is only written when the
ensure run converged, and deleting an internal auto view invalidates it.

ensureAllAutoToolsAreCreated loses its admin-only guard (member reads
must hydrate too) and reports convergence; missing default spaces now
log and skip instead of throwing so a workspace mid-creation cannot 500
a read.

The backfill workflow and script are deleted, the availability snapshot
guard no longer asks for a backfill on new auto tools, and dust-hive
warm drops the script invocation.

* Address review: zero reads on the hydration hot path

The cache check no longer reads feature flags or the deep-dive setting
per call. The entry is keyed on the plan code (in memory on the auth)
with a TTL; a stale entry is harmless as long as the rows exist, and
every way the expected set changes is covered: registry changes ship
with a deploy (cold caches), workspace flag toggles create the views at
the mutation site (poke plugin, and now the toggle_feature_flags script
too), plan changes miss on the plan code, and global rollout changes
are bounded by the TTL.

Also enforce that auto internal views cannot be deleted from the global
space (they are auto-created by design and would be recreated on the
next read), replacing the hydration-cache invalidation hooks in
delete/hardDelete.

* Bump hydration cache max size to 1M entries

* Bump hydration cache TTL to 30 minutes

fix: retry sub-8MB file uploads to GCS and time out stalled uploads (#27319)

* fix: retry sub-8MB file uploads to GCS and time out stalled uploads

Conversation file uploads below the resumable threshold are streamed
straight from the request to GCS as a single multipart POST. The request
stream is not replayable, so one transient connection reset ("socket hang
up") fails the whole upload with a 500. This is the bulk of the ~600
failed uploads per day, typically 4-7MB PDFs.

- parseUploadRequest: buffer sub-threshold payloads in memory and write
  them after parsing with withRetryOnTransientGCSError (the buffer is
  replayable). Larger files keep the resumable streamed path which already
  retries per chunk.
- Add an overall 5 minute timeout on receive + write. A stalled GCS
  connection (or client) used to hang the request forever with no error
  surfaced to the user and nothing in the logs.
- Move the resumable threshold constants to lib/file_storage to avoid an
  import cycle.

* review: clear timeout on rejection, keep socket alive when client is done

- clearTimeout in a finally so the 5 min timer does not stay armed when
  form.parse or the buffered save rejects.
- Only destroy the request on timeout when the client is the stalled side;
  if the body was fully received (GCS-side stall), keep the socket alive so
  the 500 can reach the client.
- Spread vi.importActual in the file_storage mock so constants keep their
  real values instead of re-declared copies; derive the test boundary from
  GCS_RESUMABLE_UPLOAD_THRESHOLD_BYTES.

* review: scale upload timeout with file size, build a real IncomingMessage in tests

A flat 5 minute timeout is long for a 4MB PDF and too short for a slow
350MB delimited upload. Use a 1 minute floor plus a slow-link allowance
(~2 Mbit/s) proportional to the declared size.

Also replace the as-unknown-as cast in the test with a real
IncomingMessage backed by an unconnected socket (GEN4).

* Bump upload timeout floor to 2 minutes

* Fix scheduleSeatChange test deadlock with outer CLS test transaction

scheduleSeatChange creates its own internal DB transaction. In the test
environment, every test runs inside a CLS-propagated outer transaction
(for isolation/rollback). When scheduleSeatChange acquires a second
connection and tries to UPDATE the membership row, it waits on the lock
held by the outer connection — a circular wait invisible to PostgreSQL's
deadlock detector, causing the test to hang until timeout.

Fix: add an optional `transaction` parameter to scheduleSeatChange. When
provided, Sequelize uses it as a parent and issues a SAVEPOINT on the
same connection, eliminating the cross-connection lock contention. The
tests capture the outer CLS transaction in beforeEach and pass it in.

[front] Carry over non-recurring contract balances on renewal (#27323)

dust-tt/tasks#8737

Carry the unused balance of non-recurring, contract-level commits/credits
(switch_contract initial credits, awu_purchase top-ups, business_activation
seat prepayment) into the successor contract when a RENEWAL transition ends
the prior one.

Do NOT use Metronome's rollover_fraction: a rolled-over commit becomes a
"rollover" commit, which Metronome burns down before all prepaid commits
regardless of priority ("commit type takes precedence over priority"). Since
these are non-seat-based, that ordering trips the client-level rule that a
non-seat-based commit may not be prioritized over a seat-based one, and the
RENEWAL transition is rejected with a 400.

Instead, carry the balance in the contract.start webhook:

Flag carry-eligible grants with the DUST_CARRY_ON_RENEWAL custom field. Its
value is the grant's original access expiry (ISO). A non-date marker means
"forever". Storing it on the field is necessary because Metronome clamps the
live access window to the contract end at the transition, destroying the
original expiry.
On contract.start, resolve the RENEWAL transition's source contract, read its
flagged commits/credits, derive the unused balance from their expiration
ledger entry, and re-grant each on the successor as a complimentary
(no-invoice) commit / credit at its original priority, products and expiry,
re-stamping the flag so it carries again on the next renewal. A plain prepaid
commit stays in the prepaid burn tier, ordered after the seat allocation by
priority. Expiry rules: in the past -> skip (lapsed); future -> keep it;
non-date marker -> forever.
Register DUST_CARRY_ON_RENEWAL for the commit and contract_credit entities in
metronome_setup.ts.

Note: seat commitents, coupon credits, free-seat per-user credits, recurring credits ARE NOT rolled over.

Customer-level commits/credits are out of scope since they are not coupled to a contract and hence survive contract transitions without custom logic.

[front] add seatType to MembershipInvitation model + migration (#26726)

* fix(streaming): fix GCS write stream leaks and SSE double-unsubscribe

Three distinct leak fixes, no behaviour changes.

1. GCS write streams leaked on upload error paths (utils.ts, processing.ts)
   When parseUploadRequest rejected a file (wrong MIME type, size, empty)
   or threw, the GCS WritableStream passed in was abandoned without
   destroy(). The GCS SDK internally allocates a PassThroughShim and
   wires five event-listener closures on creation; without destroy() these
   are never collected. Fix: call writableStream.destroy() on both error
   paths. Secondary case in processing.ts: writeStream was allocated before
   createReadableFromUrl, so a URL-fetch failure left it orphaned; moved
   allocation inside the try block after the fetch succeeds.

2. SSE generators double-unsubscribed after normal exit (pubsub.ts, mcp_events.ts)
   After a generator exits cleanly (timeout / end-of-stream), finally{}
   correctly calls unsubscribe(). Then res.end() causes the response close
   event to fire -> controller.abort() -> AbortSignal fires -> the still-
   registered signal.addEventListener("abort", unsubscribe) listener fires
   a second time. For multi-subscriber channels this double-decrements
   activeSubscriptionCount, causing the metric to drift negative over time.
   Fix: signal.removeEventListener("abort", unsubscribe) in finally before
   calling unsubscribe(), ensuring exactly one cleanup call per subscription.

test(llm): add request-parity regression suite for legacy vs new router (#27508)

* test(llm): add request-parity regression suite for legacy vs new router

Adds a local-only harness that verifies the new per-endpoint LLM router
(model_constructors, via StreamEndpointTransition) dispatches the same
request to the provider SDK as the legacy per-provider router, for
identical inputs.

Both routers are driven through the public LLM.stream(); the Anthropic
and Vertex SDKs are mocked so each .stream() call records its argument
instead of hitting the network. The captured payloads are compared with
a strict toEqual, minus a documented per-provider allow-list of
intentional differences. Coverage is driven by the DUST_STREAM_ENDPOINTS
registry, so new providers/models are picked up automatically once their
adapter, SDK mock, and normalizer are added.

Gated behind RUN_LLM_TEST like the other LLM suites, so it stays out of
CI. It currently characterizes the remaining legacy<->new divergences
(temperature default, cache TTL/breakpoint placement, reasoning config,
tool_result shape).

* fix(llm): emit automatic cache_control on new Anthropic stream endpoint

The new per-endpoint router was missing the request-level automatic cache
breakpoint the legacy direct-Anthropic path sets, so it lost the auto-cache
behavior. Emit cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" } at stream-input level
(stream-only, like the legacy client), and drop the corresponding allow-list
entry in the parity suite so the match is real rather than masked.

Also addresses parity-suite review feedback:
- reset captures by swapping a fresh holder instead of mutating in place (GEN5)
- run global endpoints only (eu/Vertex is not exercised locally), dropping the
  Vertex legacy branch, capture bucket, and SDK mock
- one-line run command in the header for easy copy-paste

fix(front): keep caret in place when pasted URL becomes a preview node (#27598)

When a user pasted a link and kept typing, the async replacement of the
URL with a `dataSourceLink` preview node moved the caret to just after the
inserted node — i.e. before the text already typed past the URL — so
subsequent keystrokes landed in the wrong place and scrambled the input.

`insertContentAt` defaults to `updateSelection: true`. Extract a pure
`remapCaretAfterUrlReplacement` helper that, when the caret was at or after
the replaced range, re-maps it by the document size delta so it stays at
the user's logical typing position. Carets inside/before the URL keep
TipTap's default behavior.

Tests live in a colocated useUrlHandler.test.ts: one covers the bug (caret
stays after typed text), one covers the guard (caret before the URL is not
pulled back). Both were mutation-checked to fail when their target logic is
removed.

fix(front): always allow skipping a pending personal-auth card (#27604)

The inline personal-authentication card (shown in Sessions and conversations
when a tool needs personal OAuth) could leave the user with no way out: while
a connection attempt was in flight, both Connect and Skip were disabled
(both gated on isConnecting). If the OAuth flow never resolved, the card
stayed stuck, the action was never resolved, and later user messages queued
behind it indefinitely.

- Skip is no longer gated on isConnecting (only on isResolving), so the user
  can always abandon a pending or stuck connection attempt regardless of its
  status.
- A cancelledRef guards the post-await branch so skipping mid-connection does
  not later resolve an already-denied action as completed.

The card is shared by Sessions and conversations via BlockedActionsProvider,
so both surfaces are covered. The OAuth popup flow (setupOAuthConnection) is
left untouched. Adds tests for the always-skippable behavior and the
skip-mid-connection race.

knows whether imgproxy or ConvertAPI does the work. A getImageConverter

leaky: every caller supplied both even though each provider uses only

removed, its converter and the else branch go with it.

ImageConverter declares both resizeFromUrl and resizeFromStream; each
provider overrides only the mode it supports (imgproxy URL, ConvertAPI
stream) and inherits a throwing default for the other. getImageConverter
picks the provider from the flag, and images.ts branches on the same
flag to call the matching method. resizeFromStream and the else branch

fix(llm): default reasoning effort to the model default instead of "none" (#27783)

The base LLM constructor hardcoded "none" when callers omitted reasoningEffort,
conflating "unspecified" with "explicitly none". Models such as gpt-5-mini do
not support "none" and reject the request with a ZodError. Every utility caller
going through runMultiActionsAgent / getStreamLLM and getBatchLLM omits the
effort, so they all crashed on those models.

Fall back to the model's own defaultReasoningEffort when unspecified.

feat(llm): add TogetherAI Llama 3.3 70B Instruct Turbo to the new LLM router (#27779)

* feat(llm): add TogetherAI Llama 3.3 70B Instruct Turbo to the new LLM router

Adds the first TogetherAI endpoint on top of the provider plumbing: the model
id, the model-config mixin (131k context, non-reasoning), the stream endpoint
class (global region, $1.04/1M in & out), and the Dust wrapper, registered in
both the model_constructors and lib/llms stream registries.

Also keeps `none` in the non-reasoning config schema's parsed output (instead of
transforming it away) so the Dust layer can read it as defaultReasoningEffort;
the converter still omits `reasoning_effort` for `none`, so the request is
unchanged.

Characterized against the live TogetherAI API with the integration harness
(40 cases): only `none`/default reasoning is accepted, every other effort is
rejected by the schema; tool calls, forced tools, JSON-schema output, and
instruction-following all pass.

* feat(llm): add TogetherAI router parity coverage for Llama 3.3 70B

The router parity regression test drives every registered stream endpoint
through both the legacy and the new router and compares the dispatched SDK
request, so a new endpoint needs a legacy counterpart + a parity adapter.

- add the legacy TogetheraiLLM client (OpenAI chat-completions to
  api.together.xyz, mirroring the Fireworks client) and its whitelist, with the
  non-reasoning Llama model forcing reasoning effort to none
- register the togetherai parity adapter (reusing the openai_chat capture
  bucket) and a test credential

Also make the non-reasoning config schema degrade any reasoning effort to no
reasoning instead of rejecting it. The parity matrix feeds light/medium/high to
every endpoint; rejecting them made the new router emit no request and broke
parity. Degrading matches the legacy client (which forces effort to none), so
both routers dispatch an identical request with no reasoning_effort. The
endpoint integration test is updated accordingly (every effort now succeeds,
and the r-low reasoning case expects no reasoning).

fix(analytics): exclude unbilled message statuses from credit sums (#27810)

The analyst agent and analytics-page credit views summed cost.full_awu while
excluding free origins to mirror the billed scope, but never filtered on billed
message status. Failed messages carry a non-zero cost.full_awu in the index yet
are never billed by Metronome (failed is not in AGENT_MESSAGE_STATUSES_TO_TRACK),
so the displayed credits over-counted failed runs (e.g. failed triggers) and
diverged from Metronome.

Add the status filter to buildCreditsScopeQuery (covers the analyst agent,
the credit dashboard, and the per-agent/per-user credit tables) and to the
overview agent cost stats. For the CSV exports, wrap only the credits sum in a
status filter sub-aggregation so the count metrics stay inclusive of all
activity while credits match the billed scope.

[front] Fix members-usage pagination latency: cached billing period +… (#27762)

* [front] Fix members-usage pagination latency: cached billing period + day-granularity usage queries

Every page of the members-usage table was a guaranteed cache miss on
per-user usage, which then (1) re-fetched the Metronome contract live
instead of reusing the existing no-TTL contract cache, and (2) queried
HOUR-granularity usage buckets across the entire billing period instead
of just the partial boundary days, forcing the Metronome SDK through far
more paginated API calls. Both combined to make the endpoint take ~15s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [front] Address BACK7: use ConcurrentExecutor for segmented usage queries

segments.map(...) inside Promise.all was a Promise.all over a
dynamic-length array, even though it's bounded to at most 3 in
practice. Switch to ConcurrentExecutor per BACK7.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [front] Remove uncached getMetronomeCurrentBillingPeriod, fix staleness risk

Per review: collapse to a single getCachedMetronomeCurrentBillingPeriod
entry point instead of keeping both a cached and uncached version.

The previous "cached" version reused the no-TTL active-contract cache
(getActiveContract), which is only invalidated on contract
start/end/edit events — not on billing period rollover. A workspace
whose contract went unedited across a period boundary would keep
reading a stale (expired) period indefinitely. Give billing-period
lookups their own 60s TTL cache instead, matching the pattern already
used for seat data and per-user usage in this same area.

Migrated the three remaining callers of the old uncached function
(reinforcement billing, programmatic AWU spend, the debug script) to
the new workspaceId-based cached function, and extracted the
workspace -> {customerId, contractId} resolution out of
fetchActiveContract into a shared resolveActiveMetronomeIds helper so
it isn't duplicated.

Gemini 3 has no `ThinkingLevel.NONE`, so the new google_genai converter
had no way to express the legacy "minimal thinking, hidden thoughts"
floor. Map `none` to `{ thinkingBudget: 128, includeThoughts: false }`,
matching the legacy `POST_GEMINI_3_THINKING_CONFIG_MAPPING`, and re-add

google_ai_studio flash-lite endpoint to parity with the legacy router.

feat(llm): add Gemini-on-Vertex stream client and endpoints (#27836)

Add the agent-platform (Vertex AI) Google stream client and the three
`google_ai_studio/agent-platform/eu` Gemini endpoints (3.1-flash-lite,
3.1-pro, 3.5-flash) with their live integration tests, for parity with
the legacy GoogleLLM Vertex path. The client constructs `GoogleGenAI`
with `{ vertexai: true, project, location: "global" }` and reuses the
existing google_genai converters and model-config mixins unchanged.

`location` must be "global": the native generateContent API does not
serve the `eu` multi-region alias (unlike Anthropic's rawPredict partner
API), and Gemini 3.x preview models are not published to europe-west1.
The legacy router passes no location, which the SDK defaults to
"global" — so this is exact parity, with `region: "eu"` kept as the
Dust-facing residency label.

[Microsoft] Don't silently drop subtrees on transient 404 during enumeration (#28009)

A 404 raised while listing a drive/folder's /children was treated as "node
deleted upstream": syncFiles returned no children, the workflow marked the node
as seen, and the whole subtree was silently dropped with no recovery on re-sync.
Microsoft Graph returns transient itemNotFound on /children enumeration, so a
momentary blip caused permanent, invisible data loss (files in an accessible
folder missing, no admin-facing error).

Disambiguate a bare 404 by doing a lightweight direct GET on the parent node
(mirroring the existing existence-check pattern): if it is genuinely gone, skip
gracefully as before; if it still exists, the 404 was transient so rethrow and
let Temporal retry instead of losing the subtree. isSiteNotFoundError (host
gone) keeps skipping directly.

Fix blank-line/blank-list-item artifacts in suggestion diff preview (#27989) The suggestion diff preview rendered spurious blank lines and blank list items: swapping a straight apostrophe for a curly one added a phantom line, and editing a list item rendered an empty row before the change. The accepted content was always correct — this was purely a decoration rendering artifact. Root cause: diffBlockContent() returns change ranges in the block's full content space, which includes the open/close tokens of nested blocks (paragraphs, list items). buildBlockDecorations then cut newNode at those positions and serialized the result, so an inline-level change inside a block-with-block-children got re-wrapped in its containing

/

  • and rendered inline as a phantom block. Fix interactive stdin in sandbox_exec.ts (#28080)

In the interactive PTY path, `stdin.setEncoding("utf8")` made the `data`
event emit strings, but the handler treated `data` as a Buffer and called
`new Uint8Array(data)`. `new Uint8Array(<string>)` yields an empty array,
so every keystroke was sent to the PTY as zero bytes — the shell appeared
alive but typing had no effect.

Remove the `setEncoding` call so `data` arrives as a Buffer (correct for
raw mode), letting `new Uint8Array(data)` produce the right bytes.

[front] Per-step credit gate: stop agent loop as retryable credits_exhausted failure (Stage 1) (#27683)

* [front] Per-step pool spend-limit gate, stop as retryable failure (Stage 1)

Adds a per-step credit gate to the agent loop. After each step, for
credit-priced (Metronome) workspaces, checkCreditsActivity reads the
60s-cached AWU pool balance and subtracts this message's local run usage
so far; when the pool would be exhausted it stops the message as a
RETRYABLE `credits_exhausted` failure, reusing the existing Retry button
and ReachedLimitPopup. No new status, schema, or streaming event.

Fails open like the rest of the pool/credit-balance helpers: a
non-credit-priced/legacy plan or an unreadable balance yields "don't
stop"; genuine infra exceptions propagate rather than being swallowed.
To support that, fetchPoolCredits now returns `number | null` (null =
unreadable) instead of a fail-open `1` sentinel, so the arithmetic gate
can tell "couldn't read" from a real zero.

Deliberately the simplest viable step. This is Stage 1 of a multi-step
effort (dust-tt/tasks#8715); the final goal is a resumable pause, with
later PRs evolving this interim failure model toward it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [front] Address review: credit stop finalized via its own flag + finalize

Mirrors the graceful-stop shape instead of breaking into the success
path: the per-step gate (checkCreditsActivity / checkPoolCreditGate) is
now a pure decision returning {shouldStop, reason} and publishes nothing.
The workflow sets a creditStopRequested flag and routes to a dedicated
finalizeCreditStoppedAgentLoopActivity, which publishes the retryable
credits_exhausted error (admin/member wording) and runs the failed-message
side-effects. This stops the success finalizer (completion email,
success analytics) from running on a credit-stopped message, and keeps
the gate activity side-effect-free so it's safe to retry. The publish is
single-shot-guarded, so a finalize retry can't double-publish.

Also documents the two accepted v1 limitations in computeLocalRunUsageAwu:
LLM-only AWU (tool AWU not counted) and the O(steps^2) re-sum.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [front] Credit gate: count tool AWU too; move finalize detail to common.ts

The local-spend subtraction now uses computeAgentMessageCredits (LLM run
usage + tool actions, same function the finalizer bills with) instead of
LLM-only AWU, so the gate's subtraction matches what the pool is actually
charged. Threads agentMessageModelId (to fetch this message's MCP actions)
and isFreeUsage (free-origin messages cost 0 against the pool, same as
billing).

Structural: moves the credit-stop event/detail logic into
activities/common.ts as finalizeCreditStop, mirroring finalizeGracefulStop
exactly (getAgentLoopData -> soft-delete guard -> step from contents ->
publish). finalizeCreditStoppedAgentLoopActivity in finalize.ts is now
thin (calls finalizeCreditStop, then runs side-effects), matching every
other finalize activity's shape. Drops the explicit reason/step threading
through the workflow since the common helper computes step itself.

Also fixes the dust-agent bot's GEN4 comments (non-type-safe `as` in test
mocks) by removing the avoidable LightWorkspaceType cast and documenting
why the Authenticator instance casts remain (consistent with the rest of
the test suite, which can't construct a class instance structurally).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [front] Credit gate: drop Metronome reads, reuse existing block-state checks

Per PR discussion (tdraier/remy): keep Metronome out of the agent loop
entirely. The per-step gate now re-checks the exact same Redis-cached,
DB-backed state already evaluated once before the message was sent
(isUserBlocked / isApiBlocked for pool depletion and per-user cap,
isProgrammaticApiBlocked for the monthly programmatic cap) instead of
reading a live/cached Metronome balance and subtracting this message's
local AWU spend.

This drops computeAgentMessageCredits, getCachedPoolCredits, and the
local LLM/tool usage computation entirely, along with the params that
only existed to support them. The activity no longer loads the agent
message or conversation at all -- it just resolves auth and forwards
userMessageOrigin.

Accepted tradeoff (per team agreement): an expensive multi-step message
can still exceed a cap before the state it last read catches up, since
there's no live signal of this message's own in-flight spend. Team is
monitoring actual overage amounts and will revisit if it proves to be a
real problem, rather than building the per-step-emission machinery now.

dsbx function: drop privileges via runuser (remove all unsafe) (#28174)

* refactor(dsbx): drop function privileges via runuser, removing all unsafe

Replaces the unsafe privilege-drop (libc getpwuid/getgrouplist + a pre_exec
setgroups/setgid/setuid block) with a fully-safe approach: when dsbx runs as
root, the function is executed via `runuser -u agent-proxied -- bun ...`, which
resolves that user's uid/primary gid/supplementary groups and drops privileges
before exec. No unsafe, no FFI, no fork/exec hooks.

- running_as_root() uses rustix::process::geteuid().is_root() (safe) — rustix
  was already in the tree via tempfile; enable its "process" feature.
- Bundles can be root-only, so dsbx (still root) stages the bundle into a temp
  dir and makes it + the runner world-readable (0644/0755) instead of chowning,
  so the dropped child can read them without a uid lookup. Contents aren't
  secret (runner is embedded; bundle is the function) and temp names are random.
- The code is no longer cfg(linux)-only and has no libc usage, so it compiles
  and is testable on macOS dev too.

Addresses the "no way around the unsafes?" review on #28088.
Requires `runuser` (util-linux) in the sandbox image, which the apt-based image
provides.

fix(llm): correct new-router OpenAI reasoning replay (#28139)

* fix(llm): correct new-router OpenAI reasoning round-trip

Under use_new_llm_router, gpt-5.5 failed with "400 Invalid 'input[N].id':
string too long ... length 4044". Two bugs in the new router's reasoning
round-trip; this fixes both.

Reasoning replay state is persisted as top-level { id, encrypted_content }
(the old router's shape). The new router carries it nested under
metadata.content and bridges to/from that shape in transitionLLM.

Read side (the 400): on replay, `signature` was filled with the
encrypted_content blob for every provider, and the OpenAI converter uses
`signature` as the item id (64-char max). Now branches on provider: OpenAI
puts the short id in `signature` and the blob in a new `encryptedContent`
field; Anthropic/Gemini keep their signature in `signature` as before.

Write side (silent loss): the old-event bridges only lifted
content.signature to top-level encrypted_content. OpenAI emits
content.{id, encryptedContent}, so its reasoning persisted with neither key
and was dropped on replay. New shared reasoningContentToLegacyMetadata helper
writes the old-router shape, used by both the streaming and batch bridges.

fix(tools): ensure generated tool names start with a letter or underscore (#28212)

Tool names are generated by slugifying `<server>__<tool>`, and slugify can
produce a leading digit (e.g. "1Password" -> "1password__get_item"). Gemini
requires function names to start with a letter or an underscore, and

with a 400. Prefix an underscore when the generated name does not start with a
letter or underscore so the name is valid across providers.

functionCall, so fixing it at the source keeps request/response names
consistent and covers both the old and new LLM routers.

fix(agent-loop): treat already-running parent as no-op in ancestor resume (#28219)

Ticket: https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/9115

In a parallel run_agent fan-out, sibling children completing near
simultaneously each try to relaunch the parent's agent loop. Only one
wins the race to start the workflow, the others get
agent_loop_already_running. resumeAncestorConversations treated this as
fatal and aborted the whole ancestor walk, so the losing child never
resumed the chain and the parent stalled in "Thinking..." with no error
surfaced to the user.

Treat agent_loop_already_running as a benign no-op for starting that one
parent, but keep walking up the chain. Ancestor resumption is driven
per-sibling from the request handler (validate_actions /
resolve_authentication), not by the parent workflow, so each sibling must
still attempt every higher ancestor. Stopping at the already-running
parent could strand the grandparent if the sibling that won the race fails
before reaching it. Other errors still abort as before. Scoped to the
ancestor-resume path so the front-api retry endpoint keeps surfacing the
error as a 400.

[front] API key credit cap: debounced reconcile after agent loop (#28176)

Per-key cap enforcement is pull-based (Metronome spend alerts can't attribute
spend by `api_key_name`). Instead of reconciling inline right after
`ingestMetronomeEvents` (too soon — Metronome hasn't ingested the usage yet),
the Metronome usage activity now launches a debounced reconcile workflow when
the request used a capped, non-system key:

- `reconcileApiKeyCreditStateWorkflow` (usage_queue) debounces 15s via

  bursts on the same key into one run.
- `reconcileApiKeyCreditStateActivity` re-checks workspace/contract/cap at run
  time and calls `reconcileApiKey` (live usage vs cap → flips `creditState`).

Gives Metronome time to ingest before reading usage. Best-effort throughout.

fix(front): classify Anthropic mid-stream errors like the old router (#28255)

The new LLM router streams via the Anthropic SDK's `messages.stream()`
helper, whose `MessageStream.#handleError` rewraps any non-`AnthropicError`
failure thrown while reading the SSE body (socket reset, premature close,
undici "terminated") into a bare `AnthropicError`. `APIConnectionError` is
only constructed at the connect/headers phase, never mid-body, so these bare
errors matched none of `classifyStreamError`'s cases and fell through to a
terminal, non-retryable `unknown_error` ("Unknown error from Anthropic").

The old router (`lib/api/llm`) classified the same failures via
`categorizeLLMError`'s substring matching and kept them retryable, so they
were silently retried and never surfaced. Since the `use_new_llm_router`
rollout these turned into user-visible terminal errors across sonnet/opus/
haiku.

Restore parity with the old router:
- `apiErrorToErrorEvent` defaults a missing HTTP status to 500, mirroring
  `categorizeAnthropicError`'s `status ?? 500`, so statusless mid-stream SSE
  error events map to a retryable `server_error`.
- New `bareStreamErrorToErrorEvent` ports `categorizeLLMError`'s substring
  classification to the new `ErrorType` union, keeping transient stream/
  connection failures retryable instead of terminal.

fix(teams): list_messages pagination, createdDateTime range, and tool description (#28173)

* fix(teams): correct list_messages pagination and reduce over-fetch

The list_messages pagination decided whether to keep paging based on
whether the oldest message on the current page fell inside the date
range. Since Graph returns messages newest-first, a toDate in the past
meant the first page was entirely newer than the window, the in-range
set was empty, and pagination stopped immediately — historical messages
were never fetched.

Continuation now keys off whether the oldest message on the page is
still >= fromDate (with no lower bound, page until the message limit),
so we walk back through history correctly.

Also:
- Push the date range server-side via $filter + $orderby on the chat
  endpoint (channels support neither), eliminating the now->toDate
  over-fetch. Bounds are nudged 1ms outward so the exclusive server
  filter stays a superset of the inclusive client-side filter, which
  remains authoritative.
- Cap pagination at MAX_PAGES_TO_FETCH and warn on truncation, bounding
  the channel walk that has no server-side filtering.
- Validate fromDate/toDate and guard against empty pages.

* fix(teams): replace silent page cap with transparent scan backstop

The earlier page cap (50 pages) could silently truncate the channel
walk, which is exactly the deep-history date-range retrieval the tool
is most used for — returning partial results with no signal to the
caller.

Replace it with a high scanned-messages backstop (MAX_MESSAGES_TO_SCAN)
that only guards against runaway loops / Graph throttling on very large
channels, and surface truncation in the tool output so an agent can
narrow the range instead of treating partial history as complete. The
result-size guard (MAX_NUMBER_OF_MESSAGES) remains the primary ceiling
on returned messages.

* fix(teams): range on createdDateTime; extract + test pagination logic

Two things in one pass.

Correctness: list_messages ranged on lastModifiedDateTime, so a message
sent inside the window but edited/reacted-to later (which bumps
lastModifiedDateTime) was dropped, and an old message edited inside the
window was wrongly pulled in. "Messages between April and May" means
sent then — range on createdDateTime instead, in all three places: the
client-side filter, the chat server-side $filter/$orderby, and the stop
condition.

Graph only supports the `lt` operator on createdDateTime (no `gt`), so
only the upper (toDate) bound is pushed server-side — which is the bound
that caused the over-fetch anyway; the lower bound stays the client-side
walk. The stop condition compares the field that actually orders the
pages (createdDateTime for chat listings, lastModifiedDateTime for
channels, which cannot be reordered), not the filter field.

Review follow-ups: extract the stopping logic into a pure, unit-tested
shouldContinuePagination helper (pagination.ts) with the page-size and
scan-backstop constants; surface result-size truncation to the caller
the same way the scan backstop already does; fix a stale comment and an
en-dash in model-facing copy.

* chore(teams): review follow-ups for list_messages

- Drop the dead `field` arg from the test `page()` helper; both
  timestamps were always equal, so it implied coverage the suite didn't
  have. The created-vs-modified distinction is exercised by the inline
  "compares the ordering field" case.
- Reword the result-limit note to drop the ordering claim ("showing 200
  of them") since channel results are ordered by lastModifiedDateTime,
  not the createdDateTime we range on.
- Soften the replies-endpoint comment: we skip server-side filters there
  conservatively, its filterability isn't documented.

* fix(teams): note messageId is channels-only in list_messages metadata

Agents were passing messageId on chats, where it has no meaning — it
addresses a top-level channel message to fetch its thread replies. Make
the constraint explicit in both the tool description and the messageId
field describe so the model stops generating those calls.

* chore(teams): trim list_messages comments

Cut pure 'what' comments, de-duplicate the ordering-field rationale (now
stated once on MessageOrderingField), and tighten the long blocks. The
Graph-API invariants (lt-only createdDateTime, $filter needs matching
$orderby, reply-chain ordering) are kept.

feat: bubble up ask_user_question for sub-agents (#28256)

When an agent spawns a sub-agent via run_agent, the sub-agent's
ask_user_question never surfaced in the parent conversation, so the user
couldn't answer and the run stalled. Tool approvals and auth requests
already bubbled up; questions fell out of that chain at a few spots.

- collect tool_ask_user_question into the run_agent blocking-event loop
  and route it to the parent channel via pubsubMessageId
- stamp isLastBlockingEventForStep on the deferred question event (auth
  events had it, questions didn't) so the parent finalizes the step
- on answer, resume both the child run and the blocked parent run_agent
  via the existing FE retryHandler (retryHandlerWithResetState), the same
  two-call path file authorization already uses — the child retry no-ops
  once the answer is registered, the parent retry relaunches the run
- submit the answer to the child conversation ids carried by the blocked
  action rather than the parent props

fix(conversation): stop duplicated inline activity steps on Temporal retries (#28351)

In a streaming agent turn, the inline "Thinking / activity" steps could be
rendered dozens of times within a single turn, flooding the conversation view
(tasks#9287, tasks#8022). The duplication only appeared while the turn was
streaming and disappeared once it completed. A hard refresh mid-stream did not
help.

An agent turn runs as a Temporal loop of steps (`agentLoopWorkflow`). Each step
is one `runModelAndCreateActionsActivity` (the LLM call, emitting
`generation_tokens` for chain-of-thought/text and `tool_params` for tool calls)
followed by `runToolActivity`. The model activity is configured with
`maximumAttempts: 5`, so on a transient failure (rate limit, retryable model
error, worker restart, ...) Temporal re-runs the whole step's model call.

Every emitted event takes two paths:
  - Redis stream (`stream:message-<sId>`): append-only log, tagged with its
    `step`, replayed to the client over SSE. Retried attempts are appended as
    brand-new entries.
  - DB step content (`AgentStepContentResource.createNewVersion`): versioned per
    (step, index), latest-wins. A retry overwrites the previous version.

While streaming, the client (`useAgentMessageStream`) rebuilds the timeline by
reducing the Redis event stream into `inlineActivitySteps` (append-based). Once
the turn ends, it replaces that array wholesale with the server-rendered
`contentView`, which is computed from the collapsed DB step content, which is
why the bug self-healed at "Done" and why reload was always clean.

The client reducer could not absorb a retry's re-emitted events:
  - `seenEventIds` only drops exact stream-id replays. Retried events have new
    ids.
  - `appendThinkingStep` deduped only against the most-recent thinking step
    `appendContentStep` did not dedupe at all
  - `retryCoTBuffer` only suppressed an *in-progress* (unflushed) CoT. Once a
    segment had been flushed into the timeline (because a tool call followed),
    the retry re-appended it.

So each of the up-to-5 attempts piled its steps on top of the previous ones,
and a fresh mount mid-stream replayed the same log and rebuilt the same
duplicates.

Mirror the server's per-step, latest-wins semantics in the live reducer:

  - Tag every inline activity step with the agent-loop `step` that produced it
    (`InlineActivityStep.step`, set both client-side and in the server builder).
  - Track `currentStep` (advanced only by `generation_tokens`, the only events
    that fill the CoT/text buffer).
  - When a `generation_tokens` CoT event arrives with a fresh `traceId` on the
    SAME step (a new step also gets a fresh traceId, but its step number
    advances), treat it as a Temporal retry: drop the inline steps already
    committed for that step and rebuild them from the retry's events. This
    generalizes the old `retryCoTBuffer` beyond the unflushed case. The buffer
    is kept only to de-flicker the active CoT.

Note: useChildAgentStream has the same Temporal-retry duplication, but is
out of scope for tasks#9287 which targets the main conversation view.
Will be done in a follow-up PR. Added a TODO comment about it.

fix(llm): don't route regionally-unavailable Anthropic models to Vertex (#28454)

The legacy LLM router routed all Vertex-whitelisted Anthropic models to
regional (EU) Vertex based only on the deployment region, credit pricing,
and Vertex-whitelist membership -- it never consulted the model's
`regionalAvailability`. On an `europe-west1` deployment this sent models
with no EU Vertex quota (e.g. Claude Sonnet 5, `europe-west1: false`) to a
non-existent EU deployment, failing the request.

Gate `useVertex` on the model being regionally available in the current
region, so a model without regional quota falls back to the direct
Anthropic API (the same global endpoint the new router selects). Sonnet
4.6 and other EU-available models are unaffected.

stuck/crashing boot died:

  before instrumentation and the app graph (only depends on pino).
- "front-api instrumentation initialized" — end of instrumentation-config.ts.

- "front-api server listening" — existing.

fix(labs-transcripts): don't delete retrieval schedule on transient errors (#28480)

Ticket: https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/9004

Meeting Transcript Processing silently stops for users when a transient
error deletes their Temporal retrieval schedule with no auto-recovery.
A Temporal schedule keeps firing regardless of whether individual runs
fail, so the only reason a momentary failure becomes permanent is the
explicit stopRetrieveTranscriptsWorkflow() teardown.

This PR removes the teardown from the two every-5-min external-call paths:

- getTranscriptsGoogleAuth: only tear down when the token is genuinely
  revoked (token_revoked_error). Transient OAuth/network errors now throw
  without deleting the schedule, which self-heals on the next tick.
- retrieveNewTranscriptsActivity: the Drive files.list failure path no
  longer deletes the schedule. It fails the run (schedule survives).

Also adds two read-only admin diagnostics for on-call:
- check_transcripts_connections.ts: per-config token validity, scope,
  history recency, and live-schedule status, bucketed in a summary.
- check_transcripts_pending.ts: previews the retrieval query (Drive
  listing + history dedup, no processing) to count transcripts a config
  would pick up on its next run.

fix(labs-transcripts): skip file instead of deleting schedule on config drift (#28562)

Follow-up to https://github.com/dust-tt/dust/pull/28480.

processTranscriptActivity deleted the whole retrieval schedule when a single
file could not be stored or processed (missing data source view, no write
permission, missing data source, missing/archived agent). A transient
permission/fetch blip or a since-removed resource would therefore permanently
disable processing for the user with no auto-recovery. Replace the six per-file
`stopRetrieveTranscriptsWorkflow() + return` blocks with a plain `return` (skip
this file, log it). The schedule survives, so the file is retried on the next
tick and recovers on its own once the underlying config issue is resolved. Logs
updated from "Stopping." to "Skipping file." to match the new behavior. The
remaining teardown calls (workspace/user/config not found) are left as-is: those
reflect a genuinely orphaned config and are out of scope for this fix.

fix(wakeups): delete cron schedule when a wake-up is cancelled at fire time (#28607)

When runWakeUpActivity hit a terminal condition (conversation gone/inaccessible,
or agent_configuration_not_found / agent_inaccessible / model_disabled) it called
markCancelled(), which only flips the DB row. For cron wake-ups the backing
Temporal schedule was never deleted, so Temporal kept spawning daily workflows
that no-op forever (until the maxFires cap).

The fire-time terminal paths now cancel the wake-up AND delete its cron schedule
via cleanupTemporalScheduleIfCronTerminal (generalized from the former
cleanupTemporalIfCronExpired to also cover the cancelled state). We deliberately
do not use cancel() here: for one-shot wake-ups that would cancel the very
workflow this activity runs in. Deleting the cron schedule is safe from within a
scheduled run.

Remove redundant delta dedup pass in Microsoft connector (#28656)

`fetchDeltaForRootNodesInDrive` and the legacy `syncDeltaForRootNodesInDrive`
both ran `removeAllButLastOccurences(results)` on the delta results. But
`results` always comes from `getFullDeltaResults`, which already dedups by id
(last write wins) via its item map. The extra pass therefore only rebuilt the
array (plus a Set) and reversed the order.

For large deltas this meant an additional full in-memory copy of the delta set
on a shared worker that already runs close to its memory limit, contributing to
OOM pressure. Drop the redundant pass and alias `results` directly. Downstream
(`sortForIncrementalUpdate`, `scrubRemovedFolders`) re-orders topologically and
only reads the list, so the removed reversal has no effect on correctness.

fix(front): let unstick plugin force-unlock multi-step blocked conversations (#28678)

* fix(front): let unstick plugin force-unlock multi-step blocked conversations

The Unstick Conversation poke plugin failed with
`plugin_execution_failed: All blocked actions must be from the same step`
on exactly the conversations it is meant to rescue.

updateAgentMessageWithFinalStatus("failed") calls
denyBlockedActionsForAgentMessage, which reused
listBlockedActionsForAgentMessage and inherited its
assert(uniqueSteps.length === 1). When a stuck message has blocked
actions spanning several steps, the assert throws and rolls back the
whole finalize, so the conversation stays stuck.

Split out a non-asserting fetch used by the terminal deny path so it
denies blocked actions across all steps. The resume paths (retry,
sandbox child relaunch) keep the asserting method: they need a single
unambiguous step to resume the agent loop from. Log the anomaly when we
actually see it so we can chase the root cause.

* chore(front): trim verbose comments

* refactor(front): make unstick a force flag instead of relaxing deny globally

Rework the fix so the single-step invariant stays enforced by default and
only the unstick plugin bypasses it. Add a `force` option to
updateAgentMessageWithFinalStatus (threaded to
denyBlockedActionsForAgentMessage): without it the deny path enforces the
single-step invariant and throws on a violation, surfacing the bug; with
it (unstick plugin only) it skips the check and logs the anomaly so a
genuinely stuck conversation can still be finalized.

* refactor(front): merge force path into listBlockedActionsForAgentMessage

* fix(front): clean requestedSpaceIds on all skills referencing a deleted space

When a space is deleted, affected skills were discovered only through the MCP
server views / data source views located in the space. A skill can reference a
space via requestedSpaceIds without holding a live view in it, so those skills
were never cleaned. Since an agent's requestedSpaceIds is recomputed as the union
of its capabilities plus each attached skill's requestedSpaceIds, the stale space
persisted on the skill and got re-applied to agents on the next recompute — even
after the agent rows were stripped at delete time. The result was skills and
agents left referencing a now-deleted space, making them invisible to everyone.

- Also discover skills directly by requestedSpaceIds (new
  SkillResource.listByRequestedSpaceId), mirroring the agent lookup.
- Strip agents with a fresh in-transaction query after the skill loop instead of
  a snapshot taken before it, so agents changed during skill cleanup are caught.
- Add a migration to strip a given space id from every requestedSpaceIds column
  (agent_configurations, skill_configurations, skill_versions) to repair rows
  already affected.

refactor(mcp): narrow tool handler context to runContext (#28761)

* refactor(mcp): narrow tool handler context to runContext

ToolHandlerExtra previously carried the full ToolContextType union (runContext |
listToolsContext), but tool handlers only ever execute on a connection established with a run
context; the listing phase registers handlers without invoking them. Handlers therefore carried
dead optional chaining and unreachable listToolsContext fallbacks.

Introduce ToolRunContextType (AgentLoopRunContextType | SandboxFunctionRunContextType) and make
ToolHandlerExtra carry a non-optional runContext. registerTool becomes the narrowing boundary:
createServer factories keep receiving ToolContextType (dynamic servers still need both phases to
register tools), and the run context is asserted and extracted when a handler actually fires.

This removes dead code the union invited: unreachable listToolsContext fallbacks
(set_conversation_title), "no context" error branches (jira, gmail, microsoft_drive,
web_search_browse, toolsets), and a dead connectionId fallback (google_drive). Helpers that
legitimately take ToolContextType are unchanged; handler call sites pass { runContext }.

Also fixes test fakes whose as-casts hid the shape change from the compiler (files, sandbox,
skill_management, mcp_actions search mock).
