Pod functions can no longer run (#32216)

Every .invoke() entry point already resolved Frames only, so the pod half of the execution path was unreachable. This makes that explicit and takes the pod ownership out of SandboxFunctionResource with it.

Execution is Frame-only: the pod branch of SandboxFunctionInvocationResource.execute and of invoke() refuse up front, and authorizeSandboxFunctionInvocation and the invocation token lose their "pod" owner. pod_member_required stays -- it gates on the Pod a Frame runs in, which is still a real thing.

The fast-function self-heal goes. It was Pod-only twice over: the route branched on frameId and returned "republish the Frame", and the helper itself refused with "Refusing to mutate an immutable Frame publication function". It cannot carry over, because a Frame function's executionMode is declared in its manifest, so a row-level heal would be reverted by the author's next publish. makeDurable, its only caller, goes too.

SandboxFunctionResource drops makeNew, listBySpace, deleteAllForSpace, the space getter and baseFetch's space hydration with its three flags. delete() now refuses: a Frame function's row belongs to its Frame's publication history, and FileResource already cascades the set.

One fix rather than a deletion. Removing sandboxFunction.space forced six live call sites off pod ownership -- tool outputs, generate_file, upserted files, the pod_manager tools, audit metadata and the invocation log context. Those were already broken for Frame functions: the getter asserts on a null owner space, so any Frame function whose tool wrote a file threw. The Pod is now resolved once from the Frame's own scope when the tool run context is built, and a Frame outside any Pod gets a clear refusal.

Remove the pod sandbox owner kind (#32217)

Conversation and Frame are the only owner kinds left. With the pod consumers gone from the earlier commits, the owner itself can go.

PodSandboxAdapter, ensurePodSandboxReady, the pod sandbox-only mounts (published bundles, litestream state replica) with their GCS prefixes and mount profile, and DustFileSystem.forPodSandboxProvisioning.

The "pod" arm of SandboxRuntimeOwner, which is what removes SPACE_ID: from the owner env vars, from the env manifest, from the reserved-name set in SandboxResource, and from the Fluent Bit enrichment, which now tags FRAME_ID instead. sandboxOwnerHasPersistentState loses its pod case; Frames still have durable state.

The reaper's pod branch: its owner kind, its auth map and its adapter wiring. Its requireRunning suite moves to the Frame adapter, the other owner that passes the flag through.

buildPodScopedEnvVars moves to SandboxEnvVarResource.loadPodScopedEnv, because its owner adapter is going and the two remaining adapters still need it: pod-scoped env vars, HTTPS secrets and egress policy still apply to every conversation and Frame sandbox running inside a Pod. That, and Pod file mounts, are deliberately untouched.

scripts/ensure_pod_sandbox.ts goes; setupPodStateOnColdStart and ensurePodStateHealthOnSleep lose their compat aliases now that nothing calls the Pod-named exports.

deleteLegacyPodOwnedSandbox is what is left to reach a pod-owned sandbox that already exists. Pod deletion calls it, since with no owner adapter the reaper skips such a sandbox forever and it would sit running at the provider. The next commit adds the backfill that drains them.

Check Frame function calls at publish validation (#32282)

* Check Frame function calls at publish validation

`dsbx frame validate` now reports UI code that calls a function the Frame's
manifest does not declare, or that passes an input the function's
`schema.input` rejects. Both otherwise fail only once a viewer triggers the
call, and nothing else type-checks a v2 Frame's UI source: esbuild strips types
without checking them.

Two passes. The reference pass is syntactic, so it can name what went wrong: a
literal that matches no declared function, or a leftover `<podId>/<slug>` Pod
reference, which `resolveFrameFunctionReference` rejects outright for v2.
Computed references are skipped. The input pass builds a virtual TypeScript
program over the Frame's sources with a generated `@dust/react-hooks`
declaration whose hooks map a function name to the input type compiled from its
published JSON Schema, and keeps only the diagnostics anchored inside a call's
input argument.

Warnings, never errors, and the input pass is wrapped: a schema the converter
cannot express must not stand between an author and a publish.

* Block publishing a Frame that calls an undeclared function

A bad function reference was only a validation warning, and `dsbx frame
publish` never runs validation: it goes through `buildAndPublishFramePublication`,
which collects no warnings at all (Tailwind included). So a Frame calling
`usePodFunction("list-todos-bad", {})` published cleanly and shipped a button
that always fails.

References are now checked in `buildFramePublication`, which both the publish
and the validate path share, and a literal that names nothing in the manifest
is a `FramePublicationError`. That is exact rather than heuristic:
`resolveFrameFunctionReference` pins a v2 reference to `<frameId>/<name>`, so a
name outside the manifest cannot resolve for any input or any viewer. The check
is syntactic and runs before the UI build and any sandbox work, so a rejected
publish costs nothing. Computed names are still skipped, so a UI that builds
names at run time stays publishable.

The input check stays a validate-only warning, and its code contract is
narrowed to it: the two differ precisely in that inputs are checked against
JSON Schema derived from Zod contracts, which is heuristic in both directions.

* Drop the Frame function input type-check, keep the reference check

The advisory input check rebuilt a full TypeScript program per validate call and
hand-mirrored the @dust/react-hooks surface. Only the exact undeclared-name check
remains, trimmed to a single syntactic pass. Removes json-schema-to-typescript,
which had no other consumer.

[connectors] fix: skip BigQuery enumeration when nothing is selected (#32271)

* [connectors] fix: skip BigQuery enumeration when nothing is selected

The BigQuery connector sync calls fetchTree on every run, enumerating every
dataset and table of the project even when no permission is selected. On large
warehouses this ran ~14h (observed on a 100k+ table project) only to sync 0
tables, and re-enumerated from scratch on every deploy.

sync() only creates read-granted ("selected") nodes and cleans up everything
else, so when nothing is selected the tree is irrelevant. Add
hasSelectedRemoteDatabasePermissions() and short-circuit the enumeration in the
BigQuery sync activity, passing an empty tree so cleanup still runs.

* [connectors] fix: address cc-verify findings on BigQuery skip-enumeration

- Make the contract discoverable: move the @cc directive into a /** */ JSDoc
  block so cc-check attaches it to hasSelectedRemoteDatabasePermissions.
- Guard the selection-loss race: a selection saved between the precheck and
  sync()'s findAll would be left unused and destroyed by the empty-tree cleanup,
  and the signaled resync could not recover it. The BigQuery skip path now calls
  sync() with preserveSelectedPermissions: true so a concurrently-saved
  selection is preserved (lastUpsertedAt reset, row kept) and recovered on the
  next resync. Normal (has-selection) path is unchanged.
- Add tests asserting the empty-tree cleanup preserves a selected row when

* [front] Close Gemini requests that would end on a model turn

Gemini rejects a request whose last Content is a model turn with HTTP 400

intermittently on gemini-3.8-flash. Verified against the live API: replaying a
conversation that ends on an assistant turn reproduces the error through our own
endpoint, and appending a user turn makes the identical request return 200.

The agent loop is supposed to always end its payload on a user or tool-result
turn, so reaching this state means an upstream invariant broke and the producer
is not yet identified. Append a minimal user turn so the request succeeds
instead of failing the message, and log the tail's part kinds plus the dropped
provider_passthrough count so the cause can be pinned down from production.

assistant message, but a history whose messages all convert to nothing — a
passthrough-only conversation, since those blocks are dropped here — yields an
empty array and gets no append.

Content. It was the prose that over-promised, by describing the input rather than
the return value. State the guarantee in terms of the returned contents and pin
the empty case with a test, rather than inventing a user turn for a request that
has nothing to answer.

The builder only ever emitted `builder:create_agent:submit`, and only for a
brand-new, non-draft agent: saving an edit emits nothing, changes no URL and
triggers no pageview, so time-to-save on edits is unmeasurable. The skill

Tighten the viz Frame function reference grammar to bare names (#32507)

`isFrameFunctionReference` accepted `<podId>/<slug>` and `<app>__<name>`, forms
the host refuses. `resolveFrameFunctionReference` qualifies a bare manifest name
against the calling Frame's own identity and rejects anything else, so a Frame
using either form passed viz validation and then failed at the RPC boundary.
Both forms are dead from the other end too: `validateFrameFunctionReferences`
fails a publish whose UI passes a literal that is not a declared bare name.

Prod agrees. `sandbox_functions` holds 15,071 rows in US and 25 in EU, none with
an `__` prefix, none outside the bare-name grammar, and every US row belongs to
an `application/vnd.dust.frame.v2+json` file. The oldest row is from the day the
canonical Frame invocation contract landed, so the app-prefix scheme never
shipped data.

`SANDBOX_FUNCTION_SLUG_REGEX` keeps its optional `__` branch: it guards what
enters the slug column and what the sandbox-to-sandbox call routes accept, which
is a separate boundary from the reference a Frame sends. The cross-repo check in
`sandbox_functions.test.ts` therefore asserts containment rather than equality —
every reference viz accepts is a valid slug — plus a second case pinning that
the gap is exactly the retired app prefix.

* feat: preview files in the side panel

Conversation file previews open in the resizable side panel instead of the

* fix: resolve file previews to a single addressing scheme

A file opened from a message carries a file id, one opened from the files
panel carries a sandbox path, and the two endpoints behind them are not
equivalent: only the path one converts Office documents to PDF, so clicking
an xlsx in a conversation rendered "unable to preview".

and let the panel resolve id to path. Both entry points now render from the
same source. Files with no mount path keep the id fallback.

* fix: canonicalize the file path before previewing

Agents write legacy scoped paths in messages (`conversation/report.xlsx`)
while the files panel carries canonical ones (`conversation-{cId}/...`). The
files API only resolves the canonical form, so the same file previewed from a
message failed and from the panel worked.

Drops the scoped path added to the file metadata payload in the previous
commit: it addressed a different case, and none we can point at today.

* fix: drop the node path dependency from scoped path resolution

resolveCanonicalScopedPath is now called from the conversation, and `path` is
a node builtin the SPA bundle does not ship, so `path.posix` was undefined and
every file link an agent rendered crashed the conversation.

A file preview is addressed either by sandbox path or by file id. They were
two same-typed members of OpenPanelParams told apart with an `in` check, and

Also trims the trailing-slash branch of normalizePosixPath (scoped paths never
carry one) and says which of the two failures the panel's empty state means.

Narrow SANDBOX_FUNCTION_SLUG_REGEX to the bare manifest name (#32513)

The regex admitted an optional `<appPrefix>__` half that publish derived from
the app folder a Pod function's source lived in. Nothing can produce one: the
manifest validates a function name as a single segment, and
`createForFramePublication` stores `slug: fn.name`. Prod has no prefixed slug in
either region, and every row belongs to a Frames v2 file.

With the prefix gone, the slug grammar and the manifest name grammar are the
same thing, so they are now one regex rather than two. A declared name, the slug
stored for it, and the reference a Frame sends cannot disagree.

That also empties `lib/api/sandbox_functions/slug.ts`, which existed to derive
and take apart prefixed slugs. `deriveSandboxFunctionSlug` and
`sandboxFunctionNameFromSlug` had only their own tests as callers,
`appPrefixFromSlug` had none at all, and `deriveAppPrefix` survived only in a
comment. Deleted, with its one live export — the `__` separator — inlined into
db_naming.ts, which still needs it: pod databases created under the old scheme
keep prefixed filenames, and `copy_pod_databases_to_frame.ts` strips them.

Pairs with the viz change it stacks on, which stopped Frames sending the wider
form. The cross-repo check in sandbox_functions.test.ts goes back to asserting
equality, now that both sides are the same grammar again.

Drop the pod database prefix derivation (#32514)

* Drop the pod database prefix derivation

`podDatabasePrefixFromSlug` turned a function's slug into the prefix that
namespaced its databases. Slugs no longer carry an app prefix, and the function
had no production caller — only its own test, and a comment in mount_path.ts.
Removing it also empties `podDatabasePrefixFromAppPrefix`, its only caller.

`sandboxDatabaseExecEnvVars` loses its `databasePrefix` parameter for the same
reason: no caller has ever passed it, so `DUST_POD_DATABASE_PREFIX` was already
always empty. The variable is still sent, since the @dust/pod shim reads it and
dropping a name from that ABI would need a runner-first rollout for no gain.

What is left in db_naming.ts is reading the names the old scheme already wrote:
`copy_pod_databases_to_frame.ts` strips those prefixes when moving a pod's
databases to a Frame. The module comment now describes that rather than a
namespacing scheme nothing applies.

* Drop the pod database app prefix entirely

Nothing wrote a prefix any more; this stops reading one. db_naming.ts goes with
it, and `copy_pod_databases_to_frame.ts` copies each replica directory under the
name it already has.

This is a behavior change, accepted deliberately: a pod database still on disk
as `myapp__chat.db` now lands in Frame state as `myapp__chat.db` rather than
`chat.db`, so a Frame declaring `chat` will not find it. Those databases are no
longer worth carrying the mapping for.

Two contracts went with the behavior they described:

- `strip-pod-database-app-prefix` is replaced by `preserve-pod-database-name`,
  which states what the script now does.
- `reject-frame-database-name-collisions` is removed rather than restated. It
  guarded distinct pod names converging on one frame name, which only the
  prefix strip could cause; names are now copied verbatim, so no two sources can
  collide and the check had become unreachable.

`parsePodDatabaseReplicaRelativePath` decided nothing once source and
destination names were the same string, so it is now
`isPodDatabaseReplicaRelativePath` and the caller uses the relative path it
already had.

* Delete the pod-to-frame database copy script

The migration it performed is done, and it was the last thing reading the pod
database layout. Nothing referenced it: no caller, no test, no workflow.

`POD_DATABASE_NAME_REGEX` in types/api/sandbox_functions.ts went with it, since
the script was its only consumer. The identically named constant in
lib/api/sandbox/db.ts is a separate local, and cli/dust-sandbox keeps its own
export, which its tests pin against SANDBOX_DATABASE_NAME_REGEX.

[front] Evict old agent memory entries instead of failing when full (#32531)

Refs https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/10222

Recording or editing agent memory refused any write that would exceed the
16K character limit. Memory never shrinks on its own, so once an agent
saturated, every subsequent run hit the same issue: the model read the error
and what follows is not deterministic: agents can either spent their remaining
steps compacting, abandon the rest of their plan, or continue with the
plan.

Instead of failing, we drop the oldest entries, and return to the agent
the pieces that have been removed from memory.

Note: `user_memory` can probably face the same issue, but is not part of
this PR

[frames] Purge Frame function invocations past a 7-day retention window (#32536)

* [frames] Purge Frame function invocations past a 7-day retention window

Frame function invocations were never deleted: 276k rows (118 MB) and as many GCS
payloads had accumulated in two weeks in US prod, growing ~20k/day.

Adds a daily sweep on the data-retention queue that deletes invocations older than
7 days, whatever their publication, along with their sandbox function MCP actions
and both sets of GCS objects.

The sweep walks the primary key rather than filtering on createdAt: the table has
no index on that column, so a filtered query would scan the whole tail once it
reached the retention boundary.

* Reword the retention contract so Danger's raw-SQL heuristic stops matching prose

* Simplify the Frame invocation retention sweep

Share the MCP-action-then-invocation delete cascade between the per-function
delete and the retention batch, group expired rows with lodash instead of a
hand-rolled Map, and make the retention window a plain constant: nothing set
the env override and a malformed value would have silently disabled the sweep.
Drop the heartbeat that ran after all the work, the redundant schedule option
casts, and the test's private GCS mock in favour of the global fileStorageMock.

[marketing] Launch the UK and US logo lists, point EU-27 at FR (#32633)

* [marketing] Launch the UK customer logo list

Adds UK to LIVE_LOGO_LIST_REGIONS, so the list marketing has built in Contentful
starts rendering for British visitors. FR has been live since 2026-09-14; this
is the first of the remaining markets.

This is the largest visible change of the rollout. Today the UK is served a
bespoke homepage bar (`home-trusted-gb`) and then plain *US* logos on all ten
solutions pages, because `isEUCountry` excludes GB and
`fallbackTrustedByRegion` therefore sends it to the US bar. Both now come from
the one UK list, which is the point of the model: one lineup per audience,
across every page in scope.

Unaffected: every other audience. FR keeps its own list, and US and EU-27 keep
falling through to their hardcoded lineups until their own commits land.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [marketing] Launch the US customer logo list

Adds US to LIVE_LOGO_LIST_REGIONS, so the list marketing has built in Contentful
starts rendering for the US audience.

US is the catch-all region, so this covers more than the United States: every
country not claimed by FR, UK or EU resolves here — Switzerland, Norway, Japan,
Canada, Australia, and any visitor whose country we fail to detect.

The visible change is the smaller one of the two launches. These visitors are
already served the US lineups; what changes is that the homepage and the
solutions pages stop differing. Today they split by two logos (the
Cursor/Kyriba swap between `home-trusted-default` and `trusted-by-default-us`),
which reads as an accident rather than a decision. From here both come from the
one list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [marketing] Serve EU-27 the French logo list until EU has its own

EU is the one audience with no list of its own yet, and leaving it on the
hardcoded fallback would be the worst outcome of the rollout rather than a
neutral one: `fallbackHomeTrustedGeo` returns "default" for EU, so a German or
Spanish visitor gets a homepage bar full of US companies — while FR, UK and US
all now get a lineup chosen for them. The French list is a closer fit for those
visitors than the US one while EU's own is built.

Rather than reroute EU countries in `toLogoListRegion`, which would make the EU
region unreachable and quietly strand any list published for it, this adds an
explicit alias map. `useLogoBar` consults it only when the region itself has no
published list, so EU's own list takes over the moment it is published and
made live — launching EU is adding it to LIVE_LOGO_LIST_REGIONS and deleting
the alias entry, with no change to the resolution logic.

The alias also covers the `?region=eu` preview link, which bypasses
`toLogoListRegion` and would otherwise keep showing the old hardcoded bar.

Adds a @cc contract on `useLogoBar` pinning the precedence, including the
guarantee that a bar with a `fallbackSlug` never resolves to an empty array —
which is what keeps a Contentful outage from rendering a gap.

* [frames] Purge superseded Frame publications past a 7-day retention window

A Frame keeps every publication it has ever had: 992 of the 1150 publications in
US prod are superseded, holding 13,677 function rows plus a GCS directory each
(publication.json, the UI bundle, one bundle per function). Nothing but a full
Frame deletion has ever collected them.

Extends the frames retention workflow with a second sweep: for every Frame, drop
the publications that are not the active one, were published more than 7 days ago
and have no invocation left. Publications are enumerated from storage rather than
from sandbox_functions, since one that declares no function leaves no row behind
to find it by.

Publications are listed from GCS, so a publication whose descriptor cannot be read
is reported and left alone rather than deleted on a guess.

* Keep the publication sweep's batch cap out of @app imports too

Same dev-bundling constraint as #32607: workflow code is bundled without the
tsconfig path plugin in development, so it cannot import config.ts.

* Simplify the Frame publication sweep

Tally per-publication outcomes instead of summing five-field partial results,
drop the kept count nothing accumulated, and fail fast on a non-Frame file or
a missing workspace rather than reporting an empty sweep. Check the indexed
invocation count, now one joined query, before reading the descriptor from
GCS, and build one admin authenticator per workspace rather than per frame.
Unsafe publication directory names are logged and counted as unreadable
instead of passing as kept. The test fixtures move into FrameFunctionFactory,
shared by both suites.

FrameFunctionFactory is imported by ~14 suites, so its top-level import of
storeFramePublication put @app/lib/api/viz/authorized_file_access in every one
of their module graphs. front-api's file share suite mocks that module with a

  Caused by: ReferenceError: Cannot access '__vi_import_9__' before initialization

Add a ZIP extraction lib mirroring folder download (#32615)

* [front] Add a ZIP extraction lib mirroring folder download

`planFolderArchive` turns a folder into an archive rooted at that folder. This adds the inverse:
`extractArchiveToFolder` writes an archive's entries verbatim under a destination folder, so
downloading a folder and re-uploading the archive where it came from recreates it.

The extractor validates the whole archive before writing anything, so an archive rejected for a
traversing entry path or for busting a limit leaves the destination untouched. Entry types the
upload API rejects are written as-is rather than dropped: the pod file system already holds
arbitrary agent-written files.

No caller yet; the API endpoint and the file explorer entry point follow.

* Decide ZIP entry containment on the resolved path

Review found a bypass: `DustFileSystem.normalizeScopedPath` strips control characters before
normalizing, so an entry named `.<U+0001>./escaped.txt` reads as an ordinary relative name when the
raw name is checked, and as `../escaped.txt` by the time it reaches storage. Extracting into
`pod-p1/inbox` wrote to `pod-p1/escaped.txt`. It stayed inside the pod mount, so workspace isolation
held, but it escaped the destination folder.

Containment is now decided on the entry path resolved through the same normalization storage
applies, which is the thing that actually determines where bytes land.

Two related gaps in the same pass: junk entries were skipped before their path was validated, so an
archive holding `/etc/.DS_Store` extracted instead of being rejected; and skipped entries counted
toward neither limit, so `__MACOSX/` padding bought an archive a free pass. Every entry is now
validated and counted, junk included.

Also corrects the round-trip contract, which claimed extracting into the folder an archive came from
recreates it. Archiving `reports/` yields `reports/...` entries, so the destination is that folder's
parent; extracting into the folder itself nests one level deeper.

* Take DustFileSystem directly in the extractor

Review asked for one file system type rather than a per-module structural subtype, so
`FolderExtractFileSystem` is gone and the extractor takes `DustFileSystem`.

The `Pick<>` existed to let tests pass a fake; they now build a real `DustFileSystem` over a pod
space with the storage mock, the way `dust_file_system.test.ts` does. That is the more faithful
test anyway: entry paths go through real mount resolution and normalization, which is exactly where
containment is decided, and assertions moved from a stand-in's map to the GCS paths actually
written.

Also drops `isFolderExtractError`, flagged in review as test-only. It was in fact used by the
endpoint, but `instanceof FolderExtractError` reads as well at both call sites and leaves nothing
exported for tests alone.

* Size extraction limits for a buffered, single-request extract

Reviewer flagged that buffering the archive on front-api costs pod memory. Rather than add a lazy
zip reader, the limits now match what buffering can actually afford: 1,000 entries and 40 MB
uncompressed, down from 5,000 and 100 MB.

The entry count matters as much as the size here — entries are written to storage one at a time
inside a single request, so a few thousand of them would outlast any sensible request timeout well
before memory became the binding constraint.

The uncompressed cap is now explicitly a zip-bomb guard rather than a size policy: generous against
the compressed cap so ordinary archives pass, tight enough that an archive expanding by orders of
magnitude does not.

* Restore isFolderExtractError as a type guard

Reverts the removal from the earlier review pass. `prefer-type-guards` in front/CONTRACTS requires
explicit type guards over bare `instanceof` at call sites, which is also why `isFolderArchiveError`
and `isDustFileSystemError` exist.

The guard was flagged in review as test-only; it is not — the extract endpoint uses it to separate
extraction failures from storage errors when mapping to HTTP status codes.

[front] Fix attached folders being unreachable by the agent (#32613)

Refs https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/10457

Attaching a whole Folder/Website to a conversation made the agent unable to
read it: it reported the attachment reference as invalid and found nothing
elsewhere.

A data source root has no node id. `DATA_SOURCE_NODE_ID` ("datasource_node_id")
is a placeholder core stamps on the data source projection so it fits the
`CoreContentNode` shape when the data sources and nodes ES indices are merged
(`CoreContentNode::from_es_data_source_document`). It is constant across every
data source, matches no document in the nodes index, and appears in no node's
`parents`. Model-facing tools address such roots in the `renderNode` dialect
(`datasource_node_id-<dataSourceId>`) and intercept it before core.

The attachment pipeline leaked the raw placeholder into the prompt, bypassing
that translation, and built core filters on it:

- `renderAttachmentXml` emitted `nodeId="datasource_node_id"`, which the model
  passed to the filesystem tools, yielding "Could not find node:
  datasource_node_id". It is now omitted for data source roots.
- `conversation_files__semantic_search`, `buildProjectRetrieveDataSources` and
  `listProjectContextAttachments` filtered or looked up on the placeholder and
  silently matched nothing. They now address the data source itself.

`jit/folder.ts` already had the special case, it was never mirrored elsewhere.
The derivation is extracted into `contentNodeAttachmentParentsFilter` and
`contentNodeAttachmentsDataSourceConfigurations` so every call site shares one
enforcement point, the latter also collapsing one configuration per data source
view instead of per attachment.

Adds four code contracts covering the placeholder's non-addressability, both
helpers' guarantees, and the rule that a rendered `nodeId` must be resolvable by
the model-facing tools.

Expand an uploaded ZIP into a folder (#32616)

* [front-api] Expand an uploaded ZIP into a folder

Adds `POST /api/w/:wId/files/path/{...canonicalPath}?action=extract`, the inverse of the
`?archive=zip` download the same route already serves: the path names the destination folder and
the body is the archive.

It lives on the unified file-system route rather than under `/spaces/:spaceId/files` because that
router's POST `/:rel{.+}` is the move operation, where a literal `/extract` segment would shadow
moving a file of that name. Being mount-generic, this also covers conversation folders.

Writes go through the file system abstraction, whose mount resolution rejects traversal, and the
destination is synced afterwards like any other path mutation. No FileResource is created: entries
land the way an agent-written pod file does, which is what a plain extract should do.

* Cap the uploaded archive at 4 MB

The request body cap is what actually bounds peak memory per extract: `adm-zip` reads the whole
archive into memory even when constructed from a path, so streaming the upload to disk first would
not have helped. Taking the simple route instead of adding a lazy zip reader, the cap drops from
50 MB to 4 MB.

* Narrow extract errors with the restored type guard

Pairs with the guard's restoration in the lib: the handler goes back to `isFolderExtractError`,
per `prefer-type-guards` in front/CONTRACTS.

hardcoded ["platform_actions", "personal_actions"] once well-known discovery

When a model is flagged degraded and a message fails on it, the error now
offers to switch model and retries on whatever the input bar's picker is
showing. Retrying needs the client to name the model: the retry endpoint
reuses the failed message's resolution when no selection is sent, and the
picker sends none when the pick is the agent's own default. The picker
therefore publishes its shown model with that default spelled out, and the
private retry route accepts an optional model selection.

The switcher is offered exactly when a plain retry would re-run the model
that just failed, so a tier-resolved failure only gets a plain retry.

Clicking a sub-menu command with the mouse closed the whole slash menu instead of entering the

menu. The suggestion factory now notifies extensions on exit and both slash extensions clear the
stack there.

refactor(skills): make computeRequestedSpaceIds the single source of truth (#32851)

Four call sites assembled a skill's `requestedSpaceIds` inline, each unioning the
same four inputs: the spaces of its tools and attached knowledge, the spaces its
nested skills request, the hand-picked ones, and the global space. The create route,
the PATCH route, the space-deletion cleanup and the backfill migration each kept
their own copy of that union.

`SkillResource.computeRequestedSpaceIds` now takes all four and returns the complete
set, with a contract saying so. Its previous body (tools and knowledge only) becomes
`computeToolAndKnowledgeSpaceIds`, and `getReferencedSkillSpaceModelIds` moves out of
`space_requirements` to `SkillResource.listReferencedSkillSpaceIds` beside it. The
PATCH route's inline editor-lockout check becomes
`findSkillEditorsWithoutAccessToSpaceIds`, so a caller holding space ids rather than
resolved spaces cannot forget to validate the caller as an editor.

Two observable differences, both intended: the create route now appends the global
space last rather than second, and the space-deletion cleanup drops its "deleted
space still present after filtering" error log, since it now strips that space from
the rebuilt list unconditionally.

[connectors] Resolve Slack workflow names when bots.info fails (#32697)

Refs https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/10448

Slack Workflow Builder posts arrive as `bot_message` events whose `bot_id`
Slack refuses to resolve through `bots.info` (`bot_not_found`, with or
without `team_id`) and which carry no `bot_profile`. The bot path treated
that as a bot we cannot see and returned `Ok` without posting anything,
so workflows mentioning @Dust failed silently.

The workflow's display name is on the message itself, in `username`.
Read it from the webhook event first, and when the event lacks it fetch
the message by its `ts` through `conversations.replies`. The name then
goes through the existing summoning whitelist and space checks.

Trim the resolved name before the group lookup: the whitelist check
already trimmed, so a trailing space passed the first and failed the
second.

When no name can be resolved, post an error in the thread instead of
staying silent, and point admins to the Automations page.

feat(skills): recompute attachments and spaces when applying a suggestion (#32852)

* feat(skills): recompute attachments and spaces when applying a suggestion

Applying an instruction suggestion rewrote the text but carried the skill's tools,
knowledge and requested spaces over untouched, so a suggestion that added a <tool> or
<knowledge> tag produced instructions naming something the skill did not hold.

The rewritten instructions are now the source: `resolveInstructionAttachments` reads
the tags back out of them, and `computeRequestedSpaceIds` derives the spaces from
that. A tag that names a deleted resource, or one the caller cannot read, fails the

Frames v2: rename endpoint (#32799)

* Let the Frames v2 move accept a prepared filesystem

* Follow a renamed Frame across Pod tabs and the pin

* Add the Frames v2 rename endpoint

* Repoint Pod Frame references inside the move

Renaming a Frame is a move, and a Pod addresses its pinned Frame and its tabs by
manifest path. Repointing them belonged next to the updateMount that changes the
path, under the Frame's locks, rather than a layer up in the rename: it now holds
for every move, mirroring how deleteFrameV2 already calls removeFramePath from
inside the resource.

The seeded-tab-title probe now uses the same rule the seeding sites use, so a
Frame folder whose name contains a dot no longer freezes its tab title.

The move also hands back the Frame it updated, so the route no longer re-reads it
and no longer needs a fallback that would have served the pre-rename path.

* Take a prepared filesystem in moveFrameV2Source

The earlier commit kept a conversation-scoped wrapper under the original name so
the function's existing signature and its two test files carried on unchanged.
That signature has had no production caller since it landed in #31532, so the
wrapper existed only to build a filesystem for tests.

moveFrameV2Source now takes the filesystem directly, the way moveCanonicalFile
and renameCanonicalFile already do, and the tests build one through a shared
helper. This also drops the duplicate path resolution the wrapper needed to
work out which mounts to open.

* Rename a Frame through the file endpoint, not a Frame endpoint

A Frames v2 package is a folder, and the file system already renames folders.
The dedicated PATCH /api/w/:wId/frames/:frameId went away in favour of teaching
renameCanonicalFile that a folder can be a Frame package root and delegating to
the Frame move when it is.

This also closes a hole rather than routing around it. The package's FileResource
is the manifest inside the folder, not the folder itself, so fetchLinkedFileResource
found nothing and a folder rename through the generic endpoint moved the bytes
while stranding the registration. A second, safe endpoint would have left that
door open; going through this one shuts it.

feat(conversations): show real upload progress on file attachments (#32170)

* feat(conversations): show real upload progress on file attachments

* fix(egress): always settle the clientUpload promise

`new Response()` throws on a status outside [200, 599] and on a `statusText` the
platform refuses, both of them server-controlled. `xhr.onload` is dispatched by the
event loop rather than from inside the promise executor, so such a throw escaped the
promise instead of rejecting it and left it pending for good: the attachment card
would spin forever and no error would ever surface.

Guard the whole handler and reject with a normalized error. Add
`upload-promise-always-settles` for the obligation that was violated, and reconcile
`upload-rejects-like-fetch`, which promised to resolve with whatever status the
server returned.

Also add `default-init-carries-no-content-type` on `setDefaultInitResolver`, the
invariant `clientUpload` relies on to let the browser derive the multipart boundary,
and note at the construction site that the synthesized `Response` carries no headers.

The test harness dispatched `send()` synchronously inside the executor, so a throwing
handler would have rejected the promise and hidden the failure mode; it now dispatches
asynchronously the way the browser does, which makes the new regression test fail
without the guard.

[front] Preserve bytea columns during relocation and repair malformed DSEC nonces (#33040)

Relocation stages front table rows as JSON in GCS. A Buffer such as the
workspace_sandbox_env_vars placeholder_nonce column (bytea) comes back from
JSON.parse as a plain `{ type: "Buffer", data }` object, which pg binds as
JSON text, so the destination stored ~80 bytes of JSON instead of the 16-byte
nonce. The rendered `__DSEC_<160hex>__` placeholder is then rejected by dsbx
and HTTPS secrets stop working for every relocated workspace that has one.

Revive serialized Buffers when reading relocation storage, and add a backfill
that regenerates any https_secret nonce whose stored length is not 16 bytes
(optionally scoped with --wId). The nonce is not key material and is only
rendered at sandbox start, so a fresh random value restores the secret;
running sandboxes in affected workspaces need a restart.

fix(files): reject audio uploads when voice transcription is unavailable (#32571)

* fix(files): reject audio uploads when voice transcription is unavailable

Audio content types always report a processed version, but transcription is
skipped for BYOK plans and for workspaces with allowVoiceTranscription
disabled. The processing function returned Ok without writing a transcript, so
the file was marked ready while its processed object never existed. Any later
read that resolves to the processed version - in particular the mount copy done
when the file is attached to a conversation - then failed on a missing object
and surfaced as a 500 during upload or content_fragment attachment.

Refuse the audio instead of storing it:

- isAudioTranscriptionAvailable centralizes the BYOK and workspace-policy
  checks, alongside the message shown to users.
- Both file-creation endpoints return 400 file_type_not_supported before the
  client sends any bytes.
- processAndStoreFile guards before writing the original and marks the file
  failed, covering every upload path.
- The audio processing function now returns Err rather than a silent Ok, so a
  processing function can no longer leave a file ready without its processed
  version.
- maybeUpsertFileAttachment refuses audio before stamping use-case metadata,
  which is what resolved the mount path and raised the 500.
- The file uploader hook rejects audio at selection time for the picker,
  drag-and-drop and paste, and drops audio extensions from the picker filter.

Pre-existing audio files uploaded while transcription was unavailable are not
repaired; attaching one now returns the explicit 400 instead of a 500.

feat(llm): retry flex-processing failures on the standard service tier (#33102)

Trigger and wake-up runs go out on OpenAI flex processing, which is best-effort
capacity the provider can refuse outright. The client already replays on standard
when flex fails before the first event, but a failure after that surfaced straight
to the user whenever the error type was not retryable — even though the run had
never been tried on the model's normal capacity.

Errors on a flex request are now always forwarded as retryable, and
withFlexProcessing drops flex once the run is a retry, so the retry Temporal
schedules is the run's standard-tier attempt. The retry budget is unchanged.

[dsbx] Let sandbox tool calls pick one instance of a server (#33144)

* [dsbx] Let sandbox tool calls pick one instance of a server

Adding a server twice from a space (e.g. Gmail) creates two server
instances that both report `server.name` "gmail", told apart only by their
view names (`gmail1`, `gmail2`). Sandbox tool calls matched on the server
name alone and dsbx took the first view, so a Frame function could never
reach the second instance.

`?server=` on the sandbox tools listing now resolves the reference against
the view id, then the view name, then the server name, returning every view
of the first rule that matches. dsbx fails on more than one match instead
of picking one, and `dsbx tools` lists one line per view (with its id when
two share a name). The Frames v2 skill and `tools.call` docs follow.

Bumps dsbx to 0.1.65 and dust-base to 0.8.120.

* fix(front): refresh Frame panel content on open_frame

The side panel keys viz refresh on fileId@updatedAt, but open_frame used
File.updatedAtMs which often does not move when the agent updates a Frame
(sandbox edits / publish metadata). The viz iframe also ignored that hash
in its React key, so even a new revision left stale RPC-fetched code mounted.

activePublicationId when present, and FrameRenderer remounts the iframe
(and waits for content) when contentHash changes.

and recompiled aggressively. Remount via React key alone; keep
identifier as viz-<fileId>.
